title.zh: 卷三十八 列傳第二十六: 裴駿 裴延雋 裴佗 裴果 裴寬 裴俠 裴文舉 裴仁基
title.en: Volume 38 Biographies 26: Pei Jun, Pei Yanjun, Pei Tuo, Pei Guo, Peikuan, Pei Xia, Pei Wenju, Pei Renji
title.raw: 卷三十八 列傳第二十六: 裴駿 裴延雋 裴佗 裴果 裴寬 裴俠 裴文舉 裴仁基 Volume 38 Biographies 26: Pei Jun, Pei Yanjun, Pei Tuo, Pei Guo, Peikuan, Pei Xia, Pei Wenju, Pei Renji

sentences.zh: 裴駿 裴延雋 裴佗 裴果 裴寬 裴俠 裴文舉 裴仁基

translations.literal: Pei Jun; Pei Yanjun; Pei Tuo; Pei Guo; Pei Kuan; Pei Xia; Pei Wenju; Pei Renji
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun, Pei Yanjun, Pei Tuo, Pei Guo, Pei Kuan, Pei Xia, Pei Wenju, and Pei Renji

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十六

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-Six
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 26

sentences.zh: 裴駿從孫敬憲莊伯從弟安祖裴延俊裴佗子讓之孫矩皇甫和裴果裴寬裴俠子祥肅裴文舉裴仁基

translations.literal: Pei Jun's collateral grandson Jingxian, Zhuangbo, collateral younger cousin Anzu, Pei Yanjun, Pei Tuo's son Rangzhi, grandson Ju, Huangfu He, Pei Guo, Pei Kuan, Pei Xia's sons Xiang and Su, Pei Wenju, Pei Renji
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun's collateral grandsons Jingxian and Zhuangbo, his collateral younger cousin Anzu, Pei Yanjun, Pei Tuo's son Rangzhi, his grandson Ju, Huangfu He, Pei Guo, Pei Kuan, Pei Xia's sons Xiang and Su, Pei Wenju, and Pei Renji

sentences.zh: 裴駿，字神駒，小名皮，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Jun, styled Shenju, childhood name Pi, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun, styled Shenju, whose childhood name was Pi, was from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父雙碩，位恆農太守、安邑子，贈東雍州刺史、聞喜侯。

translations.literal: His father Shuangshuo held the post of Administrator of Hengnong and Baron of Anyi; posthumously he was made Inspector of East Yongzhou and Marquis of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuangshuo served as Administrator of Hengnong and Baron of Anyi and was posthumously appointed Inspector of East Yongzhou and Marquis of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 駿幼而聰慧。

translations.literal: Jun was clever from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was exceptionally clever from childhood.

sentences.zh: 親表稱為神駒，因以為字。

translations.literal: Relatives called him Divine Colt, and he took this as his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives called him the Divine Colt, and he adopted that as his style name.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，通涉經史，方檢有禮度，鄉里宗敬焉。

translations.literal: At coming of age he had mastered the classics and histories; proper and measured in conduct, the village revered him.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he came of age he had mastered the classics and histories, conducted himself with propriety and restraint, and was revered throughout his district.

sentences.zh: 蓋吳作亂於關中，汾陰人薛永宗聚眾應之，來襲聞喜。

translations.literal: Gai Wu rebelled in Guanzhong; Xue Yongzong of Fenyin gathered a host to join him and came to attack Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai Wu rebelled in Guanzhong, Xue Yongzong of Fenyin raised troops in support and marched against Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 縣令憂惶，計無所出。

translations.literal: The county magistrate was anxious and had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate was in a panic and could think of nothing to do.

sentences.zh: 駿在家聞之，便率曆鄉豪奔赴之。

translations.literal: Jun at home heard of it and at once led the local notables of Li to rush to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, still at home, heard the news and immediately led the local notables of Li to the county's aid.

sentences.zh: 賊退，刺史以狀聞。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the inspector reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels withdrew, the provincial inspector reported what had happened.

sentences.zh: 會太武親討蓋吳，引見駿。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Taiwu personally campaigned against Gai Wu and summoned Jun for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Emperor Taiwu was personally campaigning against Gai Wu and summoned Jun to an audience.

sentences.zh: 駿陳敘事宜，帝大悅，謂崔浩曰：「裴駿有當世才，其忠義可嘉。

translations.literal: Jun presented the affairs; the emperor was greatly pleased and said to Cui Hao: "Pei Jun has talent for the age; his loyalty and righteousness are admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Jun laid out the situation; the emperor was greatly pleased and said to Cui Hao, "Pei Jun has the talent the age requires, and his loyalty and righteousness are admirable.

sentences.zh: 」補中書博士。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 浩亦深器駿，目為三河領袖。

translations.literal: Hao also deeply valued Jun and regarded him as leader of the Three Rivers region.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also held Jun in high regard and looked on him as the leading figure of the Three Rivers region.

sentences.zh: 轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice-Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice-Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宋使明僧皓來聘，以駿有才學，假給事中、散騎常侍，于境上勞接。

translations.literal: When the Song envoy Ming Senghao came on embassy, because Jun had talent and learning he was given provisional titles as Attendant and Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds to receive him at the border.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song envoy Ming Senghao came on an embassy, Jun's learning and ability earned him provisional appointment as Attendant and Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds to receive the envoy at the border.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈秦州刺史、聞喜侯，諡曰康。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Inspector of Qinzhou and Marquis of Wenxi, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Qinzhou and Marquis of Wenxi, with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 子修，字元寄。

translations.literal: His son Xiu, styled Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiu, styled Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 清辯好學，歷位秘書中散、主客令。

translations.literal: Clear in debate and fond of learning; he held posts as Palace Library Attendant and Director of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-spoken, fond of learning, he served as Palace Library Attendant and Director of Guests.

sentences.zh: 累遷中大夫，兼祠部曹事，職主禮樂，每有疑議，修斟酌故實，咸有條貫。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Master of the Palace and concurrently handled affairs of the Sacrificial Rites Bureau; charged with ritual and music, whenever there was doubt he weighed ancient precedents, and all had clear order.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Grand Master of the Palace and concurrently handled the Sacrificial Rites Bureau. Charged with ritual and music, whenever a question arose he weighed ancient precedents, and his rulings were always systematic.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰恭伯，宣武時追贈東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death his posthumous title was Gongbo; under Emperor Xuanwu he was posthumously made Inspector of East Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he received the posthumous title Gongbo, and under Emperor Xuanwu was posthumously appointed Inspector of East Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 修早孤，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xiu was orphaned early; in mourning he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu lost his father early and became known for the filial devotion he showed in mourning.

sentences.zh: 二弟三妹，並在幼弱，撫養訓誨，甚有義方。

translations.literal: Two younger brothers and three younger sisters were all still young; he reared and instructed them with great moral propriety.
translations.idiomatic: With two younger brothers and three younger sisters all still small, he reared and instructed them with exemplary moral discipline.

sentences.zh: 次弟務早喪，修哀傷之，感于行路。

translations.literal: His next younger brother Wu died early; Xiu mourned him, moving passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: His next younger brother Wu died young, and Xiu's grief for him moved everyone who passed by on the road.

sentences.zh: 愛育孤侄，同于己子，及將異居，奴婢田宅悉推與之，時人以此稱焉。

translations.literal: He cherished and reared an orphaned nephew as his own son; when they were about to live separately he yielded all slaves, fields, and houses to him, and people of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He raised an orphaned nephew as he would his own son, and when they were about to set up separate households he gave the nephew all the slaves, fields, and houses. People of the day praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子詢，字敬叔。

translations.literal: His son Xun, styled Jingshu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun, styled Jingshu.

sentences.zh: 美儀貌，多藝能，音律博弈，咸所閑解。

translations.literal: Handsome in appearance, with many talents; music, weiqi, and all were within his easy mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing and skilled in many arts, he was equally at home with music, weiqi, and the like.

sentences.zh: 位平昌太守。

translations.literal: He held the post of Administrator of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 時太原長公主寡居，與詢私奸，明帝仍詔詢尚焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Princess of Taiyuan lived in widowhood; she and Xun had a secret liaison, yet Emperor Ming still ordered Xun to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Taiyuan was then living in widowhood; she and Xun had been carrying on an affair in secret, yet Emperor Ming nevertheless ordered Xun to marry her.

sentences.zh: 尋以主婿，特除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon, as the princess's husband, he was specially appointed Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as the princess's husband, he was specially appointed Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds.

sentences.zh: 時本邑中正闕，司徒召詢為之。

translations.literal: At the time the local Rectifier of his native district was vacant; the Minister of Education summoned Xun to the post.
translations.idiomatic: The Rectifier of his native district had fallen vacant, and the Minister of Education summoned Xun to fill the post.

sentences.zh: 詢族叔昞，自陳情願此官，詢遂讓焉。

translations.literal: Xun's clansman-uncle Bing stated his wish for this office, and Xun yielded it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's clansman-uncle Bing asked for the post himself, and Xun yielded it to him.

sentences.zh: 時論善之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋監起居事，遷秘書監，出為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised the Daily Records, was transferred to Director of the Palace Library, and went out as Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon supervised the Daily Records, was promoted to Director of the Palace Library, and then sent out as Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詢以凡司戍主蠻酋田樸特，地居要險，眾逾數萬，足為邊捍，遂表朴特為西郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Xun, because the garrison chief of Fansi, the Man chieftain Tian Putie, held terrain of strategic danger with followers exceeding tens of thousands and sufficient to guard the border, memorialized to make Putie Inspector of West Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xun noted that Tian Putie, the Man chieftain who served as garrison chief of Fansi, held strategically vital ground with more than ten thousand followers and could serve as a border bulwark, and memorialized to appoint Putie Inspector of West Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝議許之。

translations.literal: Court deliberation approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 梁將李國興寇邊，樸特與部曲為表裏聲援，郢州獲全，樸特頗有力焉。

translations.literal: When the Liang general Li Guoxing raided the border, Putie and his followers gave support from within and without; Yingzhou was preserved, and Putie contributed considerable force.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang general Li Guoxing raided the frontier, Putie and his followers supported Yingzhou from within and without, the province was preserved, and Putie contributed substantially to the defense.

sentences.zh: 徵為七兵尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 武泰中，以本官兼侍中為關中大使。

translations.literal: In the Wutai era, with his present office he was concurrently made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Ambassador to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wutai era he was concurrently appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Ambassador to Guanzhong while retaining his present office.

sentences.zh: 未及發，于河陰遇害。

translations.literal: Before he could set out, he met harm at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公，諡曰貞烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Duke of Works, with posthumous title Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Duke of Works with the posthumous title Zhenlie.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 修弟宣，字叔令。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Xuan, styled Shuling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's younger brother Xuan, styled Shuling.

sentences.zh: 通辯博物，早有聲譽。

translations.literal: Fluent in debate and broad in learning, he had early reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in debate and widely learned, he had won an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母兄以孝友稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served mother and elder brother and was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was known for the filial devotion and brotherly affection he showed his mother and elder brother.

sentences.zh: 司空李沖有人倫鑒，見而重之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Li Chong had discernment in human relations; seeing him, he valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Chong was a keen judge of character and, on meeting Xuan, held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，徵為尚書主客郎，累遷太尉長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was summoned as Director of Guests in the Secretariat and rose in succession to Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was summoned as Director of Guests in the Secretariat and rose through successive posts to Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 宣上言：自遷都以來，凡戰陣之處及軍罷兵還之道，所有骸骼無人覆藏者，請悉令州郡戍邏檢行埋掩。

translations.literal: Xuan submitted: Since the move of the capital, at every place of battle and on every road where armies withdrew and troops returned, wherever bones lie uncovered with no one to bury them, request that all be ordered to the provinces and commanderies for the border garrisons to patrol, inspect, and bury.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan submitted a memorial: "Since the move of the capital, wherever battles have been fought and wherever armies have marched home, all unburied remains along those routes should be ordered buried through patrols by the border garrisons of every province and commandery."

sentences.zh: 並符出兵之鄉，其家有死於戎役者，皆使招魂復魄，祔祭先靈，復其年租調。

translations.literal: Also issue orders to the districts that sent troops: wherever a family had one die in military service, have them summon the soul and restore the spirit, offer collateral sacrifice to the ancestral spirits, and restore their annual tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: "In every district that had sent men to war, wherever a family had lost someone on campaign, they should be required to perform rites to recall the soul and restore the spirit, offer collateral sacrifice to the ancestral spirits, and have their annual tax and corvée obligations restored."

sentences.zh: 身被傷痍者，免其兵役。

translations.literal: Those whose bodies bore wounds were to be exempted from military service.
translations.idiomatic: "Those who had been wounded in body were to be exempted from military service."

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 出為益州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 宣至州綏撫，甚得戎羌之心。

translations.literal: When Xuan reached the province he pacified and comforted, winning the hearts of the Rong and Qiang deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office Xuan governed with conciliation and won the deep loyalty of the Rong and Qiang peoples.

sentences.zh: 後晉壽更置益州，改宣所蒞為南秦州。

translations.literal: Later Jingshou was re-established as Yizhou, and the province Xuan had governed was changed to South Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Jingshou was re-established as Yizhou, the territory Xuan had governed was redesignated South Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣家世以儒學為業，常慕廉退，每歎曰：「以賈誼之才，漢文之世，而不曆公卿，將非運也？

translations.literal: The Xuan family for generations took Confucian learning as their profession; he often admired integrity and withdrawal, sighing each time: "With Jia Yi's talent, in Emperor Han Wen's age, yet not rising through the ranks of ministers and dukes—is it not fate?
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan family had pursued Confucian learning for generations, and he often admired the ideal of integrity and withdrawal. He would sigh and say, "With Jia Yi's talent, in the age of Emperor Wen of Han, yet never rising to ministerial rank—was that not simply fate?

sentences.zh: 」乃謂親賓曰：「吾本無當世之志，直隨牒至此，祿厚養親，效不光國，可以言歸矣。

translations.literal: " Then he said to kin and guests: "I originally had no ambition for the age; I simply followed my appointment to this point. Salary is thick enough to support my parents; my service has not glorified the state—it is time to speak of returning.
translations.idiomatic: " He then told relatives and guests, "I never had ambitions for public life; I simply followed one appointment after another to reach this point. My salary is ample enough to support my parents, yet I have done nothing to bring glory to the state. It is time to speak of going home.

sentences.zh: 」因奉表求解。

translations.literal: " Accordingly he submitted a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: " He accordingly submitted a memorial requesting release from office.

sentences.zh: 宣武不許，乃作《懷田賦》以敘心焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu did not permit it, so he composed "Rhapsody on Longing for the Fields" to express his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu refused, so he wrote "Rhapsody on Longing for the Fields" to express what he felt.

sentences.zh: 宣素明陰陽之書，自始患便克亡日，果如其言。

translations.literal: Xuan was from of old versed in books of yin and yang; from the first illness he fixed the day of death, and it was indeed as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had long been versed in the yin-yang texts, and from the onset of his illness he fixed the day of his death, which came to pass exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 贈豫州刺史，諡曰定，尋改為穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Inspector of Yuzhou, posthumous title Ding, soon changed to Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Inspector of Yuzhou with the posthumous title Ding, soon changed to Mu.

sentences.zh: 子敬憲嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jingxian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 敬憲字孝虞，少有志行，學博才清，撫訓諸弟，專以讀誦為業。

translations.literal: Jingxian, styled Xiaoyu, had ambition and conduct from youth; learning broad and talent clear; he reared and instructed his younger brothers, taking reading and recitation alone as his profession.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian, styled Xiaoyu, showed moral purpose from youth. Broad in learning and clear in talent, he reared and instructed his younger brothers and devoted himself entirely to reading and recitation.

sentences.zh: 淡于榮利，風氣俊遠。

translations.literal: Indifferent to glory and profit, his bearing lofty and remote.
translations.idiomatic: Indifferent to fame and gain, he carried himself with a lofty, distant air.

sentences.zh: 郡征功曹不就，諸府辟命，先進其弟，世人歡美之。

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as Merit Officer but he did not accept; when various offices issued appointments he advanced his younger brothers first, and people praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery summoned him as Merit Officer he declined; whenever offices issued appointments he put his younger brothers forward first, and people praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 司州牧、高陽王雍舉秀才，射策高第，除太學博士。

translations.literal: The Governor of Sizhou, Prince Yong of Gaoyang, recommended him as Presented Scholar; in the archery examination he took high rank and was appointed Academician of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang, Governor of Sizhou, recommended him as Presented Scholar; he placed at the top of the archery examination and was appointed Academician of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 性和雅，未嘗失色於人。

translations.literal: His nature was harmonious and refined; he never showed a change of countenance toward others.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was gentle and refined, and he never once lost his composure in dealing with others.

sentences.zh: 工隸草，解音律，五言之作，獨擅于時，名聲甚重，後進咸共宗慕之。

translations.literal: Skilled in clerical and cursive script, understood music; in five-character compositions he alone excelled in the age—his fame very weighty, and younger men all together took him as object of veneration.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in clerical and cursive script and versed in music, he stood alone in his age for five-character verse. His reputation was immense, and younger writers all looked to him as their model.

sentences.zh: 中山將之部，朝賢送于河梁，賦詩言別，皆以敬憲為最。

translations.literal: When the general of Zhongshan went to his post, court worthies saw him off at the River Bridge; composing poems of farewell, all took Jingxian's as finest.
translations.idiomatic: When the general of Zhongshan departed for his post, court worthies saw him off at the River Bridge and composed farewell poems, all agreeing that Jingxian's were the finest.

sentences.zh: 其文不能贍逸，而有清麗之美。

translations.literal: His writings could not supply abundance and ease, yet had the beauty of clarity and refinement.
translations.idiomatic: His writing lacked breadth and ease, yet possessed a clear, refined beauty.

sentences.zh: 少有氣病，年三十三卒，人物甚悼之。

translations.literal: From youth he had a qi disorder; at thirty-three he died, and men greatly mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He had suffered from a qi disorder since youth and died at thirty-three, to the deep grief of all who knew him.

sentences.zh: 敬憲世有仁義於鄉里，孝昌中，蜀賊陳雙熾所過殘暴，至敬憲宅，輒相約束，不得焚燒，為物所伏如此。

translations.literal: The Jingxian family for generations had benevolence and righteousness in the village; in the Xiaochang era the Shu bandit Chen Shuangchi wherever he passed was brutal, yet at Jingxian's house they at once bound one another not to burn, so revered was he by things.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingxian family had been known for benevolence and righteousness in their district for generations. In the Xiaochang era the Shu bandit Chen Shuangchi ravaged everything in his path, yet at Jingxian's house his men bound one another not to set fires—such was the respect his moral standing commanded.

sentences.zh: 永興三年，贈中書侍郎，諡曰文。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxing he was posthumously made Vice-Director of the Secretariat, posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxing he was posthumously appointed Vice-Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 敬憲弟莊伯，字孝夏。

translations.literal: Jingxian's younger brother Zhuangbo, styled Xiaoxia.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian's younger brother Zhuangbo, styled Xiaoxia.

sentences.zh: 亦有文才，器度閒雅，喜慍不形於色；

translations.literal: He also had literary talent; bearing leisurely and refined, joy and anger did not show on his face;
translations.idiomatic: He too had literary talent, carried himself with easy refinement, and never let joy or anger show on his face;

sentences.zh: 博識多聞，善以約言辯物。

translations.literal: broad in knowledge and many in what he heard, skilled at judging things with concise words.
translations.idiomatic: he was widely learned and skilled at judging things in a few well-chosen words.

sentences.zh: 司空、任城王澄辟為行參軍，甚加知賞。

translations.literal: Minister of Works, Prince Cheng of Rencheng, recruited him as Traveling Aide and greatly appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng, Minister of Works, recruited him as Traveling Aide and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 年二十一，上《神龜頌》，時人異之。

translations.literal: At twenty-one he submitted "Ode to the Divine Tortoise," and people of the time marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-one he submitted his "Ode to the Divine Tortoise," which astonished his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 文筆與敬憲相亞。

translations.literal: His literary brush was next below Jingxian's.
translations.idiomatic: His literary gifts ranked just below Jingxian's.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧北討，引為記室參軍，委以章奏之事。

translations.literal: Prince Yu of Linhuai on the northern campaign took him as Recorder Aide and entrusted him with memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Linhuai marched north on campaign, he took Zhuangbo as Recorder Aide and entrusted him with all memorials and reports.

sentences.zh: 及聞敬憲寢疾，求假不許，遂逕自還，亦矜而不問。

translations.literal: When he heard Jingxian was gravely ill he requested leave but was not permitted; he then returned directly on his own, yet was treated with sympathy and not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Jingxian was gravely ill he asked for leave but was refused, so he returned home on his own. The prince treated him with sympathy and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 扶侍兄病，晝夜不離于側，形容憔悴。

translations.literal: Supporting and attending his brother's illness, day and night he did not leave his side; his appearance was haggard.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed his brother day and night without leaving his side until he was worn to emaciation.

sentences.zh: 因葬敬憲於鄉，遇病卒，年二十八。

translations.literal: Because he buried Jingxian in the village he fell ill and died, age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: After burying Jingxian in their home district he fell ill and died at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 兄弟才學知名，同年俱喪，世共嗟惜之。

translations.literal: The brothers were famed for talent and learning; in the same year both were lost, and the age together sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers had been famed for talent and learning, and their deaths in the same year moved the world to shared lament.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，贈通直散騎侍郎，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he was posthumously made Vice-Director of the Rapid Steeds for Direct Communication, posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an he was posthumously appointed Vice-Director of the Rapid Steeds for Direct Communication with the posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並無子，所著詞藻，莫為集錄。

translations.literal: The brothers both had no sons; the compositions they wrote were never gathered into a collection.
translations.idiomatic: Neither brother left a son, and the writings they produced were never collected.

sentences.zh: 莊伯弟獻伯，廷尉卿、濟州刺史，少以學尚風流，有名京洛。

translations.literal: Zhuangbo's younger brother Xianbo, Director of the Court of Justice and Inspector of Jizhou, from youth with learning esteemed the elegant and had fame in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangbo's younger brother Xianbo served as Director of the Court of Justice and Inspector of Jizhou. From youth he cultivated learning and elegance and was well known in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴酷，不得吏人之和，但以清白流譽。

translations.literal: In government he was severe and harsh, not winning the harmony of clerks and people, yet solely with integrity and purity he flowed in reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was severe and harsh and won him no goodwill among officials or commoners, yet he was known throughout for his integrity and probity.

sentences.zh: 卒于殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the post of Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 駿從弟安祖，少聰慧，年八九歲，就師講《詩》，至《鹿鳴篇》，語諸兄云：「鹿得食相呼，而況人乎。

translations.literal: Jun's collateral younger cousin Anzu was clever from youth; at eight or nine he went to a teacher to study the Odes, and at the "Deer Cry" section he told his elder brothers: "When deer get food they call to one another—how much more should men.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's collateral younger cousin Anzu was clever from childhood. At eight or nine he went to a teacher to study the Odes, and when they reached the "Deer Cry" he told his elder brothers, "When deer find food they call to one another—how much more should human beings do so?

sentences.zh: 」自此未曾獨食。

translations.literal: " From this time he never ate alone.
translations.idiomatic: " From that day on he never ate alone.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At coming of age the province recruited him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age the province recruited him as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 人有兄弟爭財，詣州相訟。

translations.literal: Some men had brothers disputing property and came to the province to sue one another.
translations.idiomatic: When brothers came to the province to sue one another over disputed property,

sentences.zh: 安祖召其兄弟，以禮義責讓之。

translations.literal: Anzu summoned the brothers and with ritual propriety and righteousness reproved them.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu summoned them and rebuked them in the name of ritual propriety and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 此人兄弟，明日相率謝罪。

translations.literal: These men's brothers the next day together led one another to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the brothers came together to apologize.

sentences.zh: 州內欽服之。

translations.literal: Within the province all admired and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the province admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 後有人勸其仕進，安祖曰：「高尚之事，非敢庶幾，但京師遼遠，實憚於棲屑耳。

translations.literal: Later someone urged him to advance in office; Anzu said: "Lofty matters I do not dare aspire to, but the capital is distant and far—I truly fear the bother of scrambling about.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone urged him to take office. Anzu said, "I do not presume to aspire to lofty public service, but the capital is far away and I truly dread the petty scramble of official life.

sentences.zh: 」於是閒居養志，不出城邑。

translations.literal: " Accordingly he lived in leisure cultivating his will, not going beyond the town.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore lived in retirement, cultivating his aims, and never left his home district.

sentences.zh: 曾天熱，舍於樹下。

translations.literal: Once when the day was hot he lodged under a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on a hot day, he rested under a tree.

sentences.zh: 有鷙鳥逐雉，雉急投之，遂觸樹而死。

translations.literal: There was a fierce bird chasing a pheasant; the pheasant in desperation flew toward him, and so struck a tree and died.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce bird was chasing a pheasant; in desperation the pheasant flew straight toward him and struck a tree, dying on the spot.

sentences.zh: 安祖湣之，乃取置陰地，徐徐護視，良久得蘇，喜而放之。

translations.literal: Anzu pitied it, then took it and placed it in a shaded place, slowly tending and watching it; after a long while it revived, and he rejoiced and released it.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu took pity on the bird, set it in a shady spot, and patiently nursed it until, after some time, it revived; overjoyed, he set it free.

sentences.zh: 後夜忽夢一丈夫，衣冠甚偉，著繡衣曲領，向安祖再拜。

translations.literal: Later that night he suddenly dreamed of a man, imposing in cap and robes, wearing embroidered garments with curved collars, who bowed twice to Anzu.
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed of a stately man in embroidered robes with curved collars, who bowed deeply to him.

sentences.zh: 安祖怪問之，此人云：「感君前日見放，故來謝德。

translations.literal: Anzu wondered and questioned him; the man said, "Moved by your grace in releasing me the other day, I have come to repay your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu asked in astonishment what this meant. The man replied, "I am grateful that you spared me the other day, and have come to thank you for your virtue.

sentences.zh: 」聞者異焉。

translations.literal: " Those who heard of it were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: " All who heard the story were amazed.

sentences.zh: 後孝文幸長安，至河東，存訪故老，安祖朝于蒲阪。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowen visited Chang'an, reached Hedong, inquired after the elders of old, and Anzu presented himself at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Xiaowen traveled to Chang'an and reached Hedong to visit the region's old worthies, Anzu came to pay his respects at Puban.

sentences.zh: 帝與語甚悅，仍拜安邑令，以老病固辭，詔給一時俸以供湯藥焉。

translations.literal: The emperor spoke with him and was greatly pleased, and immediately appointed him Magistrate of Anyi; citing old age and illness he firmly declined, and an edict granted him a stipend for the time being to supply medicines.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased with their conversation and appointed him Magistrate of Anyi, but Anzu firmly declined on account of age and illness. The throne then granted him a stipend to cover his medicines.

sentences.zh: 年八十三，卒於家。

translations.literal: Age eighty-three; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 裴延俊，字平子，河東聞喜人也，魏冀州刺史徽之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Pei Yanjun, styled Pingzi, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong, eighth-generation descendant of Pei Hui, Inspector of Jizhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanjun, styled Pingzi, was from Wenxi in Hedong and an eighth-generation descendant of Pei Hui, who had served as Inspector of Jizhou under Wei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖奣，諮議參軍、并州別駕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Weng served as Advisory Staff Officer and Vice Director of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Weng had served as Advisory Staff Officer and Vice Director of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖雙彪，河東太守，贈雍州刺史，諡曰順。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuangbiao was Administrator of Hedong; posthumously made Inspector of Yongzhou, posthumous title Shun.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuangbiao had been Administrator of Hedong and was posthumously appointed Inspector of Yongzhou with the posthumous title Shun.

sentences.zh: 父山松，州主簿，行平陽郡事，以平蜀賊丁蟲功，贈東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shansong was Chief Clerk of the province and acted as Administrator of Pingyang commandery; for merit in pacifying the Shu bandit Ding Chong he was posthumously made Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shansong had served as the province's Chief Clerk and acting Administrator of Pingyang commandery; for suppressing the Shu bandit Ding Chong he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 延俊少孤，事後母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Yanjun lost his father young and served his stepmother, becoming famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun lost his father in childhood and won renown for the filial devotion with which he served his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 涉獵墳史，頗有才筆。

translations.literal: He ranged through the classics and histories and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories and showed real talent as a writer.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，射策高第，除著作佐郎，累遷太子洗馬，又領本邑中正。

translations.literal: Recommended as Outstanding Scholar, he ranked high in the written examination, was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Composition Office, was repeatedly promoted to Groom of the Crown Prince's Household, and also headed the Rectifier of his native district.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Outstanding Scholar, he placed at the top of the palace examination and was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Composition Office. He rose to Groom of the Crown Prince's Household and also served as Rectifier of his native district.

sentences.zh: 及太子恂廢，以宮官例免。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Xun was deposed, by the precedent for palace officials he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Xun was deposed, Yanjun was dismissed under the rule that applied to palace officials.

sentences.zh: 宣武即位，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Yanjun became Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu came to the throne, Yanjun was appointed Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時帝專心釋典，不事墳籍，延俊上疏致諫。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor devoted himself to Buddhist sutras and did not attend to the classical texts; Yanjun submitted a memorial offering earnest remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then wholly absorbed in Buddhist sutras and neglected the classical canon, so Yanjun submitted a memorial urging him to change course.

sentences.zh: 後除司州別駕。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Vice Director of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Vice Director of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 及詔立明堂，群官博議，延俊獨著一堂之論。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered the establishment of the Bright Hall, officials broadly debated it, and Yanjun alone set forth a theory of a single hall.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for building the Bright Hall and officials debated the design at length, Yanjun alone argued for a single-hall plan.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌時典眾議，讀而笑曰：「子故欲遠符僕射也。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi then presided over the general deliberations; reading it he laughed and said, "You surely wish to match the Vice Director from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi, who was overseeing the deliberations, read Yanjun's essay and laughed. "You mean to agree with the Vice Director from a distance, don't you?

sentences.zh: 」明帝時，累遷幽州刺史。

translations.literal: " In Emperor Ming's time he was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Emperor Ming he rose to Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 范陽郡有舊督亢渠，徑五十里；

translations.literal: Fanyang commandery had an old Dukang Canal, fifty li in width;
translations.idiomatic: In Fanyang commandery there was an old Dukang Canal fifty li across;

sentences.zh: 漁陽、燕郡有故戾陵諸堨，廣袤三十里，皆廢毀多時，莫能修復。

translations.literal: Yuyang and Yan commanderies had the old Liling weirs, thirty li in breadth and length; all had long lain ruined, and none could restore them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyang and Yan commanderies had the old Liling weirs, thirty li across, all long abandoned and beyond repair.

sentences.zh: 時水旱不調，延俊乃表求營造。

translations.literal: At that time floods and droughts were out of balance; Yanjun therefore memorialized requesting construction.
translations.idiomatic: With floods and droughts alternating in distress, Yanjun memorialized the throne requesting that the works be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 遂躬自履行，相度形勢，隨力分督，未幾而就，溉田百萬餘畝，為利十倍，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: He then personally went on foot to inspect, surveyed the terrain, and according to capacity divided supervision; in no long time it was completed, irrigating more than a million mu of fields, with benefits tenfold, and the people relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: He walked the ground himself, surveyed the terrain, and assigned work according to local capacity. The projects were finished in short order, irrigating more than a million mu and yielding tenfold returns on the investment; the people came to depend on them.

sentences.zh: 又命主簿酈惲修起學校，禮教大行，人歌謠之。

translations.literal: He also ordered Chief Clerk Li Yun to repair and establish schools; ritual teaching flourished greatly, and people sang songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Chief Clerk Li Yun to restore the schools. Confucian teaching spread widely, and the people sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 在州五年，考績為天下最。

translations.literal: In five years in the province, his performance evaluation was the highest in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in office his performance review ranked first in the empire.

sentences.zh: 拜太常卿，曆七兵殿中二尚書、散騎常侍、中書令、御史中尉，又以本官兼侍中、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of Ceremonies, successively served as Director of the Seven Armies and of the Palace Secretariat, Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds, Director of the Secretariat, Censor-in-Chief, and also with his original office concurrently served as Attendant-in-Chief and Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of Ceremonies and went on to serve as Director of the Seven Armies, Director of the Palace Secretariat, Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds, Director of the Secretariat, and Censor-in-Chief, while also holding his original post concurrently with Attendant-in-Chief and Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 延俊在台閣，守職而已，不能有所裁斷直繩也。

translations.literal: Yanjun in the central offices merely kept his post and could not make judgments or enforce the straight cord.
translations.idiomatic: At court Yanjun merely fulfilled his duties and was unable to render decisive judgments or enforce the law with rigor.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，于河陰遇害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he met with harm at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈儀同三司、都督、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Commander-in-Chief, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted rank equal to the Three Excellencies and appointed Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子元直、敬猷，並有學尚，與父同時遇害。

translations.literal: His sons Yuanzhi and Jingyou both had scholarly attainments and met with harm at the same time as their father.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yuanzhi and Jingyou were both men of learning and were killed together with their father.

sentences.zh: 元直贈光州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi was posthumously made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi was posthumously appointed Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬猷妻丞相、高陽王雍外孫，超贈尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Jingyou's wife was granddaughter of Chancellor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong; he was posthumously promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyou's wife was a granddaughter of Chancellor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, and he was posthumously promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延俊從叔愛醜、桃弓並見稱於鄉里。

translations.literal: Yanjun's clansman-uncles Aichou and Taogong were both praised in their home district.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun's clansman-uncles Aichou and Taogong were both well regarded in their home district.

sentences.zh: 子夙，字買興。

translations.literal: His son Su, styled Maixing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su, styled Maixing.

sentences.zh: 沈雅有器識，儀望甚偉，孝文見而異之。

translations.literal: Composed and refined, with capacity and insight; his bearing and appearance were imposing; Emperor Xiaowen saw him and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Su was composed and refined, with real breadth of mind, and cut an imposing figure. Emperor Xiaowen noticed him and marked him as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書、任城王澄有知人鑒，每歎美夙，以遠大許之。

translations.literal: Minister of the Civil Service, Prince of Rencheng Cheng had a discerning eye for men; he often sighed in praise of Su and promised him a far-reaching future.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Rencheng Cheng, Minister of the Civil Service, was known for judging talent well; he often praised Su and predicted a great future for him.

sentences.zh: 位河北太守，以忠恕接下，百姓感而懷之。

translations.literal: He held the post of Administrator of Hebei; with loyalty and forbearance he treated those below him, and the people were moved and cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Hebei, treating subordinates with loyalty and forbearance until the people were moved to love him.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡。

translations.literal: He died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 三子，範、升之、鑒。

translations.literal: Three sons: Fan; Sheng Zhi; Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Fan, Sheng Zhi, and Jian.

sentences.zh: 鑒字道徽，性強正，有學涉，卒于廷尉卿。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Daohui, was by nature forceful and upright, with scholarly attainments; he died as Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, styled Daohui, was forceful and upright by nature, well read and accomplished, and died while serving as Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 鑒居官清苦，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Jian in office lived in integrity and hardship, and contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian lived an austere and incorrupt life in office, and public opinion praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 贈東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 澤本勁直，無所回避，及被出追還，折節和光。

translations.literal: Ze by nature was firm and straight, never avoiding anything; after being sent out and then recalled, he bent his conduct and softened his light.
translations.idiomatic: Ze had originally been forceful and blunt, never shying from a fight; but after exile and recall he tempered his manner and learned to conciliate.

sentences.zh: 然好戲笑，無規檢，故頻敗。

translations.literal: Yet he loved jesting and laughter, without restraint, and therefore frequently met with failure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved banter and lacked self-restraint, and so met with misfortune again and again.

sentences.zh: 妻钜鹿魏氏，恩好甚隆，不能暫相離，澤每從駕，其妻不宿。

translations.literal: His wife was of the Wei clan of Julu; their affection was very deep and they could not be parted even briefly; whenever Ze accompanied the imperial carriage, his wife would not stay the night apart.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a Wei of Julu, and their love ran so deep they could not bear even a brief separation. Whenever Ze accompanied the emperor on tour, his wife refused to spend the night apart from him.

sentences.zh: 亦至性強立，時人以為健婦夫半。

translations.literal: She too was by nature strong and resolute; people of the time considered her a vigorous woman equal to half a man.
translations.idiomatic: She too was strong-willed and resolute, and people of the day said she was half the man her husband was.

sentences.zh: 延俊從祖弟良，字元賓，稍遷尚書考功郎中。

translations.literal: Yanjun's collateral cousin Liang, styled Yuanbin, gradually rose to Gentleman of the Merit Evaluation Bureau in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun's collateral cousin Liang, styled Yuanbin, rose gradually to Gentleman of the Merit Evaluation Bureau in the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 時汾州吐京胡薛羽等作逆，以良兼尚書左丞，為西北道行台。

translations.literal: At that time the Tujing Hu of Fenzhou, Xue Yu and others rebelled; Liang was made concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Ministry and Commissioner of the Northwest Route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tujing Hu of Fenzhou, Xue Yu and others rebelled, Liang was appointed concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Ministry and Commissioner of the Northwest Route.

sentences.zh: 時有五城郡山胡馮宜都、賀悅回成等，以妖妄惑眾，假稱帝號，服素衣，持白傘白幡，率諸逆眾，於雲台郊抗王師。

translations.literal: At that time the mountain Hu of Wucheng commandery, Feng Yidu; He Yue; Huicheng; and others, with sorcery and falsehood deluded the masses, falsely claimed imperial titles, wore white garments, carried white umbrellas and white banners, and led the rebel hosts to resist the royal army at the outskirts of Yuntai.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain Hu of Wucheng commandery, Feng Yidu, He Yue, Huicheng, and others deluded the people with sorcery, proclaimed themselves emperors, dressed in white, and carrying white umbrellas and banners led their rebels against the imperial army at the outskirts of Yuntai.

sentences.zh: 良大破之。

translations.literal: Liang inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 又山胡劉蠡升，自雲聖術，胡人信人，咸相影附，旬日之間，逆徒還振。

translations.literal: Again the mountain Hu Liu Lisheng, claiming sacred arts, the Hu people believed in him, all followed one another's shadows and attached themselves; within ten days the rebels revived.
translations.idiomatic: Then the mountain Hu Liu Lisheng, claiming sacred powers, won the faith of the Hu people, who flocked to him in droves; within ten days the rebels had rallied again.

sentences.zh: 以良為汾州刺史，加輔國將軍，行台如故。

translations.literal: Liang was made Inspector of Fenzhou, promoted to General Who Assists the State, and the commission remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was appointed Inspector of Fenzhou and promoted to General Who Assists the State, while retaining his commission.

sentences.zh: 良以城人饑窘，夜率眾奔西河。

translations.literal: Liang because the people in the city were hungry and distressed, by night led the masses and fled to Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: With the city beset by famine, Liang led his forces by night to Xihe.

sentences.zh: 汾州之居西河，自良始也。

translations.literal: Fenzhou's residence in Xihe began with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: It was Liang who first moved the seat of Fenzhou to Xihe.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，為衛大將軍、太府卿，卒於官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was made Grand General of the Guard and Director of the Imperial Treasury; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was appointed Grand General of the Guard and Director of the Imperial Treasury, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，諡曰貞，又重贈侍中、尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of the Civil Service, posthumous title Zhen; again posthumously made Attendant-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of the Civil Service and given the posthumous title Zhen, and later posthumously promoted to Attendant-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子叔祉，粗涉文學，居官甚著聲績，位終司空右長史。

translations.literal: His son Shuzhi had a rough acquaintance with letters; in office he was very noted for reputation and achievement, and ended as Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuzhi had some literary training and won a strong reputation in office, ending his career as Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 良從父兄子慶孫，字紹遠。

translations.literal: Liang's clansman-brother's son Qingsun, styled Shaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's clansman-brother's son Qingsun, styled Shaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，性倜儻，重然諾。

translations.literal: He lost his father young; by nature he was free-spirited and valued keeping his word.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was free-spirited by nature and prized his word above all.

sentences.zh: 正光末，汾州吐京群胡薛悉公、馬牒騰並自立為王，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhengguang era, the Tujing Hu of Fenzhou, Xue Xigong; Ma Diedeng; and others all set themselves up as kings, their hosts reaching tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhengguang era the Tujing Hu of Fenzhou, Xue Xigong, Ma Diedeng, and others each declared themselves kings, gathering forces in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 詔慶孫為募人別將，招率鄉豪以討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Qingsun a Separate Commander for Recruiting Men, to summon and lead local magnates to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Qingsun Separate Commander for Recruiting Men and ordered him to rally local leaders against them.

sentences.zh: 慶孫每摧其鋒，進軍深入，至雲台郊；

translations.literal: Qingsun each time broke their spearhead, advanced the army deep in, and reached the outskirts of Yuntai;
translations.idiomatic: Qingsun repeatedly broke their vanguard and pushed deep into enemy territory as far as the outskirts of Yuntai;

sentences.zh: 大戰郊西，賊眾大潰。

translations.literal: A great battle west of the outskirts; the rebel masses were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: in a great battle west of the city he put the rebels to rout.

sentences.zh: 征赴都，除直後。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, he was appointed Direct Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital, he was appointed Direct Guard.

sentences.zh: 於是賊復鳩集，北連蠡升，南通絳蜀，凶徒轉盛。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandits again gathered like doves, linking north with Lisheng and south with Jiang-Shu, and the vicious hosts grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then regrouped, linking with Lisheng in the north and the Jiang-Shu insurgents in the south, and the outlaw bands grew stronger still.

sentences.zh: 以慶孫為別將，從軹關入討，深入二百餘里，至陽胡城。

translations.literal: Qingsun was made Separate Commander, entered to attack through Zhiguan Pass, penetrated deep more than two hundred li, and reached Yanghu city.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsun was appointed Separate Commander, entered through Zhiguan Pass to attack, and pushed more than two hundred li inland to Yanghu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以此地被山帶河，衿要之所，明帝末，遂立邵郡，因以慶孫為太守。

translations.literal: The court because this region was girded by mountains and embraced by rivers, a place of strategic throat, at the end of Emperor Ming's reign therefore established Shao commandery, and accordingly made Qingsun its Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Because the region was hemmed in by mountains and rivers and held a strategic choke point, the court established Shao commandery late in Emperor Ming's reign and appointed Qingsun its Administrator.

sentences.zh: 慶孫務安緝之，咸來歸業。

translations.literal: Qingsun devoted himself to pacifying and settling it; all came back to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsun worked to pacify and settle the region, and the people all returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之死也，世隆擁眾北度，詔慶孫為大都督，與行台源子恭率眾追擊。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong led the masses north across the river; an edict made Qingsun Grand Commander-in-Chief, and with Commissioner Yuan Zigong he led the hosts in pursuit and attack.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Shilong led his forces north across the Yellow River. Qingsun was appointed Grand Commander-in-Chief and, with Commissioner Yuan Zigong, pursued them.

sentences.zh: 慶孫與世隆密通，事泄，追還河內斬之。

translations.literal: Qingsun secretly communicated with Shilong; the matter leaked out, he was recalled and beheaded at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsun had been in secret contact with Shilong; when this came to light he was recalled and executed at Henei.

sentences.zh: 慶孫任俠有氣，鄉曲壯士及好事者多相依附，撫養咸有恩紀。

translations.literal: Qingsun was chivalrous and spirited; local stalwarts and men who loved bold deeds mostly relied on and attached themselves to him, and in nurturing them all he had bonds of kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Qingsun was a man of chivalry and spirit; local braves and men who loved adventure gathered around him, and he treated them all with generous care.

sentences.zh: 在郡日，逢歲饑凶，四方遊客恆有百餘，慶孫自以家糧贍之。

translations.literal: While in the commandery, encountering years of famine and disaster, traveling guests from the four directions constantly numbered more than a hundred, and Qingsun with his household grain supported them.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the commandery, during years of famine more than a hundred itinerants were constantly under his roof, and Qingsun fed them from his own stores.

sentences.zh: 性雖粗武，愛好文流，與諸才學之士咸相交結。

translations.literal: Though by nature somewhat rough and martial, he loved and favored men of letters, and with all talented and learned scholars he equally formed friendships.
translations.idiomatic: Though rough and martial by temperament, he loved the company of scholars and befriended every man of talent he met.

sentences.zh: 輕財重義，坐客恆滿，是以為時所稱。

translations.literal: He held righteousness heavy and wealth light; seated guests were constantly full, and therefore he was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He valued honor over money, his hall was always full of guests, and for this he was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 延俊從祖弟仲規，少好經史，頗有志節。

translations.literal: Yanjun's collateral cousin Zhonggui from youth loved the classics and histories and had considerable resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun's collateral cousin Zhonggui loved the classics and histories from youth and showed real strength of character.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧為司州牧，辟為主簿，仍表行建興郡事。

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi as Governor of Sizhou recruited him as Chief Clerk, and also memorialized that he act as Administrator of Jianxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Xianyang Xi became Governor of Sizhou he recruited Zhonggui as Chief Clerk and recommended him to act as Administrator of Jianxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 車駕自代還洛，次於郡境。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage from Dai returned to Luoyang and halted within the commandery's borders.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned from Dai to Luoyang, it halted within the commandery's borders.

sentences.zh: 仲規備供帳，朝于路側。

translations.literal: Zhonggui prepared supplies and tents and presented himself beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggui prepared provisions and lodging and presented himself beside the road.

sentences.zh: 詔仲規曰：「畿郡望重，卿何能自致此也？

translations.literal: An edict addressed Zhonggui: "The capital circuit commandery carries heavy prestige—how could you bring this about on your own?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor addressed Zhonggui: "This capital circuit commandery carries great weight—how did you manage all this yourself?

sentences.zh: 」仲規曰：「陛下棄彼玄壤，來宅紫縣，臣方躍馬吳、會，冀功銘帝籍，豈一郡而已。

translations.literal: " Zhonggui said, "Your Majesty abandoned that dark earth and came to dwell in the Purple Capital; your servant was just then ready to gallop through Wu and Kuaiji, hoping that merit would be inscribed in the imperial registers—how could it be only one commandery?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhonggui replied, "Your Majesty left the northern capital to establish the Purple Capital; I was ready to ride through Wu and Kuaiji and hoped to win merit recorded in the imperial annals—not for the sake of one commandery alone.

sentences.zh: 」孝文笑曰：「冀卿必副此言。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowen laughed and said, "I hope you will surely live up to these words.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowen laughed and said, "I expect you will live up to those words.

sentences.zh: 」駕還，見咸陽王曰：「昨得汝主簿為南道主人，六軍豐贍。

translations.literal: " The carriage returned; seeing the Prince of Xianyang he said, "Yesterday I had your Chief Clerk as host on the southern route—the Six Armies were abundantly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return the emperor told the Prince of Xianyang, "Yesterday your Chief Clerk served as host on the southern route, and the Six Armies wanted for nothing.

sentences.zh: 元弟之寄，殊副所望。

translations.literal: The trust placed in younger brother Yuan fully matched what was hoped.
translations.idiomatic: The charge I placed in you, younger brother Yuan, has been fully answered.

sentences.zh: 」除司徒主簿。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhonggui was appointed Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 仲規父在鄉疾病，棄官奔赴，以違制免。

translations.literal: Zhonggui's father was ill in the village; he abandoned his office and rushed to him, and was dismissed for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhonggui's father fell ill at home he left his post to go to him and was dismissed for violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 久之，中山王英征義陽，引為統軍，奏復本資。

translations.literal: After a long while, Prince of Zhongshan Ying campaigned against Yiyang and brought him in as Army Controller; he memorialized to restore his original salary.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Prince of Zhongshan Ying campaigned against Yiyang, took him on as Army Controller, and memorialized for restoration of his original rank and pay.

sentences.zh: 于陣戰沒。

translations.literal: He fell in battle in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈河東太守，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Administrator of Hedong, posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Administrator of Hedong and given the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟叔義以第二子伯茂後之。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Shuyi made his second son Bomao his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his younger brother Shuyi had his second son Bomao succeed him.

sentences.zh: 伯茂少有風望，學涉群書，文藻富贍，釋褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: Bomao from youth had reputation and bearing, ranged in learning through many books, and his literary adornments were rich and ample; upon leaving the hemp he was made Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao won early renown, read widely, and wrote with rich fluency; upon entering office he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、京兆王繼西討，引為鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: Great General, Prince of Jingzhao Ji on the western campaign brought him in as Army Staff Officer of the Armor Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Great General, Prince of Jingzhao Ji launched the western campaign, he took Bomao on as Army Staff Officer of the Armor Bureau.

sentences.zh: 南征絳蜀陳雙熾，為行台長孫承業行台郎中。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign against the Jiang-Shu Chen Shuangchi, he served as Gentleman of the Commission under Commissioner Zhangsun Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign against the Jiang-Shu rebel Chen Shuangchi he served as Gentleman of the Commission under Commissioner Zhangsun Chengye.

sentences.zh: 承業還京師，留伯茂仍知行台事。

translations.literal: Chengye returned to the capital; Bomao was left behind and still acted as commissioner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengye returned to the capital, Bomao remained behind to continue handling commission affairs.

sentences.zh: 以平薛鳳賢等，賞平陽伯。

translations.literal: For pacifying Xue Fengxian and others, he was rewarded with the title Baron of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing Xue Fengxian and others he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 再遷散騎常侍，典起居注。

translations.literal: Again promoted to Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds, he managed the Records of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: He was next promoted to Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds and put in charge of the Records of the Emperor's Movements.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was appointed Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，孝武帝兄子廣平王贊盛選賓寮，以伯茂為文學。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, Emperor Xiaowu's elder brother's son Prince of Guangping Zan greatly selected guest officials, and made Bomao Literary Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, Prince of Guangping Zan, a nephew of Emperor Xiaowu, carefully chose his staff and appointed Bomao Literary Instructor.

sentences.zh: 後加中軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally made Great General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was later additionally appointed Great General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 伯茂好飲酒，頗涉疏傲。

translations.literal: Bomao loved drinking wine and rather fell into looseness and arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao was fond of wine and inclined toward heedlessness and arrogance.

sentences.zh: 久不徙官，曾為《豁情賦》。

translations.literal: Long without transfer of office, he once composed "Rhapsody on Opening the Feelings."
translations.idiomatic: Untransferred for a long time, he once wrote "Rhapsody on Opening the Feelings."

sentences.zh: 天平初遷鄴，又為《遷都賦》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, when the court moved to Ye, he again composed "Rhapsody on Moving the Capital."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianping era, when the court moved to Ye, he also wrote "Rhapsody on Moving the Capital."

sentences.zh: 二年，因內宴，伯茂侮慢殿中尚書、章武王景哲。

translations.literal: In the second year, during an inner palace banquet, Bomao insulted and slighted Palace Attendant Secretary, Prince of Zhangwu Jingzhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, at an inner palace banquet, Bomao insulted Palace Attendant Secretary, Prince of Zhangwu Jingzhe.

sentences.zh: 景哲遂申啟，稱伯茂棄其本列，與監同行，以梨擊案，傍汙冠服，禁庭之內，令人挈衣。

translations.literal: Jingzhe then submitted a report, saying Bomao had abandoned his proper rank, walked alongside the superintendent, struck the table with a pear, and beside him soiled cap and robes; within the forbidden court he had men clutch his garments.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhe submitted a report charging that Bomao had left his proper place, walked abreast with a superintendent, struck the table with a pear and splattered those nearby, and within the palace grounds had attendants hold up his clothes for him.

sentences.zh: 詔付所司，後竟無坐。

translations.literal: An edict handed the matter to the relevant office; in the end he was never punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the case handed to the appropriate authorities, but in the end Bomao was never convicted.

sentences.zh: 伯茂既出後其伯仲規，與兄景融別居。

translations.literal: After Bomao had left being heir to his elder brother Zhonggui, he lived separately from his elder brother Jingrong.
translations.idiomatic: After Bomao ceased to be heir to his elder brother Zhonggui, he lived apart from his elder brother Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 景融貧窘，伯茂了無賑恤，殆同行路，世以此貶薄之。

translations.literal: Jingrong was poor and straitened; Bomao entirely lacked relief and aid, almost like passers-by on the road; the age for this belittled and slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong lived in poverty, yet Bomao gave him no help at all—as if they were strangers—and the world despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十九，知舊嘆惜焉。

translations.literal: He died, aged thirty-nine; old acquaintances sighed and lamented.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-nine, to the sorrow of all who knew him.

sentences.zh: 伯茂末年，劇飲不已，乃至傷性，多有愆失。

translations.literal: In Bomao's last years he drank immoderately without stop, even to harming his nature, and often had faults and lapses.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years Bomao drank without restraint, to the point of damaging his health, and committed many lapses.

sentences.zh: 未亡前數日，忽雲吾得密信，將被收掩，乃與婦乘車西逃避。

translations.literal: Several days before he had not yet died, he suddenly said he had received a secret letter and would be arrested and seized, and so with his wife took a carriage and fled west to escape.
translations.idiomatic: A few days before his death he suddenly declared he had received a secret message that he was about to be seized, and fled west with his wife in a carriage.

sentences.zh: 後因顧指壁中，言有官人追逐，其妻方知其病。

translations.literal: Later he turned and pointed at the wall, saying officials were pursuing; his wife then knew he was ill.
translations.idiomatic: Later he turned and pointed at the wall, saying officials were chasing him; only then did his wife realize he was deranged.

sentences.zh: 卒後，殯於家園。

translations.literal: After he died, he was encoffined at the family estate.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was laid out for burial at the family estate.

sentences.zh: 友人常景、李渾、王元景、盧元明、魏季景、李騫等十許人於墓傍置酒設祭，哀哭涕泣，一飲一酹，曰：「裴中書魂而有靈，知吾曹也。

translations.literal: Friends Chang Jing, Li Hun, Wang Yuanjing, Lu Yuanming, Wei Jijing, Li Qian, and some ten others set out wine and made offerings beside the tomb, wailing and weeping in grief; with each drink and each libation they said: "Director of the Secretariat Pei, if your soul has spirit, you know us."
translations.idiomatic: Some ten friends—Chang Jing, Li Hun, Wang Yuanjing, Lu Yuanming, Wei Jijing, Li Qian, and others—set up wine and offerings beside his tomb, weeping in grief; with each drink and each libation they said, "Director of the Secretariat Pei, if your spirit lives on, you know who we are."

sentences.zh: 」乃各賦詩一篇。

translations.literal: " Each then composed one poem.
translations.idiomatic: " Each then wrote a poem.

sentences.zh: 李騫以魏收亦與之友，寄以示收。

translations.literal: Li Qian, since Wei Shou was also his friend, sent them to show Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qian sent the poems to Wei Shou, who had also been Bomao's friend.

sentences.zh: 收時在晉陽，乃同其作，論敘伯茂，其十字云：「臨風想玄度，對酒思公榮。

translations.literal: Shou was then at Jinyang, and joined in their composition, narrating Bomao; its ten characters said: "Facing the wind one thinks of Xuandu; facing wine one thinks of Gongrong."
translations.idiomatic: Shou was then at Jinyang and contributed his own piece on Bomao; its ten-character line read, "Facing the wind I think of Xu Xuan; over wine I think of Liu Gongrong."

sentences.zh: 」時人以伯茂性侮傲，謂收詩頗得事實。

translations.literal: " People of the time, because Bomao's nature was arrogant and insulting, said Shou's poem rather hit the facts.
translations.idiomatic: " Because Bomao's nature was haughty and overbearing, contemporaries said Shou's lines captured him well.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、衛將軍、度支尚書，雍州刺史，重贈吏部尚書，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds, Guard General, Minister of Revenue, Inspector of Yongzhou; again posthumously made Minister of the Personnel, posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds, Guard General, and Minister of Revenue with concurrent duty as Inspector of Yongzhou; later posthumously promoted to Minister of the Personnel with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 伯茂曾撰晉書，竟未能成。

translations.literal: Bomao once compiled a History of Jin; in the end he was unable to finish it.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao once undertook a History of Jin but never completed it.

sentences.zh: 無子，兄景融以第二子孝才繼。

translations.literal: He had no son; elder brother Jingrong had his second son Xiaocai succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his elder brother Jingrong had his second son Xiaocai succeed him.

sentences.zh: 齊武平末，位中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi Wuping, he held the post of Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Wuping era of Northern Qi he served as Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 叔義亦有學行，累遷太山太守，為政清靜，吏人安之。

translations.literal: Shuyi also had learning and conduct; promoted repeatedly to Administrator of Taishan; his government was pure and quiet, and officials and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyi was likewise learned and principled; promoted to Administrator of Taishan, he governed quietly and effectively, and officials and commoners alike lived at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to Attendant Officer of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Officer of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈東秦州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Inspector of Eastern Qinzhou, posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Eastern Qinzhou and given the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子景融，字孔明，篤學好屬文。

translations.literal: His son Jingrong, styled Kongming, deeply studied and loved composing writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingrong, styled Kongming, was deeply learned and fond of literary composition.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，射策高第，除太學博士，稍遷諫議大夫，領著作。

translations.literal: Recommended as Presented Scholar; in the policy-examination he placed high; appointed Erudite of the Imperial University; gradually promoted to Grand Master of Remonstrance, concurrently Director of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he placed at the top in the policy examination and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University; he rose gradually to Grand Master of Remonstrance and concurrent Director of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 元象中，儀同高嶽以為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era, Yitong Gao Yue made him Recording Affairs Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanxiang era, Yitong Gao Yue appointed him Recording Affairs Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 弟景龍、景顏被劾廷尉獄，景融入選。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Jinglong and Jingyan were impeached and imprisoned in the Court of Justice; Jingrong entered the capital for selection.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Jinglong and Jingyan were impeached and held in the Court of Justice prison; Jingrong went to the capital seeking an appointment.

sentences.zh: 吏部擬郡，為御史中尉崔暹所彈，雲其貪榮昧進，遂坐免官。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel proposed him for a commandery; he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian, who said he greedily sought glory and blindly advanced; he was consequently dismissed and deprived of office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Personnel proposed him for a commandery post, Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian impeached him for seeking advancement while blind to propriety, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 病卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 景融卑退廉謹，無競于時，雖才不稱學，而緝綴無倦，文詞氾濫，理會處寡。

translations.literal: Jingrong was humble, retiring, honest, and careful, without competing in his time; though his talent did not match his learning, he compiled and stitched without weariness; literary language overflowed, and where reasoning grasped the point was very little.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong was modest, retiring, and scrupulously honest, seeking no edge in worldly competition; though his talent did not equal his learning, he wrote tirelessly—yet his prose ran to excess and sound reasoning was scarce in it.

sentences.zh: 所作文章，別有集錄。

translations.literal: The writings he composed were separately collected in a record.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were collected in a separate compilation.

sentences.zh: 景顏頗有學尚，孝靜初，為司空長史，在官貪穢，為中尉崔暹所劾，遇病死獄中。

translations.literal: Jingyan had considerable scholarly attainment; early in Xiaojing he was Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works; in office he was greedy and corrupt, was impeached by Censor Cui Xian, and happened to die of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan was a man of some learning; early in the Xiaojing reign he served as Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, but in office he was corrupt; Censor Cui Xian impeached him, and he died in prison of illness.

sentences.zh: 延俊族兄聿，字外興，以操尚貞立，被孝文所知。

translations.literal: Yanjun's collateral elder clansman Yu, styled Waixing, because of pure and upright principles was known to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun's collateral elder clansman Yu, styled Waixing, won Emperor Xiaowen's notice for his upright character.

sentences.zh: 為北中府長史。

translations.literal: He was Chief Clerk of the Northern Central Prefecture headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chief Clerk of the Northern Central Prefecture headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時帝以聿與中書侍郎崔亮清貧，欲以幹錄優之，乃以亮帶野王縣事，聿帶溫縣。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor, because Yu and Secretariat Attendant Cui Liang were pure and poor, wished to favor them with stipends from administrative posts, and so had Liang concurrently oversee Yewang County affairs and Yu concurrently oversee Wen County.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting that Yu and Secretariat Attendant Cui Liang lived in upright poverty, wished to augment their income with administrative posts and had Liang take charge of Yewang County and Yu take charge of Wen County.

sentences.zh: 時人榮之。

translations.literal: People of the time honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held this up as an honor.

sentences.zh: 卒于平秦郡太守，贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Died as Administrator of Pingqin commandery; posthumously made Inspector of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Administrator of Pingqin Commandery and was posthumously appointed Inspector of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 子子袖入關西。

translations.literal: His son Zixiu entered Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixiu went west through the passes into Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 延俊族人瑗，字珍寶，太和中析屬河北郡。

translations.literal: Yanjun's clansman Yuan, styled Zhenbao, in the Taihe era was partitioned off to belong to Hebei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun's kinsman Yuan, styled Zhenbao, was reassigned to Hebei Commandery in the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，清苦自立。

translations.literal: From youth orphaned and poor, he stood on his own through purity and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from youth, he maintained himself through austere self-reliance.

sentences.zh: 為汝南王悅郎中令。

translations.literal: He was Chief of the Palace Office for Prince of Runan Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chief of the Palace Office for Prince of Runan Yue.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，卒于雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaojing he died as Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaojing reign he died while serving as Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 延俊從父兄宣明，位華州刺史，有惠政，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Yanjun's collateral elder cousin Xuanming held the post of Inspector of Huazhou; he had benevolent government; posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun's collateral elder cousin Xuanming served as Inspector of Huazhou, where his rule was humane; he received the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 二子景鸞、景鴻，並有逸才，河東呼景鸞為驥子，景鴻為龍文。

translations.literal: Two sons Jingluan and Jinghong; both had exceptional talent; east of the River they called Jingluan "Colt" and Jinghong "Dragon Pattern."
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Jingluan and Jinghong both showed exceptional talent; in Hedong people called Jingluan "the Foal" and Jinghong "Dragon Script."

sentences.zh: 景鸞位華州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingluan held the post of Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingluan served as Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 子文端，齊行台郎。

translations.literal: Son Wenduan, Qi Directorate staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenduan was a staff officer of the Qi Directorate.

sentences.zh: 四子，願、安志、弘、振。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yuan, Anzhi, Hong, and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Yuan, Anzhi, Hong, and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 景鴻，齊和夷郡守。

translations.literal: Jinghong, Qi Prefect of Heyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghong served as Prefect of Heyi Commandery under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 子叔卿，博涉有孝行，時人號曰「裴曾子」。

translations.literal: Son Shuqing, broadly versed and with filial conduct; people of the time called him "Pei Zengzi."
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuqing was widely read and renowned for filial piety; contemporaries called him "Pei Zengzi."

sentences.zh: 隋貝丘令。

translations.literal: Sui Magistrate of Beiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he was Magistrate of Beiqiu.

sentences.zh: 子神舉、神符，而神舉最知名。

translations.literal: Sons Shenju and Shenfu; Shenju was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Shenju and Shenfu; Shenju was the best known.

sentences.zh: 裴佗，字元化，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Tuo, styled Yuanhua, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tuo, styled Yuanhua, was from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 六世祖詵，仕晉位太常卿。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Shen served Jin and held the post of Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Shen served under the Jin and rose to Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 因晉亂，避地涼州。

translations.literal: Because of Jin disorder, he avoided the turmoil by going to Liangzhou.
