translations.idiomatic: When the Jin fell into chaos he fled to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 苻堅平河西，東歸，因居解縣。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian pacified Hexi, he returned east and hence lived in Jie County.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian conquered Hexi he returned east and settled in Jie County.

sentences.zh: 世以文學顯，五舉秀才，再舉孝廉，時人美之。

translations.literal: For generations they were illustrious in literary learning; five times recommended as Presented Scholar, twice as Filial and Incorrupt; people of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The family was renowned for generations in letters; he was five times recommended as Presented Scholar and twice as Filial and Incorrupt, winning contemporaries' admiration.

sentences.zh: 父景惠，州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Jinghui, Vice-Prefect of the province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jinghui served as Vice-Prefect of the province.

sentences.zh: 佗容貌魁偉，聵然有器望。

translations.literal: Tuo's appearance was towering and imposing; with dignity he had capacity and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was tall and imposing, with a dignified bearing that commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，以高第除中書博士。

translations.literal: Recommended as Presented Scholar; with high placement appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he placed at the top and was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 累遷趙郡太守，為政有方，威惠甚著，狡吏奸人，莫不改貫，所得俸祿，分恤貧窮。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to Administrator of Zhao commandery; his government had method; authority and kindness were very marked; crafty officials and wicked men none failed to change their ways; salary received he divided to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Zhao Commandery, where he governed effectively and won renown for both firmness and kindness; corrupt officials and evil-doers all mended their ways, and he gave his salary in shares to the poor.

sentences.zh: 轉前將軍、荊州刺史，郡人戀仰，傾境餞送。

translations.literal: Transferred to General of the Vanguard, Inspector of Jingzhou; commandery people yearned for and honored him; the whole territory turned out to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Vanguard and Inspector of Jingzhou; the people clung to him in devotion, and the whole region turned out to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋田磐石、田敬宗等部落萬餘家，恃眾阻險，不賓王命，前後牧守，未能降款。

translations.literal: Man chieftains Tian Panshi, Tian Jingzong, and others—more than ten thousand households in their tribes—relied on numbers and blocked by danger, did not submit to the king's command; successive governors and prefects were unable to reduce them to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Man chieftains Tian Panshi, Tian Jingzong, and others commanded more than ten thousand tribal households; relying on numbers and rugged terrain they refused imperial authority, and successive regional governors had failed to bring them in.

sentences.zh: 佗至州，單使宣慰，示以禍福，田敬宗聞風歸附。

translations.literal: When Tuo reached the province, he sent envoys alone to proclaim consolation, showed them fortune and disaster; Tian Jingzong heard the wind and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuo took up his post he sent emissaries alone to offer reassurance, showing them the consequences of submission or resistance; Tian Jingzong submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 於是合境清晏，繈負至者千餘家。

translations.literal: Thereupon the whole territory was pure and peaceful; families carrying infants on their backs who arrived numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The whole region then grew calm and orderly, and more than a thousand households arrived carrying infants on their backs.

sentences.zh: 後加中軍將軍，以老乞還。

translations.literal: Later additionally made General of the Central Army; because of age requested return.
translations.idiomatic: He was later additionally appointed General of the Central Army and, citing old age, asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺令不聽請贈，不受賵襚，諸子皆遵行之。

translations.literal: He died; testamentary order did not permit requesting posthumous honors, did not accept funeral gifts and shroud offerings; all sons obeyed and carried this out.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he left instructions forbidding posthumous honors, refusing funeral gifts and grave goods—and his sons all obeyed.

sentences.zh: 佗性剛直，不好與俗人交遊，其投分者必當時名勝。

translations.literal: Tuo's nature was upright and straight; he did not like to associate and roam with vulgar men; those with whom he shared conviction were necessarily famous worthies of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was forthright by nature and avoided the company of ordinary men; his intimate friends were invariably the celebrated figures of the age.

sentences.zh: 清白任真，不事家產，宅不過三十步，又無田園，暑不張蓋，寒不衣裘，其貞儉若此。

translations.literal: Pure and white, trusting to truth, he did not tend family property; his dwelling was no more than thirty paces, and he had no fields or gardens; in summer he did not spread a canopy, in cold he did not wear furs; his integrity and thrift were thus.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in plain integrity and cared nothing for wealth; his house measured no more than thirty paces and he owned no farmland; in summer he used no parasol, in winter wore no furs—such was his austerity.

sentences.zh: 子讓之。

translations.literal: Son Rangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rangzhi.

sentences.zh: 讓之字士禮，年十六喪父，殆不勝哀。

translations.literal: Rangzhi, styled Shili, at age sixteen lost his father and nearly could not bear the grief.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi, styled Shili, lost his father at sixteen and nearly succumbed to grief.

sentences.zh: 其母辛氏泣撫之曰：「棄我滅性，得為孝子乎！

translations.literal: His mother Lady Xin, weeping, comforted him and said: "Abandoning me and extinguishing your nature—can that be filial?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Xin, wept as she comforted him: "Would you leave me and destroy yourself and still call that filial piety?"

sentences.zh: 」由是自勉。

translations.literal: " From this he roused himself.
translations.idiomatic: " From that he rallied himself.

sentences.zh: 辛氏高明婦人，又閑禮度；

translations.literal: Lady Xin was an eminent and discerning woman, and also versed in ritual and measure;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xin was a woman of high intelligence, well versed in ritual propriety;

sentences.zh: 夫喪，諸子多幼弱，廣延師友，或親自教授，內外親屬有吉凶禮制，多取則焉。

translations.literal: When her husband died, the sons were mostly young and weak; she widely extended teachers and friends, or personally taught; inner and outer kin for auspicious and inauspicious rites and institutions mostly took their norms from her.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband's death, with most of her sons still young, she sought out teachers far and wide and sometimes taught them herself; kin near and distant alike looked to her for guidance in ritual matters, joyous or mournful.

sentences.zh: 讓之少好學，有文情，清明俊辯，早得聲譽。

translations.literal: Rangzhi from youth loved learning, had literary sensibility, was clear and bright, handsome in disputation, and early gained reputation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Rangzhi loved learning; gifted in letters, lucid and eloquent, he won an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 魏天平中，舉秀才，對策高第。

translations.literal: In Wei Tianping, recommended as Presented Scholar; policy answer high placement.
translations.idiomatic: During Northern Wei's Tianping era he was recommended as Presented Scholar and placed at the top in the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷屯田、主客郎中，省中語曰「能賦詩，裴讓之」。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to Gentleman of the Colonies and of the Hosts; within the secretariat the saying was "Able to compose poetry—Pei Rangzhi."
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts as Gentleman of the Colonies and Gentleman of the Hosts; at court they said, "When poetry is needed, there is Pei Rangzhi."

sentences.zh: 為太原公開府記室。

translations.literal: Became Recorder for Prince of Taiyuan's office establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Recorder on the staff of Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 與楊愔友善，相遇則清談竟日。

translations.literal: With Yang Yin he was good friends; when they met they would pure-talk the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Yang Yin; when they met they would talk abstruse matters all day long.

sentences.zh: 愔每云：「此人風流警拔，裴文季為不亡矣。

translations.literal: Yin often said: "This man's style is flowing, alert, and outstanding; Pei Wenji is not dead."
translations.idiomatic: Yin often said, "This man's brilliance is sharp and extraordinary—Pei Wenji lives again in him."

sentences.zh: 」梁使至，常令讓之攝主客郎。

translations.literal: " When Liang envoys arrived, he was often made Acting Gentleman of the Hosts.
translations.idiomatic: " When envoys from Liang arrived, Rangzhi was regularly deputized as Gentleman of the Hosts.

sentences.zh: 第二弟諏之奔關右，兄弟五人皆拘系。

translations.literal: Second younger brother Souzhi fled to Guan right; five brothers all were detained and bound.
translations.idiomatic: His second younger brother Souzhi fled west to Guanzhong, and all five brothers were arrested.

sentences.zh: 齊神武問云：「諏之何在？

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu asked saying: "Where is Souzhi?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan of Northern Qi asked, "Where is Souzhi?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔吳、蜀二國，諸葛兄弟各得盡心，況讓之老母在此，君臣分定，失忠與孝，愚夫不為。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Formerly in the two states of Wu and Shu, the Zhuge brothers each could give full heart; moreover Rangzhi's old mother is here; lord and minister roles are fixed—losing loyalty and filiality, a dull man would not do it."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "In Wu and Shu the Zhuge brothers each served his own lord with full devotion; and Rangzhi's aged mother is here. When the roles of ruler and subject are fixed, neither loyalty nor filial piety can be cast aside—no fool would do that."

sentences.zh: 伏願明公以誠信待物。

translations.literal: I bow and wish the enlightened lord to treat beings with sincerity and trust.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, my lord, to treat people with sincerity and good faith.

sentences.zh: 若以不收處物，物亦安能自信？

translations.literal: If one treats beings with distrust and non-acceptance, how can beings confidently trust themselves?
translations.idiomatic: If you receive people with suspicion, how can they trust you in return?

sentences.zh: 以此定霸，猶卻行而求道耳。

translations.literal: Using this to settle hegemony is like walking backward while seeking the Way.
translations.idiomatic: To build an empire on that would be like walking backward while trying to find the road ahead.

sentences.zh: 」神武善其言，兄弟俱釋。

translations.literal: " Shenwu approved his words; the brothers were all released.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan was pleased with his answer and released all the brothers.

sentences.zh: 曆文襄大將軍主簿，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Served successively as Chief Clerk to Wenxiang Great General, concurrently Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Chief Clerk on Wenxiang's staff and as concurrent Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 後兼散騎常侍聘梁。

translations.literal: Later concurrently Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds, envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Rapid Steeds on a mission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 文襄嘗入朝，讓之導引，容儀醖籍，文襄目之曰：「士禮，佳舍人也。

translations.literal: Wenxiang once entered court; Rangzhi guided him; bearing and manner were cultured and refined; Wenxiang eyed him saying: "Shili, excellent drafting officer."
translations.idiomatic: Once when Gao Cheng attended court, Rangzhi guided him—his carriage graceful and dignified. Gao Cheng looked at him and said, "Shili, what an excellent drafting officer."

sentences.zh: 」遷長兼中書侍郎，領舍人。

translations.literal: " Promoted to senior concurrent Secretariat Attendant, heading drafting officers.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to senior concurrent Secretariat Attendant and put in charge of the drafting officers.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，靜帝遜居別宮，與諸臣別，讓之流涕歔欷。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Emperor Jing withdrew to a separate palace and parted from the various ministers; Rangzhi shed tears and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi accepted the abdication, Emperor Jing withdrew to a detached palace to take leave of his ministers; Rangzhi wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 以參掌儀注，封寧都縣男。

translations.literal: For participating in managing ritual regulations, enfeoffed as Baron of Ningdu county.
translations.idiomatic: For helping to oversee court ritual he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningdu County.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以為黃門侍郎，或言其體重不堪趨侍，乃除清河太守。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make him Attendant of the Yellow Gate; someone said his body was heavy and could not bear hurrying attendance; he was then appointed Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint him Attendant of the Yellow Gate, but others said his stout frame was unsuited to close attendance at court, and he was made Administrator of Qinghe instead.

sentences.zh: 至郡未幾，楊愔謂讓之諸弟曰：「我與賢兄交款，企聞善政，適有人從清河來，雲奸吏斂跡，盜賊清靖。

translations.literal: Not long after reaching the commandery, Yang Yin said to Rangzhi's various younger brothers: "I and your worthy elder brother are close in friendship; I hope to hear of good government; just now someone came from Qinghe saying corrupt officials reined in their steps, bandits and thieves were pure and quiet."
translations.idiomatic: Not long after Rangzhi took office, Yang Yin told his brothers, "Your worthy elder brother and I are close friends, and I have long looked forward to news of his good governance; someone has just arrived from Qinghe reporting that corrupt officials have gone into hiding and banditry has been suppressed."

sentences.zh: 期月之期，翻更非速。」

translations.literal: The period of a full month—a turn, rather not fast."
translations.idiomatic: To accomplish so much in little more than a month is almost too quick for belief."

sentences.zh: 清河有二豪吏田轉貴、孫舍興，久吏奸猾，多有侵削，因事遂脅人取財，計贓依律不至死，讓之以其亂法，殺之。

translations.literal: In Qinghe there were two powerful petty officials Tian Zhuangui and Sun Shexing—long-serving crafty and cunning men who greatly encroached and cut away; taking advantage of affairs they then extorted people for wealth; calculating the stolen goods by law did not reach death; Rangzhi because they disrupted law killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe had two powerful petty officials, Tian Zhuan'gui and Sun Shexing, veteran clerks who were cunning and corrupt and who for years had extorted and embezzled from the people. On one matter they blackmailed people for money; by the statute the amount stolen did not warrant the death penalty, but Rangzhi had them executed for subverting the law.

sentences.zh: 時清河王岳為司州牧，遣部從事案之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Qinghe Yue was Governor of Sizhou; he dispatched a headquarters assistant to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Qinghe Yue was serving as Governor of Sizhou and sent a headquarters aide to investigate.

sentences.zh: 侍中高德政舊與讓之不協，密奏言：「當陛下受禪之時，讓之眷戀魏朝，嗚咽流涕，比為內官，情非所願。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Dezheng had long been at odds with Rangzhi; he secretly memorialized saying: "When Your Majesty received the abdication, Rangzhi was attached to the Wei dynasty and sobbed with flowing tears; now made inner court official, in feeling it is not what he wished."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Gao Dezheng had long been at odds with Rangzhi and submitted a secret memorial: "When Your Majesty accepted the abdication, Rangzhi clung to devotion for the Wei and wept aloud; now serving as an inner-court official, his heart is not in it."

sentences.zh: 」既而楊愔請救之，雲罪不合死。

translations.literal: " Then Yang Yin pleaded to save him, saying the crime did not merit death.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Yin then interceded on his behalf, arguing that the offence did not call for death.

sentences.zh: 文宣大怒，謂愔曰：「欲得與裴讓之同塚邪！

translations.literal: Wenxuan was greatly angry and said to Yin: "Do you wish to share a grave with Pei Rangzhi?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan flew into a rage and said to Yin, "Do you want to share a tomb with Pei Rangzhi?

sentences.zh: 」於是無敢言者，事奏，竟賜死於家。

translations.literal: " Thereupon none dared speak; the matter was reported; in the end he was granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: " After that no one dared speak up. When the case was reported up, Rangzhi was ultimately ordered to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 讓之次弟諏之，字士正。

translations.literal: Rangzhi's next younger brother Souzhi, styled Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi's next younger brother Souzhi was styled Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 少好儒學，釋褐太學博士。

translations.literal: From youth he loved Confucian learning; upon removing brown he became Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he devoted himself to Confucian studies and upon entering service was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 嘗從常景借書百卷，十許日便返。

translations.literal: Once he borrowed from Chang Jing one hundred scrolls of books; in about ten days he returned them.
translations.idiomatic: He once borrowed a hundred scrolls from Chang Jing and returned them in little more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 景疑其不能讀，每卷策問，應答無遺。

translations.literal: Jing doubted he could not read them; every scroll he tested by questioning; replies were without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Jing doubted he could have read them all and tested him scroll by scroll; Souzhi answered without missing a point.

sentences.zh: 景歎曰：「應奉五行俱下，禰衡一覽便記，今復見之于裴生矣。

translations.literal: Jing sighed and said: "Ying Feng could take five columns at once; Mi Heng would memorise at one glance—now I see this again in Master Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Jing exclaimed, "Ying Feng could read five lines at a glance and Mi Heng could memorize at a single look—today I find the same gift in young Master Pei.

sentences.zh: 」楊愔闔門改葬，托諏之頓作十餘墓誌，文皆可觀。

translations.literal: " When Yang Yin had his entire clan's remains reinterred, he entrusted to Souzhi the rapid composition of more than ten tomb inscriptions; all the texts were worthy of appreciation.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yang Yin reburied his entire family line, he had Souzhi dash off more than a dozen epitaphs at once—all of them fine pieces.

sentences.zh: 讓之、諏之及皇甫和、和弟亮，並知名於洛下。

translations.literal: Rangzhi, Souzhi, and Huangfu He, and He's younger brother Liang, were all renowned below the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi, Souzhi, Huangfu He, and He's younger brother Liang were all celebrated in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「諏勝於讓，和不如亮。

translations.literal: People of the time said: "Sou surpasses Rang; He does not match Liang.
translations.idiomatic: People then said, "Souzhi outshines Rangzhi, but He falls short of Liang.

sentences.zh: 」司空高乾致書曰：「相屈為戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: " Minister of Works Gao Gan sent a letter saying: "I wish to invite you as Household Affairs Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Works Gao Gan wrote inviting him to serve as Household Affairs Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 」諏之復書不受署。

translations.literal: " Souzhi wrote back and did not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " Souzhi replied declining the appointment.

sentences.zh: 沛王開大司馬府，辟為記室。

translations.literal: Prince of Pei Kai opened his Grand Marshal's office and recruited him as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pei Kai, on opening his Grand Marshal's office, recruited him as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴後，諏之留在河南。

translations.literal: After the move to Ye, Souzhi remained in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved to Ye, Souzhi stayed behind in the Henan region.

sentences.zh: 西魏領軍獨孤信入據金墉，以諏之為開府屬，號曰「洛陽遺彥」。

translations.literal: Western Wei supreme commander Dugu Xin entered and held Jinyong; he made Souzhi opening-office staff member, calling him "Luoyang's surviving luminary."
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin of Western Wei took Jinyong Fort, he appointed Souzhi to his staff and hailed him as "Luoyang's surviving brilliant scholar."

sentences.zh: 信敗，諏之居南山，洛州刺史王元軌召為中從事。

translations.literal: When Xin was defeated, Souzhi lived on South Mountain; Inspector of Luozhou Wang Yuangui summoned him as middle staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin's defeat Souzhi went to live on Mount Nan; Wang Yuangui, Inspector of Luozhou, summoned him as a staff aide.

sentences.zh: 西師忽至，尋退，遂隨西師入關。

translations.literal: Western army suddenly arrived, soon withdrew; he then followed the Western army west through the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Western forces suddenly appeared and then withdrew, he followed them west through the passes into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 周文帝以為大行台倉曹郎中。

translations.literal: Zhou Wendi made him Gentleman of the Storage Bureau of the Grand Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Western Zhou appointed him Gentleman of the Storage Bureau on the Grand Directorate staff.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 次讞之，字士平。

translations.literal: Next Yanzhi, styled Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Yanzhi, styled Shiping.

sentences.zh: 七歲便勤學，早知名。

translations.literal: At seven he was already diligent in study; early known for reputation.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he was already a diligent student and gained an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 累遷司徒主簿。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 楊愔每稱歎曰：「河東士族，京官不少，唯此家兄弟，全無鄉音。

translations.literal: Yang Yin often praised in admiration saying: "Among Hedong gentry families, capital officials are not few—but only these brothers of this house entirely lack hometown accent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin often marvelled: "Among Hedong gentry families there are many court officials in the capital, but only the brothers of this household have no trace of regional accent.

sentences.zh: 」讞之雖年少，不妄交遊，唯與隴西辛術、趙郡李繪、頓丘李構、清河崔贍為忘年友。

translations.literal: " Though Yanzhi was young, he did not lightly associate and roam; only with Longxi Xin Shu, Zhao commandery Li Hui, Dunqiu Li Gou, and Qinghe Cui Zhan did he become friends who forget age.
translations.idiomatic: " Though still young, Yanzhi formed no casual friendships; his only intimates, older and younger alike, were Xin Shu of Longxi, Li Hui of Zhao, Li Gou of Dunqiu, and Cui Zhan of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 昭帝梓宮將還鄴，轉儀曹郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhao's coffin was to return to Ye, he transferred to Gentleman of Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhao's coffin was about to be returned to Ye, he was transferred to Gentleman of the Rites Bureau.

sentences.zh: 尤悉歷代故事，儀注、喪禮皆能裁正。

translations.literal: He especially knew past generations' precedents; ritual regulations and mourning rites he could all adjudicate and correct.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in precedents of past dynasties and could adjudicate and correct ritual codes and mourning ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 為許昌太守，客旅過郡，皆出私財供給，人間無所預。

translations.literal: As Administrator of Xuchang, travelers passing through the commandery, all from private wealth he supplied; among the people nothing was imposed on them.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Xuchang he paid from his own purse to supply every traveler passing through the commandery without levying a burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 代下日，為吏人所懷。

translations.literal: When replaced and descended from office, he was cherished by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office the officials and people mourned his departure.

sentences.zh: 仕周，卒伊川太守。

translations.literal: Served Zhou; died as Administrator of Yichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Northern Zhou and died while holding the post of Administrator of Yichuan.

sentences.zh: 次謀之，字士令。

translations.literal: Next Mouzhi, styled Shiling.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Mouzhi, styled Shiling.

sentences.zh: 少有風格，邢邵每云「我裴四」。

translations.literal: From youth had style; Xing Shao often said "my Pei Number Four."
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had distinction; Xing Shao would call him "my Pei Number Four."

sentences.zh: 武成為開府，辟為參軍，掌書記。

translations.literal: Wucheng opened his office; recruited him as Army Aide, in charge of record-keeping.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng opened his office he recruited Mouzhi as Army Aide in charge of records.

sentences.zh: 次訥之，字士言。

translations.literal: Next Nezhi, styled Shiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Nezhi, styled Shiyan.

sentences.zh: 純謹有局量。

translations.literal: Pure and careful, with capacity for measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was honest, cautious, and broad-minded.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為平原公開府墨曹，掌書記，從至并州。

translations.literal: At weak-cap age he was Pingyuan Prince Kai's office Ink Bureau, in charge of record-keeping; followed to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he served on Prince of Pingyuan's staff as head of the records bureau and accompanied the prince to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其母在鄴，忽得心痛，訥之是日不勝思慕，心亦驚痛，乃請急而還。

translations.literal: His mother was at Ye; suddenly had heart-pain; Nezhi that day could not bear longing and thinking, his heart also startled with pain, and so requested urgent leave and returned.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was in Ye. When she was suddenly seized with heart pain, Nezhi that same day was overcome with longing and felt a stabbing ache in his own chest; he obtained emergency leave and hurried home.

sentences.zh: 當時以為孝感。

translations.literal: People of the time took it as filial response to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries regarded this as an act of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 文宣踐阼，幸晉陽。

translations.literal: Wenxuan ascended the throne and visited Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan took the throne he made a tour to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 皇太子監國；

translations.literal: Crown Prince supervised the realm;
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was left to supervise the realm;

sentences.zh: 留訥之與杜台卿並為齋帥，領東宮管記。

translations.literal: Nezhi and Du Taiqing were both retained as fast chiefs, heading Eastern Palace record management.
translations.idiomatic: Nezhi and Du Taiqing were left behind as supervisors of fasting rites, concurrently heading the Eastern Palace record office.

sentences.zh: 轉太子舍人，奏中書舍人事。

translations.literal: Transferred to Crown Prince Attendant; handled Secretariat Drafting Officer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant and discharged the duties of a Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 衛尉杜弼被其家客誣云「有怨言，誹訕時政」。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guard Du Bi was by his household guest falsely accused saying "had resentful words, slandered current government."
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guard Du Bi was denounced by a household servant, who claimed he had spoken resentfully and slandered current affairs.

sentences.zh: 並稱訥之與弼交好，亦知之。

translations.literal: It was also said Nezhi and Bi were good friends and likewise knew.
translations.idiomatic: The accuser also claimed that Nezhi, being close to Bi, knew of it as well.

sentences.zh: 坐免官。

translations.literal: For this he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 卒，天統中追贈平州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; in Tiantong posthumously made Inspector of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Pingzhou during the Tiantong era.

sentences.zh: 長子曰樊，出後讓之。

translations.literal: Eldest son named Fan, went out as heir to Rangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fan was given in adoption as Rangzhi's heir.

sentences.zh: 次子矩，最知名。

translations.literal: Second son Ju, most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Ju became the most famous.

sentences.zh: 矩字弘大，繈褓而孤；

translations.literal: Ju styled Hongda, in swaddling clothes orphaned;
translations.idiomatic: Ju, styled Hongda, was orphaned in infancy;

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，頗愛文藻，有智數。

translations.literal: When grown, loved learning, quite loved literary ornament, had stratagem and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: as he grew he loved learning, took to literary craft, and showed an astute mind.

sentences.zh: 世父讓之謂曰：「觀汝神識，足成才士，欲求宦達，當資幹世之務。

translations.literal: Uncle Rangzhi said to him: "Observing your spirit and insight, enough to become a talented scholar; seeking official success, you should rely on practical worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Rangzhi told him, "From your wit and insight you could easily become a gifted scholar—but if you mean to rise in office you must master the business of governing the world.

sentences.zh: 」矩由是始留情世事。

translations.literal: " Ju from this began to fix attention on worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " From that point Ju began to turn his mind to public affairs.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，為高平王文學。

translations.literal: Served Qi as Literary Adjunct to Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Qi service as Literary Adjunct on the staff of Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，不得調。

translations.literal: Qi perished; could not obtain appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he received no new appointment.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為定州總管，補記室，甚親敬之。

translations.literal: Sui Wendi as Governor-General of Dingzhou supplemented him as Recorder; greatly personally respected him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as Governor-General of Dingzhou he took Ju on as Recorder and treated him with exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for mother left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 及帝作相，遣使馳召之，參相府記室事。

translations.literal: When Emperor became Chancellor, dispatched messenger urgently summoned him; participated in chancellor's office recorder affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor became Chancellor he sent a fast courier to summon Ju, who then served on the chancellor's staff as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 受禪，遷給事郎，奏舍人事。

translations.literal: Received abdication; promoted to Drafting Officer, handled drafting officer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication and founding of Sui he was promoted to Drafting Officer and performed the duties of a Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，領元帥記室。

translations.literal: Chen conquest campaign; headed commander's Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Chen he served as Recorder on the commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 既破丹陽，晉王廣令矩與高熲收陳圖籍。

translations.literal: Having captured Danyang, Prince of Jin Guang ordered Ju and Gao Jiong to collect Chen maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: After Danyang fell, Prince Jin Guang ordered Ju and Gao Jiong to gather Chen's maps and archives.

sentences.zh: 明年，奉詔巡撫嶺南。

translations.literal: Next year, received edict to tour and pacify Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received orders to tour and pacify Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 未行而高智慧、汪文進等作亂，吳、越道閉。

translations.literal: Before departing Gao Zhihui, Wang Wenjin and others rebelled; Wu and Yue routes closed.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could set out, Gao Zhihui, Wang Wenjin, and others rose in rebellion and the routes through Wu and Yue were cut off.

sentences.zh: 上難遣矩行，矩請速進，上許之。

translations.literal: Emperor had difficulty sending Ju; Ju requested to advance quickly; emperor permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated to send Ju into such danger, but Ju asked to press ahead at once and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 行至南康，得兵數千人。

translations.literal: Reaching Nankang, obtained several thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Nankang he mustered several thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 時俚帥王仲宣逼廣州，遣其部將周師舉圖東衡州，矩與大將軍鹿願赴之。

translations.literal: At the time Liao chieftain Wang Zhongxuan pressed Guangzhou, sent his general Zhou Shiju to besiege Eastern Heng commandery; Ju and Great General Lu Yuan went to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao chieftain Wang Zhongxuan was then pressing Guangzhou and sent his general Zhou Shiju to invest Eastern Hengzhou; Ju marched there with General Lu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 賊立九柵，屯大庾嶺，共為聲援。

translations.literal: Bandits set up nine palisades, stationed at Dayu Ridge, together as mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels erected nine palisaded camps on Dayu Ridge to support one another.

sentences.zh: 矩進擊破之。

translations.literal: Ju advanced and broke and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ju attacked and broke them.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，釋東衡州，據原長嶺，又擊敗之。

translations.literal: Bandits feared; released Eastern Heng commandery, held Yuan-Chang Ridge, again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled, abandoning Eastern Hengzhou to hold Yuan-Chang Ridge; Ju defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 遂斬師舉，進軍自南海拔廣州，仲宣懼而潰散。

translations.literal: Thereupon beheaded Shiju, advanced army from Nanhai captured Guangzhou; Zhongxuan feared and dispersed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: He then beheaded Shiju, advanced from Nanhai to take Guangzhou, and Zhongxuan's forces collapsed in terror.

sentences.zh: 矩所綏集者二十餘州，又承制署渠帥為刺史縣令。

translations.literal: Ju's pacified and gathered were more than twenty prefectures; also by imperial mandate appointed chieftains as inspectors and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Ju brought more than twenty prefectures back under control and, by imperial authorization, appointed tribal chieftains as regional inspectors and county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 及還，上大悅，命升殿勞苦之，謂高熲、楊素曰：「韋洸將二萬兵，不能早度嶺，每患其兵少。

translations.literal: When he returned, emperor greatly pleased, ordered him ascend hall and labor-counsel him, said to Gao Jiong and Yang Su: "Wei Guang led twenty thousand troops, could not early cross the range, always worried his troops too few.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor was elated, had him ascend the hall to be personally commended, and said to Gao Jiong and Yang Su, "Wei Guang led twenty thousand men and still could not cross the mountains in time—we always feared he had too few troops.

sentences.zh: 裴矩以三千弊卒徑至南海，有臣若此，朕亦何憂。

translations.literal: Pei Ju with three thousand worn-out soldiers directly reached Nanhai; having minister like this, I also what worry.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju marched straight to Nanhai with three thousand ragged troops—with a minister like this, what have I to fear?

sentences.zh: 」以功拜開府，賜爵聞喜縣公，賚物二千段。

translations.literal: " For merit enfeoffed Opening Office, granted title Duke of Wenxi County, bestowed goods two thousand lengths.
translations.idiomatic: " For his service he was appointed Opening Grand Master, enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County, and granted two thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 除戶部侍郎，遷內吏侍郎。

translations.literal: Appointed Vice Minister of the Household, promoted Vice Minister of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and then promoted to Vice Minister of the Interior.

sentences.zh: 時西域諸蕃多至張掖與中國交市，帝令矩掌其事。

translations.literal: At the time Western Regions various tribes mostly came to Zhangye to trade with China; emperor ordered Ju manage this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Many peoples of the Western Regions then came to Zhangye to trade with China, and the emperor put Ju in charge of the market.

sentences.zh: 矩知帝方勤遠略，諸胡至者，矩誘令言其國俗山川險易，撰西域圖記三卷，入朝奏之。

translations.literal: Ju knew emperor was then diligently pursuing distant strategy; various Hu who arrived, Ju induced them to speak of their countries' customs, mountains and rivers, dangers and eases; compiled Western Regions Illustrated Record three scrolls; entered court and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor was keen on expanding the frontier, Ju questioned every arriving foreigner about his homeland's customs and terrain and compiled a three-scroll Western Regions Illustrated Record, which he presented at court.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：

translations.literal: Its preface says:
translations.idiomatic: The preface reads:

sentences.zh: 臣聞禹定九州，導河不逾積石。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard Yu fixed the Nine Provinces; guiding the river did not cross beyond Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: I have read that Yu divided the land into Nine Provinces and that the Yellow River he channeled did not extend beyond Mount Jishi.

sentences.zh: 秦兼六國，設防止於臨洮。

translations.literal: Qin annexed the Six States, set a defensive barrier at Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin conquered the Six States it erected a barrier at Lintao.

sentences.zh: 故知西胡雜種，僻居遐裔，禮教之所不及，書典之所罕傳。

translations.literal: Hence one knows Western Hu mixed breeds, dwelling remote in distant borderlands—where ritual teaching does not reach, where written classics rarely transmit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the mixed peoples of the western barbarian lands dwelt far on the frontier, beyond the reach of ritual culture and barely mentioned in the written record.

sentences.zh: 自漢氏興基，開拓河右，始稱名號者有四十六國。

translations.literal: From Han's rise and foundation, opening and expanding the right bank of the river, those first claiming names and titles numbered forty-six states.
translations.idiomatic: From the rise of the Han dynasty, which opened the Hexi corridor, forty-six states first came to be named in the records.

sentences.zh: 其後分立，乃五十五王。

translations.literal: Afterwards they divided and stood apart, then fifty-five kings.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as they split apart, there were fifty-five rulers.

sentences.zh: 仍置校尉、都護，以存招撫。

translations.literal: Still set Colonel Protector and Chief Commandant to preserve recruitment and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: The Han also established Protector-Colonels and Chief Commandants to maintain contact and offer reassurance.

sentences.zh: 然叛服不恆，屢經征戰。

translations.literal: Yet rebellion and submission were not constant; repeatedly passed through campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Yet submission and rebellion were never constant, and the region saw repeated campaigns.

sentences.zh: 後漢之世，頻廢此官；

translations.literal: In Later Han's age, frequently abolished these offices;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Han these posts were repeatedly abolished;

sentences.zh: 雖大宛以來，略知戶數，而諸國山川，未有名目。

translations.literal: Although from Dayuan onward, roughly knew household numbers, yet various states' mountains and rivers had no names and entries.
translations.idiomatic: and although since Dayuan there had been rough tallies of population, the mountains and rivers of the various states went unnamed in the books.

sentences.zh: 至如姓氏、風土、服章、物產，全無纂錄，世所弗聞。

translations.literal: As for surnames, customs and soil, dress and insignia, products of the land—entirely none compiled and recorded; the age had never heard of them.
translations.idiomatic: As for family names, customs, dress, and local products, nothing had been systematically compiled; the world knew nothing of them.

sentences.zh: 復以春秋遞謝，年代久遠，兼併誅討，互有興亡。

translations.literal: Moreover because seasons and years passed in succession, ages long and distant, annexation and punitive extermination—in turn had rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as dynasties succeeded one another and centuries passed, conquest and punitive war brought one state after another to rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 或地是故邦，改從今號；

translations.literal: Sometimes the land was an old state but adopted a new title;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes an old land survived but took a new name;

sentences.zh: 或人非舊類，同襲昔名。

translations.literal: Sometimes people were not the old kind yet bore the same ancient name.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes a new people borrowed an ancient name.

sentences.zh: 兼復部人交錯，封疆移改，戎狄音殊，事難窮驗。

translations.literal: Moreover again clans and peoples intermixed, borders and frontiers shifted and changed; barbarian sounds differed—the matter was hard to exhaustively verify.
translations.idiomatic: Populations shifted, borders changed, and the tongues of the frontier peoples diverged—making truth difficult to establish.

sentences.zh: 于闐之北，蔥嶺以東，考于前史，三十餘國。

translations.literal: North of Khotan, east of Onion Mountains, examining former histories—more than thirty states.
translations.idiomatic: North of Khotan and east of the Pamirs, the earlier histories mention more than thirty states.

sentences.zh: 其後更相屠滅，僅有十存，自餘淪沒，掃地俱盡，空有丘墟，不可記識。

translations.literal: Afterwards they in turn slaughtered and extinguished one another; only ten survived; the rest sunk and perished, swept clean altogether—only empty mounds and ruins remain, impossible to record and identify.
translations.idiomatic: Later they slaughtered one another until only ten survived; the rest were wiped from the earth, leaving nothing but ruins impossible to identify.

sentences.zh: 皇上應天育物，無隔華夷；

translations.literal: Your Majesty responds to Heaven and nurtures beings; without barrier between Chinese and barbarian;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, responding to Heaven and nurturing all creation, makes no distinction between Chinese and foreign;

sentences.zh: 率土黔黎，莫不慕化。

translations.literal: Throughout the land common folk, none do not admire and be transformed.
translations.idiomatic: and throughout the realm the people look to you for civilization.

sentences.zh: 風行所及，日入以來，職貢皆通，無遠不至。

translations.literal: Where wind teaching reaches, from where the sun sets inward, tribute duties all connect; none so distant they do not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Where your influence reaches, from the lands of the sunset inward, tribute missions come from every quarter, however far.

sentences.zh: 臣既因撫納，監知關市，尋討書籍，訪采胡人。

translations.literal: Your servant has because of pacification and acceptance overseen and known the barrier markets, searched through books and records, inquired and gathered from Hu people.
translations.idiomatic: In overseeing the border markets and receiving these peoples, I have searched the books and questioned the foreigners firsthand.

sentences.zh: 或有所疑，即詳眾口，依其本國服飾儀形，王及庶人各顯容止，即丹青摸寫為《西圖域記》，共成三卷，合三十五國。

translations.literal: When there was something doubtful, then in detail questioned all mouths; according to each state's native dress and ceremonial forms, kings and commoners each displayed bearing and deportment; then with cinnabar and green traced and copied into the Western Regions Illustrated Record, altogether completing three scrolls, together thirty-five states.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever doubt remained, I questioned everyone in detail; according to each country's native dress and ceremonial bearing, I had kings and commoners alike show their appearance and deportment, then painted them for the Western Regions Illustrated Record—a work of three scrolls covering thirty-five states.

sentences.zh: 仍別造地圖，窮其要害，從西頃以去，北海之南，縱橫所互，將二萬里。

translations.literal: Still separately made maps, exhausted their strategic points; from where the sun sets westward to south of the North Sea, vertically and horizontally mutually crossing—nearly twenty thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: I also drew separate maps mapping every strategic point; from the western horizon to south of the North Sea, the area covered runs to nearly twenty thousand li in every direction.

sentences.zh: 諒由富商大賈，周遊經涉，故諸國之事，罔不偏知。

translations.literal: Surely because wealthy merchants and great traders circulated and passed through all routes, hence affairs of various states—none not entirely known.
translations.idiomatic: This is surely because the great merchants who travel the routes have passed through everywhere, so that nothing of these countries escapes notice.

sentences.zh: 復有幽荒遠地，卒訪難曉，不可憑虛，是以致闕。

translations.literal: Moreover there were dark wilderness distant lands; sudden inquiry hard to understand; impossible to fabricate from emptiness—therefore omissions resulted.
translations.idiomatic: Some lands remain remote and obscure; sudden inquiry cannot make them clear, and one cannot invent what is not known—hence the gaps in the record.

sentences.zh: 而二漢相踵，西域為傳，戶人數十，即稱國王，徒有名號，有乖其實。

translations.literal: Yet two Han dynasties followed in succession; Western Regions served as biographical records—households and people numbering tens then called kings; only empty names and titles, departing from reality.
translations.idiomatic: Under the two Han dynasties, the Western Regions appear in the histories—but states with only dozens of households were called kings in name only, far from the truth.

sentences.zh: 今者所編，皆餘千戶，利盡西海，多產珍異。

translations.literal: What is compiled now—all have surplus of a thousand households; profit extends to the Western Sea; many produce rare and strange things.
translations.idiomatic: Those included in the present compilation all have more than a thousand households, trade reaches the Western Sea, and they produce many rare goods.

sentences.zh: 見山居之屬，非有國名及部落小者，多亦不載。

translations.literal: As for mountain-dwelling types, those without state names and small tribes—mostly also not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain dwellers without state names, and petty tribes, are for the most part omitted.

sentences.zh: 發自燉煌，至於西海，凡為三道，各有襟帶。

translations.literal: Starting from Dunhuang, reaching the Western Sea—in all three routes, each having connecting links like collar and belt.
translations.idiomatic: From Dunhuang to the Western Sea there are three main routes, each with its chain of stations and dependencies.

sentences.zh: 北道從伊吾經蒲類海、鐵勒部、突厥可汗庭，度北流河水、至拂菻國，達於西海。

translations.literal: Northern route from Yiwu via Pulei Sea, Tiele tribes, Türk qaghan court; crossed north-flowing river water; reached Fulin state; arrived at Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The northern route runs from Yiwu through the Pulei Sea, the Tiele tribes, and the Türk qaghan's court, crosses the north-flowing river, reaches Fulin (Byzantium), and arrives at the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 其中道從高昌、焉耆、龜茲、疏勒，度蔥嶺，又經吲汗、蘇勒沙那國、康國、曹國、何國、大小安國、穆國，至波斯，達於西海。

translations.literal: The central route from Gaochang, Yanqi, Kucha, Kashgar; crossed Onion Mountains; again passed Yehana, Sule shana state, Kang state, Cao state, He state, Greater and Lesser An states, Mu state; reached Persia; arrived at Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The central route goes from Gaochang through Yanqi, Kucha, and Kashgar, crosses the Pamirs, then passes Yehana, Sule shana, Kang, Cao, He, Greater and Lesser An, and Mu, and reaches Persia and the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 其南道從鄯善、于闐、硃俱波、喝盤陀，度蔥嶺，又經護密、吐火羅、挹騑、忛延、漕國，至北婆羅門，達於西海。

translations.literal: The southern route from Shanshan, Khotan, Zhujubo, Hepantuo; crossed Onion Mountains; again passed Wumi, Tuhuoluo, Yipi, Ganyan, Cao state; reached North Brahman; arrived at Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The southern route runs from Shanshan through Khotan, Zhujubo, and Hepantuo, crosses the Pamirs, then passes Wumi, Tuhuoluo, Yipi, Ganyan, and Cao, and reaches North Brahman and the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 其三道諸國，亦各自有路，南北交通。

translations.literal: These three routes' various states also each have their own roads; north and south connect in traffic.
translations.idiomatic: The states along these three routes also have their own byways, linking north and south.

sentences.zh: 其東安國、南婆羅門國等，並隨其所往，諸處得達。

translations.literal: As for Eastern An state, South Brahman state, and the like—all follow where one goes; every place can be reached.
translations.idiomatic: States such as Eastern An and South Brahman can likewise be reached by whichever route one takes.

sentences.zh: 故知伊吾、高昌、鄯善並西域之門戶也，總湊燉煌，是其咽喉之地。

translations.literal: Hence one knows Yiwu, Gaochang, and Shanshan are all gateways of the Western Regions; all converge at Dunhuang—this is the throat-and-gullet place.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yiwu, Gaochang, and Shanshan are the gateways to the Western Regions, and all traffic converges on Dunhuang—the strategic choke point of the route.

sentences.zh: 以國家威德，將士驍雄，泛濛汜而揚旌，越昆侖而躍馬，易如反掌，何往不至。

translations.literal: By the state's majesty and virtue, generals and soldiers fierce and heroic—sailing the western waters to raise banners, leaping horses over Kunlun—as easy as turning the palm; what place would not be reached.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire's majesty and the valor of its troops, to sail the western seas and raise our banners, to gallop over the Kunlun—would be as easy as turning one's hand; no destination would lie beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 但突厥、吐谷渾分領羌胡之國，為其擁遏，故朝貢不通。

translations.literal: Only Türks and Tuyuhun separately held Qiang and Hu states, blocking them on their behalf—hence tribute missions did not connect.
translations.idiomatic: But the Türks and Tuyuhun controlled the Qiang and Hu states and blocked the routes, so tribute missions could not get through.

sentences.zh: 今並因商人，密送誠款，引領翹首，願為臣妾。

translations.literal: Now all through merchants secretly send sincere pledges; craning necks and raising heads, they wish to become subjects and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Now, through merchants, they secretly send pledges of loyalty; they stretch their necks in hope and wish to become your subjects.

sentences.zh: 聖情含養，澤及普天，服而撫之，務在安輯。

translations.literal: Sagely feeling embraces and nurtures; grace reaches all under Heaven; subdue and comfort them—the task lies in pacification and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's grace embraces all creation and extends to every corner of the sky; to win them over and put them at ease is the true aim.

sentences.zh: 故皇華遣使，弗動兵車，諸蕃既從，突厥可滅。

translations.literal: Therefore imperial envoys are dispatched; no need to move chariots and troops; once the various barbarians follow, the Türks can be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Send imperial envoys rather than armies; once the frontier peoples submit, the Türks can be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 混一戎夏，其在茲乎。

translations.literal: Uniting barbarian and Chinese—perhaps it lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The unification of Chinese and foreign lands may well begin here.

sentences.zh: 不有所記，無以表威化之遠也。

translations.literal: Without some record, there is no means to display the reach of majestic transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Without recording these matters, there is no way to show how far your civilizing power extends.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜物五百段，每日引矩至御坐，親問西方之事。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed five hundred bolts of goods; daily summoned Ju to the imperial seat and personally inquired about Western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, granted him five hundred bolts of silk, and each day summoned Ju to the imperial seat to question him personally about the West.

sentences.zh: 矩盛言胡中多諸寶物，吐谷渾易可併吞。

translations.literal: Ju greatly spoke that among the Hu there were many treasures and goods; Tuyuhun could easily be swallowed and annexed.
translations.idiomatic: Ju spoke at length of the riches of the western lands and argued that Tuyuhun could easily be conquered and absorbed.

sentences.zh: 帝由是甘心，將通西域，西夷經略，咸以委之。

translations.literal: The emperor from this set his heart on it; about to open the Western Regions; western barbarian strategy—all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up: he would open the Western Regions and entrusted Ju with the entire western frontier strategy.

sentences.zh: 後遷黃門侍郎，復令往張掖，引致西蕃，至者十餘國。

translations.literal: Later transferred to Yellow Gate Attendant; again ordered to go to Zhangye, to lead and summon western barbarians—those who arrived numbered more than ten states.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Yellow Gate Attendant and again sent to Zhangye to summon the western peoples; more than ten states responded.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，帝有事于恆嶽，咸來助祭。

translations.literal: Daye third year, the emperor had business at Mount Heng; all came to assist at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye, when the emperor performed rites at Mount Heng, they all came to assist at the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 帝將巡河右，復令矩往敦煌，矩遣使說高昌王麹伯雅及伊吾吐屯設等，啖以厚利，導之使入朝。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to tour the right bank of the river; again ordered Ju to go to Dunhuang; Ju dispatched envoys to persuade King Qu Boya of Gaochang and Yiwu Tudu she and the like, enticing them with great profit, guiding them to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to tour the Hexi region, he again sent Ju to Dunhuang. Ju dispatched envoys to King Qu Boya of Gaochang, the Yiwu Tudu she, and others, tempting them with rich rewards and guiding them to court.

sentences.zh: 及帝西巡，次燕支山。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured west, he halted at Mount Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured west, he halted at Mount Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 高昌王、伊吾設等及西蕃胡二十七國謁于道左，皆令佩金玉，被錦罽，焚香奏樂，歌舞喧噪。

translations.literal: King of Gaochang, Yiwu she, and the like, and twenty-seven states of western barbarian Hu, paid homage at the left of the road—all ordered to wear jade and gold, draped in brocade and felt, burning incense and performing music, singing and dancing with clamorous noise.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Gaochang, the Yiwu she, and envoys from twenty-seven western states waited by the roadside to pay homage, all adorned with jade and gold, draped in brocade and felt, burning incense and playing music amid singing and dancing.

sentences.zh: 復令張掖、武威士女盛飾縱觀，填咽周互數十里，以示中國之盛。

translations.literal: Again ordered Zhangye and Wuwei scholars' and commoners' daughters in full adornment to watch freely; filling and choking for several tens of li all around—to display China's splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the daughters of scholars and commoners of Zhangye and Wuwei dress in their finest and line the route for miles on end, to display the splendor of the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 帝見而大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor saw it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased at the sight.

sentences.zh: 竟破吐谷渾，拓地數千里。

translations.literal: In the end broke Tuyuhun, expanded territory by several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun was at last defeated and territory was expanded by several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 並遣兵戍之，每歲委輸巨億萬計。

translations.literal: Also dispatched troops to garrison them; every year tribute and transport totaled tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were garrisoned there as well, and every year the cost of supplies ran to tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃懼懾，朝貢相續。

translations.literal: Various barbarians feared and submitted; tribute missions followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples submitted in fear, and tribute missions came one after another.

sentences.zh: 帝謂矩有綏懷略，進位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor said Ju had pacification and cherishing strategy; advanced in rank to Silver Seal Blue-Gleaming Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Ju had a gift for winning hearts, and promoted him to Silver Seal Blue-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，帝至東都。

translations.literal: That year in winter, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 矩以蠻夷朝貢者多，諷帝令都下大戲，征四方奇伎異藝陳於端門街，衣錦綺、珥金翠者以十萬數。

translations.literal: Ju because barbarian tribute missions were many, indirectly advised the emperor to hold a great festival in the capital, summoning strange skills and exotic arts from the four directions to display at Duanmen Street—those wearing brocade and silk, dangling gold and kingfisher, numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Because so many barbarian envoys were presenting tribute, Ju suggested that the emperor hold a great festival in the capital, summoning exotic performers from every quarter to display their arts on Duanmen Street—those dressed in brocade and silk with gold and kingfisher ornaments numbered in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又勒百官及百姓士女列坐棚閣而縱觀焉，皆被服鮮麗，終月而罷。

translations.literal: Also ordered officials of every rank and commoners, scholars and women, to sit in rows in booths and galleries and watch freely—all clothed in fresh splendor; ended after a full month.
translations.idiomatic: He also had officials and commoners, men and women, seated in tiers of booths and galleries to watch; all were splendidly dressed, and the spectacle lasted a full month.

sentences.zh: 又令交市店肆皆設帷帳，盛酒食，遣掌蕃率蠻夷與人貿易，所至處悉令邀延就坐，醉飽而散。

translations.literal: Also ordered market shops at trading posts all to set up curtains and tents, abundantly providing wine and food; dispatched overseers of barbarians to lead barbarians in trade with people; every place reached was all ordered to invite and extend, urging them to sit—drunk and full then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Market stalls were draped with canopies and stocked with food and wine; officials in charge of foreign guests led the barbarians to trade with the townspeople, inviting them everywhere to sit, eat, and drink their fill before they departed.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷嗟歎，謂中國為神仙。

translations.literal: Barbarians sighed in admiration, saying China was the land of immortals.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians marveled and declared that the Middle Kingdom was the realm of immortals.

sentences.zh: 帝稱矩至誠，謂宇文述、牛弘曰：「裴矩凡所陳奏，皆朕之成算，朕未發，矩輒以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Ju's utmost sincerity and said to Yuwen Shu and Niu Hong: "Pei Ju in all he memorializes—all are my settled plans; I have not yet spoken, and Ju already reports them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Ju's devotion and said to Yuwen Shu and Niu Hong, "Everything Pei Ju submits in memorial is already my own settled plan—before I have even spoken, Ju has already reported it.

sentences.zh: 自非奉國，孰能若是。」

translations.literal: " Unless serving the state, who could be like this?"
translations.idiomatic: " Who but a man wholly devoted to the state could do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 帝遣將軍薛世雄城伊吾，令矩共往經略。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched General Xue Shixiong to fortify Yiwu, ordering Ju to go together to conduct strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent General Xue Shixiong to build a fortress at Yiwu and ordered Ju to accompany him and oversee the operation.

sentences.zh: 矩諷諭西域諸國曰：「天子為蕃人交易懸遠，所以城耳。

translations.literal: Ju indirectly instructed the various states of the Western Regions, saying: "The Son of Heaven because barbarian people's trade is distant and suspended—that is why he fortifies.
translations.idiomatic: Ju persuaded the western states, saying, "The Son of Heaven is building this fortress only because trade with the frontier peoples is so far-flung.

sentences.zh: 」咸以為然，不復來競。

translations.literal: " All thought it so; no longer came to compete.
translations.idiomatic: " They all accepted this explanation and ceased to contest the project.

sentences.zh: 及還，賜錢四十萬。

translations.literal: When he returned, bestowed forty thousand coins.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was granted forty thousand coins.

sentences.zh: 矩又白狀，令反間射匱，潛攻處羅。

translations.literal: Ju again reported in person, ordering stratagem to divide Shekui, secretly attacking Chuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Ju also submitted a plan to set Shekui and Chuluo against each other through intrigue.

sentences.zh: 後處羅為射匱所迫，竟隨使者入朝。

translations.literal: Later Chuluo was pressed by Shekui; in the end followed the envoy to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chuluo, hard pressed by Shekui, finally came to court with the envoy.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜矩貂裘及西域珍器。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed on Ju sable fur coat and Western Regions rare vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and granted Ju a sable-fur coat and rare treasures from the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 從帝巡塞北，幸啟人帳。

translations.literal: Followed the emperor touring the northern frontier, visiting Qiren's tent.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on a tour of the northern frontier and visited Qiren Khan's camp.

sentences.zh: 時高麗遣使先通於突厥，啟人不敢隱，引之見帝。

translations.literal: At the time Goryeo dispatched envoys first to connect with the Türks; Qiren did not dare conceal it, led them to see the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Goryeo had sent envoys to establish contact with the Türks; Qiren did not dare hide it and brought them before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 矩因奏曰：「高麗地本孤竹國，周代以之封箕子，漢世分為三郡，晉氏亦統遼東。

translations.literal: Ju thereupon memorialized saying: "Goryeo's land was originally the state of Guzhu; in Zhou times it was enfeoffed to Jizi; in Han times divided into three commanderies; Jin also ruled Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Ju thereupon memorialized: "The land of Goryeo was originally the state of Guzhu; in the Zhou it was enfeoffed to Jizi; in the Han it was divided into three commanderies; the Jin too held Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 今乃不臣，列為外域，故先帝欲征之久矣。

translations.literal: Now yet not subject, ranked as outer domain—hence the former emperor long wished to campaign against it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now it refuses submission and is treated as a foreign land—so the former emperor long wished to campaign against it.

sentences.zh: 但以楊諒不肖，師出無功。

translations.literal: But because Yang Liang was unworthy, the army went out without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: But because Yang Liang proved unworthy, the expedition came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 當陛下時，安得不事，使此冠帶之境仍為蠻貊之鄉乎？

translations.literal: At Your Majesty's time, how can one not act—allow this girdled-and-capped territory still to be barbarian lands?
translations.idiomatic: In Your Majesty's reign, how can we fail to act and leave this land that once wore the cap and belt still a barbarian frontier?

sentences.zh: 今其使朝於突厥，親見啟人合國從化，必懼皇靈之遠暢，慮後服之先亡，脅令入朝，當可致也。

translations.literal: Now its envoy pays court at the Türks; personally sees Qiren's whole state follow transformation—surely will fear the imperial numen reaching far and flowing; worry later submission will perish first; coerced to order entry at court—can be brought about.
translations.idiomatic: Now its envoy has come to the Türks and seen Qiren's entire people submit to your rule; he will surely fear that your imperial majesty reaches so far and that Goryeo will be the first to perish if it submits late. If we pressure him to return and bid his king come to court at once, we can bring this about.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「如何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "How?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "How?

sentences.zh: 」矩曰：「請面詔其使，放還本國，遣語其王，令速朝覲。

translations.literal: " Ju said: "I request to face and decree their envoy, release and return to his native state, send word to his king, ordering swift court audience.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju replied, "Let me speak to the envoy face to face, send him home, and tell his king to come to court at once.

sentences.zh: 不然者，當率突厥，即日誅之。

translations.literal: If not, then will lead the Türks—same day execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise tell him that the Türks will destroy Goryeo that very day.

sentences.zh: 」帝納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 高元不用命，始建征遼之策。

translations.literal: Gao Yuan did not obey the command; then first established the strategy to campaign against Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When King Gao Yuan disobeyed, the plan to campaign against Liaodong was first drawn up.

sentences.zh: 王師臨遼，以本官領武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Imperial army approached Liaodong; with his original office held post of Brave Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army reached Liaodong, he served in his existing post as Brave Guard General.

sentences.zh: 明年，復從至遼東。

translations.literal: Next year, again followed to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again accompanied the campaign to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎斛斯政亡入高麗，帝令矩兼掌兵事。

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs Vice Director Husizheng fled and entered Goryeo; the emperor ordered Ju concurrently to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Husizheng defected to Goryeo; the emperor ordered Ju to take charge of military affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 以前後度遼功，進位右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because of earlier and later merit crossing Liaodong, advanced in rank to Right Blue-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: For his repeated service in the Liaodong campaigns he was promoted to Right Blue-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 時皇綱不振，人皆變節，左翊衛大將軍宇文述、內史侍郎虞世基等用事，文武多以賄聞。

translations.literal: At the time imperial discipline was not restored; people all changed their integrity; Left Wing Guard Grand General Yuwen Shu, Palace Secretariat Vice Director Yu Shiji, and the like held power; civil and military mostly became known through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time imperial authority was failing; men everywhere abandoned principle; Yuwen Shu, Left Wing Guard Grand General, and Yu Shiji, Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, and others held power, and officials civil and military were widely known for taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 唯矩守常，無贓穢之響，以是為世所稱。

translations.literal: Only Ju maintained constancy; no sound of corruption and filth—therefore was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Ju alone held to his ways and was never tainted by corruption, for which the world praised him.

sentences.zh: 後以楊玄感初平，帝令矩安集隴右，因之會寧，存問曷薩那部落，遣闕達度設寇吐谷渾，頻有虜獲，部落致富。

translations.literal: Later because Yang Xuangan was first pacified, the emperor ordered Ju to pacify and settle Longyou; because of this met at Huining, inquired after the Hesana tribe, dispatched Quetadu she to raid Tuyuhun—frequently had captive gains; the tribe grew wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Xuangan's rebellion was first suppressed, the emperor sent Ju to pacify Longyou. At Huining he received the Hesana tribe, sent the Quetadu she to raid Tuyuhun, and won repeated spoils that enriched the tribe.

sentences.zh: 還而奏狀，帝大賞之。

translations.literal: On return memorialized the situation; the emperor greatly rewarded it.
translations.idiomatic: He reported back on his return, and the emperor richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 後從至懷遠鎮，詔護北蕃軍事。

translations.literal: Later followed to Huaiyuan garrison; edict to oversee northern barbarian military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later accompanied the emperor to Huaiyuan garrison and was ordered to oversee military affairs on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 矩以始畢可汗部眾漸盛，獻策分其勢。

translations.literal: Ju because Shibi qaghan's clans and masses gradually grew strong, presented strategy to divide his power.
translations.idiomatic: Ju saw that Qaghan Shibi's following was growing strong and proposed a plan to divide his power.

sentences.zh: 將以宗女嫁其弟叱吉設，拜為南面可汗。

translations.literal: About to marry a clan daughter to his younger brother Chiji she, appoint him Southern Face Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed marrying an imperial clanswoman to Shibi's younger brother Chiji she and appointing him Southern Face Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 叱吉不敢受，始畢聞而漸怨。

translations.literal: Chiji did not dare accept; Shibi heard and gradually resented.
translations.idiomatic: Chiji did not dare accept; when Shibi heard of it, resentment grew between them.

sentences.zh: 矩又曰：「突厥本淳，易可離間，由其內多有眾胡，盡皆桀黠，教導之耳。

translations.literal: Ju also said: "Türks by nature are simple; easily can be divided; because within them there are many various Hu—all are fierce and cunning; it is they who teach and guide this.
translations.idiomatic: Ju also said, "The Türks are by nature straightforward and can easily be set against one another; within their ranks there are many Hu, all of them crafty, and it is they who stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 臣聞史蜀胡悉尤多奸計，幸于始畢，請誘殺之。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard Shishu Husi especially has many treacherous stratagems, favored by Shibi—please lure and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Hu chieftain Shishu Husi is especially full of treacherous schemes and enjoys Shibi's favor—I ask permission to lure and kill him.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Good.

sentences.zh: 」矩因遣人告胡悉曰：「天子大出珍物，今在馬邑，欲共蕃內多作交關，若前來者，即得好物。

translations.literal: " Ju thereupon dispatched men to tell Husi: "The Son of Heaven greatly brings out rare objects; now at Mayi; wishes together with many within the barbarian lands to make much trade; if you come forward, then will obtain good things.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju then sent word to Husi: "The Son of Heaven has brought out great stores of treasure at Mayi and wishes to trade freely with the frontier peoples; if you come first, you will get the best goods.

sentences.zh: 」胡悉信之，不告始畢，率其部落，盡驅六畜爭進，冀先互市。

translations.literal: " Husi believed it; did not tell Shibi; led his tribe, driving all six livestock competing to advance—hoped first to mutually market.
translations.idiomatic: " Husi believed him, told Shibi nothing, and drove all his herds at full speed toward Mayi, hoping to trade before anyone else.

sentences.zh: 矩伏兵馬邑，誘而斬之。

translations.literal: Ju ambushed troops at Mayi, lured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ju lay in ambush at Mayi, lured Husi in, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 詔報始畢曰：「史蜀胡悉忽領部落，走來至此，雲背可汗，請我容納。

translations.literal: Edict reported to Shibi saying: "Shishu Husi suddenly led his tribe, ran away and came here, saying he turned against the qaghan, requesting our acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was sent to Shibi: "Shishu Husi suddenly led his tribe here, saying he had turned against the qaghan and asking us to receive him.

sentences.zh: 今已斬之，故令往報。

translations.literal: Now already beheaded him—therefore order to go report.
translations.idiomatic: We have now executed him and send this report.

sentences.zh: 」始畢亦知其狀，由是不朝。

translations.literal: " Shibi also knew the situation; from this did not come to court.
translations.idiomatic: " Shibi understood what had happened and from that time ceased coming to court.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝北巡狩，始畢率騎數十萬圍帝於雁門，詔矩與虞世基宿朝堂以待顧問。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, the emperor northward toured the hunt; Shibi led cavalry of several hundred thousand and surrounded the emperor at Yanmen; edict Ju and Yu Shiji to lodge in the court hall awaiting consultation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, during the emperor's northern hunt, Shibi led several hundred thousand horsemen and surrounded the emperor at Yanmen; Ju and Yu Shiji were ordered to remain in the court hall for consultation.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，從至東都。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, followed to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege was lifted, Ju accompanied the emperor to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 屬射匱可汗遣其猶子率西蕃諸胡朝貢，詔矩宴接之。

translations.literal: Just then Shekui qaghan dispatched his nephew's son to lead western barbarian various Hu in tribute; edict Ju to feast and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: About that time Qaghan Shekui sent his nephew's son to lead western Hu peoples in tribute, and Ju was ordered to feast and receive them.

sentences.zh: 尋從幸江都宮。

translations.literal: Soon followed in visiting Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the emperor to Jiangdu Palace.

sentences.zh: 時四方盜賊蜂起，郡縣上奏者不可勝計。

translations.literal: At the time bandits and robbers in the four directions swarmed up; commanderies and counties reporting upward could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere, and reports of unrest from the commanderies and counties became too numerous to count.

sentences.zh: 矩言之，帝怒，遣矩詣京師接蕃客。

translations.literal: Ju spoke of them; the emperor was angry, dispatched Ju to go to the capital to receive barbarian guests.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju spoke of this, the emperor grew angry and sent him to the capital to receive foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 以疾不行。

translations.literal: Because of illness did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 及義兵入關，帝遣虞世基就宅問矩方略。

translations.literal: When righteous troops entered the passes, the emperor dispatched Yu Shiji to his residence to ask Ju's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel armies entered the passes, the emperor sent Yu Shiji to Ju's home to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「太原有變，京畿不靜，遙為處分，恐失事機，唯願鑾輿早還。

translations.literal: Ju said: "Taiyuan has change; capital region not quiet; remotely making disposition—fear losing the opportunity; only wish the imperial carriage early return.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "There is trouble at Taiyuan and the capital region is unsettled; to manage affairs from afar will miss the moment—I pray only that Your Majesty return north at once.

sentences.zh: 」俄而驍衛大將軍屈突通敗問至，矩以聞，帝失色。

translations.literal: " Soon Brave Guard Grand General Qu Tu Tong's defeat report arrived; Ju reported it to the emperor; the emperor changed color.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon came word that Brave Guard Grand General Qu Tutong had been defeated; Ju reported it, and the emperor turned pale.

sentences.zh: 矩素勤謹，未嘗忤物，又見天下方亂，恐為身禍，其待遇人，多過其所望，故雖廝役，皆得其歎心。

translations.literal: Ju by nature was diligent and careful, never once offended others; also seeing the realm was just in disorder, feared becoming personal disaster; in treating people, mostly exceeded what they hoped—therefore even menials all obtained their sighing hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was by nature diligent and careful and never gave offence; seeing the empire falling into chaos, he feared for his own safety and treated everyone better than they expected, so that even servants spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 時從駕驍果數有逃散。

translations.literal: At the time those following the imperial carriage—the brave guards—several times had desertions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many of the elite guards accompanying the emperor had begun to desert.

sentences.zh: 帝憂之，以問矩。

translations.literal: The emperor worried about it, and asked Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled by this and asked Ju's advice.

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「今車駕留此，已經二年。

translations.literal: Ju said: "Now the imperial carriage stays here—already two years.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "Your Majesty has kept the court here at Jiangdu for two years already.

sentences.zh: 驍果之徒，盡無家口，人無匹合，則不能久安。

translations.literal: The brave guards—none have family mouths; people without pairing cannot long be settled.
translations.idiomatic: These guards have left their families behind; men without wives cannot be kept content for long.

sentences.zh: 臣請聽兵士于此納室。

translations.literal: Your servant requests permission to let soldiers here take wives.
translations.idiomatic: I ask permission to let the soldiers marry here.

sentences.zh: 」帝大書曰：「公定多智，此奇計也。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly praised saying: "Sir surely has much wisdom—this is a marvelous stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor exclaimed, "You are full of wisdom—this is a brilliant plan.

sentences.zh: 」因令矩檢校為將士等娶妻。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ordered Ju to inspect and verify taking wives for generals, soldiers, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Ju to organize marriages for the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 矩召江都境內寡婦及未嫁女皆集宮監。

translations.literal: Ju summoned within Jiangdu territory widows and unmarried girls—all gathered at the palace overseer's office.
translations.idiomatic: Ju summoned every widow and unmarried woman in Jiangdu to assemble at the palace superintendent's quarters.

sentences.zh: 又召諸將帥及兵等恣其所取。

translations.literal: Again summoned various generals, commanders, and soldiers—allowed them to take as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the generals, officers, and soldiers and let each man choose for himself.

sentences.zh: 因聽自首，先有奸通婦女及尼、女官等，並即配之。

translations.literal: Thereupon permitted self-report; those who before had illicit relations with women, nuns, and female officials—altogether immediately paired with them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came forward to confess prior liaisons with local women, nuns, or palace women were at once formally matched to their partners.

sentences.zh: 由是驍果等悅，咸相謂曰：「裴公之惠也。」

translations.literal: Hence the elite guards and the like were pleased; all said to one another: "This is Lord Pei's kindness."
translations.idiomatic: The elite guards were delighted and said among themselves, "This is Lord Pei's bounty."

sentences.zh: 宇文化及反。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 矩晨起將朝，至坊門，遇逆黨數人，控矩馬詣孟景所。

translations.literal: Ju early in the morning rose intending court audience; reached the ward gate; encountered rebel party of several men; seized Ju's horse and went to Meng Jing's place.
translations.idiomatic: One morning Ju was on his way to court when, at the ward gate, several rebels seized his horse and dragged him to Meng Jing's residence.

sentences.zh: 賊皆曰：「不關裴黃門。

translations.literal: Rebels all said: "Nothing to do with Vice Minister Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels all cried, "This has nothing to do with Vice Minister Pei!

sentences.zh: 」既而化及從百餘騎至，矩迎拜，化及慰諭之。

translations.literal: " Soon after Huaji followed with a hundred-odd horsemen; Ju went forward and bowed; Huaji comforted and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Yuwen Huaji arrived with more than a hundred riders. Ju came forward to pay obeisance, and Huaji reassured him.

sentences.zh: 令矩參定儀注，推秦王子浩為帝。

translations.literal: Ordered Ju to participate in fixing ceremonial regulations; elevated Qin Prince Hao as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He put Ju in charge of drafting the court ritual and installed Prince Hao of Qin as emperor.

sentences.zh: 以矩為侍內，隨化及至河北。

translations.literal: Made Ju attendant within the palace; followed Huaji and arrived at Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was appointed palace attendant and accompanied Huaji north to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 化及僭帝號，以矩為尚書右僕射，加光祿大夫，封蔡國公，為河北道宣撫大使。

translations.literal: Huaji usurped imperial title; made Ju Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, added Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Cai, made Hebei Circuit pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji declared himself emperor, he appointed Ju Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, created him Duke of Cai, and made him commissioner for pacification of the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 及宇文氏敗，為竇建德所獲。

translations.literal: When the Yuwen clan was defeated, was captured by Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuwen faction fell, Ju was taken captive by Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 以矩隋代舊臣，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Because Ju was an old minister of the Sui dynasty, treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Dou treated Ju with great favor, regarding him as a veteran minister of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 復以為吏部尚書，轉尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Again made him Minister of Personnel; transferred to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He again made Ju Minister of Personnel, then transferred him to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
