sentences.zh: 建德起自群盜，未有節文，矩為之制定朝儀，旬月之間，憲章頗擬于王者。

translations.literal: Jiande had risen from bandit hordes, had no ritual and regulations; Ju for him established court ceremony; within ten days and a month, statutes and ordinances largely approximated those of a true king.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande had risen from the bandit ranks and knew no court protocol; Ju drew up a full ritual code for him, and within a month his regime bore the outward form of kingship.

sentences.zh: 建德大悅。

translations.literal: Jiande greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande was delighted.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗時，矩與其將曹旦等於洛州留守。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, Ju together with his general Cao Dan and others garrisoned Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande was defeated, Ju remained at Luozhou with the general Cao Dan and others.

sentences.zh: 旦長史李公淹及大唐使人魏徵等說旦及齊善行，令矩歸順。

translations.literal: Dan's chief administrator Li Gongyan and Great Tang envoy Wei Zheng and others persuaded Dan and Qi Shanxing to let Ju submit in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Dan's chief administrator Li Gongyan, together with the Tang envoy Wei Zheng, persuaded Dan and Qi Shanxing to bring Ju over to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 旦等從之，乃令矩與徵、公淹領旦及八璽，舉山東之地歸降。

translations.literal: Dan and others followed; thereupon ordered Ju together with Zheng, Gongyan to lead Dan and the eight seals; raised the lands east of the mountains to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dan agreed, and Ju, Wei Zheng, and Li Gongyan were sent with Dan and the eight imperial seals to bring all the territory east of the mountains over to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 授左庶子，轉詹事、戶部尚書，卒。

translations.literal: Granted Left Companion to the Heir Apparent; transferred to Grand Steward, Minister of Revenue; died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Companion to the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Grand Steward and Minister of Revenue, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 讓之第六弟謁之，字士敬。

translations.literal: Rangzhi's sixth younger brother Yezhi, courtesy name Shijing.
translations.idiomatic: Rangzhi's sixth younger brother, Yezhi, courtesy name Shijing.

sentences.zh: 少有志節，好直言。

translations.literal: In youth had ambition and integrity; loved blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was high-minded and unafraid to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 文宣末年昏縱，朝臣罕有言者。

translations.literal: Wenxuan's late years were dissolute and unrestrained; court ministers rarely had speakers.
translations.idiomatic: In his late years Emperor Wenxuan grew dissolute and wild, and few at court dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 謁之上書正諫，言甚切直。

translations.literal: Yezhi submitted memorial with straight remonstrance; words very cutting and blunt.
translations.idiomatic: Yezhi memorialized the throne with blunt remonstrance, his language sharp and unsparing.

sentences.zh: 文宣將殺之，白刃臨頸，謁之辭色不變。

translations.literal: Wenxuan about to kill him; naked blade at the neck; Yezhi's words and expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was about to execute him and set a blade to his throat, but Yezhi's voice and bearing never faltered.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「癡漢何敢如此！

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Fool—how dare you like this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cried, "You fool—how dare you go this far!

sentences.zh: 」楊愔曰：「望陛下放以取後世名。

translations.literal: " Yang Yin said: "Hope Your Majesty release him to obtain a name in later ages.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Yin said, "I pray Your Majesty spare him, and so win a noble name for yourself in posterity.

sentences.zh: 」帝投刀歎曰：「小子望我殺爾以取後世名，我終不成爾名。

translations.literal: " Emperor cast aside blade and sighed saying: "Little brat—you hope I kill you to obtain a name in later ages; I will finally not complete your name.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor threw down his blade and sighed, "You whelp—you want me to kill you so you can win a name in history? I won't give you that satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 」遣人送出。

translations.literal: " Dispatched someone to escort him out.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent men to escort Yezhi out.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，卒于壺關令。

translations.literal: Qi perished; died as magistrate of Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell, he was serving as magistrate of Huguan, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 皇甫和者，字長諧，安定朝那人。

translations.literal: Huangfu He—courtesy name Changxie; a man of Chaona in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu He, courtesy name Changxie, was a native of Chaona in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先因官，寓居漢中。

translations.literal: His forebears because of office sojourned and dwelt in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had settled in Hanzhong while serving in office there.

sentences.zh: 祖澄，南齊秦、梁二州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandfather Cheng—Southern Qi governor of Qin and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng served as governor of Qin and Liang provinces under Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父征，字子玄，梁安定、略陽二郡守。

translations.literal: Father Zheng, courtesy name Zixuan—Liang prefect of Anding and Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng, courtesy name Zixuan, was prefect of Anding and Lueyang under Liang.

sentences.zh: 魏正始二年，隨其妻父夏侯道遷入魏。

translations.literal: Wei Zhengshi second year—followed his wife's father Xiahou Daqian into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengshi (505), he followed his father-in-law Xiahou Daqian in defecting to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 道遷別上勳書，欲以徽為元謀。

translations.literal: Daqian separately submitted merit memorial; wished to make Hui the primary plotter.
translations.idiomatic: Daqian submitted a separate account of the merit owed, intending to name Zheng as the chief instigator of the plot.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「創謀之始，本不關預，雖貪榮賞，內愧於心。

translations.literal: Hui said: "At the beginning of plotting the scheme, originally not involved beforehand; though greedy for glory and reward, inwardly ashamed in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "I had no part in the original plan. Though I might covet the honors, my conscience would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 」遂拒而不許。

translations.literal: " Thereupon refused and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史羊靈祐重其敦實，表為征虜府司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Liang Province inspector Yang Lingyou valued his honest solidity; memorialized him as General Who Punishes Barbarians headquarters marshal; died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lingyou, governor of Liang province, admired his steadfast honesty and recommended him as marshal on the staff of the General Who Punishes Barbarians; he died in that service.

sentences.zh: 和十一而孤。

translations.literal: He at eleven then orphaned.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at eleven.

sentences.zh: 母夏侯氏才明有禮則，親授以經書。

translations.literal: Mother Lady Xiahou—talented and bright, had ritual norms; personally instructed him in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, a Lady Xiahou, was accomplished and versed in propriety, and taught him the classics herself.

sentences.zh: 及長，深沈有雅量，尤明禮義，宗親吉凶，多相諮訪。

translations.literal: When grown—deep and reserved, had refined capacity; especially clear in ritual and righteousness; clan relatives in joy and sorrow—many mutually consulted and inquired.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was sober, broad-minded, and deeply versed in ritual; kinsmen often turned to him in matters of ceremony and mourning.

sentences.zh: 卒于濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Died as Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Administrator of Jiyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 子聿道，以幹局知名，位廣平令。

translations.literal: Son Lüdao—because of capability and efficiency became known; position Magistrate of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lüdao won renown for his practical ability and served as magistrate of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，比部郎。

translations.literal: Sui Daye beginning—Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye era under Sui, he served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 和弟亮，字君翼。

translations.literal: He's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: He's younger brother, Liang, courtesy name Junyi.

sentences.zh: 九歲喪父，哀毀有若成人。

translations.literal: At nine lost father; grief and ruin like an adult's.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at nine and mourned with the grief of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 齊神武起義，為大行台郎中。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Divine Warrior raised righteous army; served as Director at the Grand Mobilization Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised his army, he served as a director on the Grand Mobilization Staff.

sentences.zh: 亮率性任真，不樂劇職，除司徒東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: Liang followed nature and was true to himself; did not enjoy heavy duties; appointed Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was plain-spoken and free by nature and disliked onerous office; he was made Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion under the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 思還鄉里，啟乞梁州褒中，即本郡也。

translations.literal: Thought of returning home village; memorial begging for Liangzhou, Baozhong—that is, his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Longing to return home, he petitioned for a post at Baozhong in Liang province, his native district.

sentences.zh: 後降梁。

translations.literal: Later surrendered to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He later defected to Liang.

sentences.zh: 以母兄在北，求還。

translations.literal: Because mother and elder brothers were in the north, requested return.
translations.idiomatic: With his mother and elder brothers still in the north, he asked to be allowed back.

sentences.zh: 梁武不奪也。

translations.literal: Liang Wu did not deprive him of this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang granted his wish.

sentences.zh: 至鄴，無復宦情，遂入白鹿山，恣泉石之賞，縱酒賦詩，超然自樂。

translations.literal: Reached Ye; no longer had desire for office; thereupon entered Mount Bailu; indulged in springs and stones' delight; unrestrained wine and composing verse; transcendent, self-pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Ye, he lost all appetite for office, retired to Mount Bailu, and gave himself over to landscape, wine, and poetry in unhurried contentment.

sentences.zh: 復為尚書殿中郎，攝儀曹事。

translations.literal: Again made Director in the Secretariat Palace; acted in charge of Ritual Office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed a director in the Secretariat and put in charge of ritual affairs.

sentences.zh: 以參撰禪代儀注，封榆中男。

translations.literal: Because participated in compiling abdication and succession ceremonial regulations; enfeoffed as Baron of Yuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: For helping draft the ceremony of dynastic transfer, he was created Baron of Yuzhong.

sentences.zh: 亮疏慢自任，無干務才，每有禮儀大事，常令余司攝焉。

translations.literal: Liang was careless and self-indulgent; had no talent for practical affairs; whenever there were great ritual matters, often ordered another office to act in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was lax and self-willed and had little gift for administration; when major ritual business arose, others were routinely left to handle it for him.

sentences.zh: 性質樸純厚，終無片言矯飾。

translations.literal: Nature simple, plain, pure, and thick; to the end not a word of affected ornament.
translations.idiomatic: His character was unvarnished and honest; he never trimmed a word for effect.

sentences.zh: 屬有敕下司，各列勤惰。

translations.literal: There happened to be an edict sent down to offices—each to list diligence and idleness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came down ordering every department to report who had been diligent and who idle.

sentences.zh: 亮三日不上省，文宣親詰其故。

translations.literal: Liang three days did not go up to the ministry; Wenxuan personally questioned the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had absented himself from office for three days, and Wenxuan questioned him in person.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「一日雨，一日醉，一日病酒。

translations.literal: Liang said: "One day rain; one day drunk; one day sick from wine.
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied, "One day it rained, one day I was drunk, and one day I was ill from wine.

sentences.zh: 」文宣以其恕實，優容之，杖脛三十而已。

translations.literal: " Wenxuan because of his honest simplicity, showed generous forbearance; caned shins thirty only.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenxuan, taking his plain honesty for sincerity, let the matter pass with thirty strokes on the shins.

sentences.zh: 所居宅洿下，標榜賣之。

translations.literal: His dwelling house low and damp; posted a placard selling it.
translations.idiomatic: His house stood in a low, marshy spot, and he put up a sign offering it for sale.

sentences.zh: 將買者或問其故，亮每答云：「為宅中水淹不洩，雨即流入床下。

translations.literal: Would-be buyers sometimes asked the reason; Liang each time answered saying: "Because in the house water floods and does not drain; when it rains it flows in under the bed.
translations.idiomatic: When prospective buyers asked why, he always answered, "The house floods and the water won't drain—when it rains, it comes in under the bed.

sentences.zh: 」由此宅終不售。

translations.literal: " From this the house finally was not sold.
translations.idiomatic: " The house, not surprisingly, never sold.

sentences.zh: 其淳實如此。

translations.literal: His honest simplicity was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his guileless honesty.

sentences.zh: 以兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主，以不稱免官。

translations.literal: As concurrent Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; chief host for Chen envoy—because of not suiting, dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: While serving concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, he headed the reception for a Chen envoy; judged unsatisfactory, he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 後除任城太守，病不之官，卒於鄴。

translations.literal: Later appointed Administrator of Rencheng; illness—did not go to office; died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Administrator of Rencheng, but illness kept him from taking up the post, and he died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General of Flying Cavalry and Governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of Flying Cavalry and Governor of An province.

sentences.zh: 裴果，字戎昭，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Guo, courtesy name Rongzhao—a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guo, courtesy name Rongzhao, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖思賢，魏青州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandfather Sixian—Wei Governor of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sixian was Governor of Qing province under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父遵，齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Zun—Governor of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun served as Governor of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 果少慷慨有志略。

translations.literal: Guo in youth was bold and generous, had ambition and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bold and far-seeing.

sentences.zh: 魏太昌中，為陽平郡丞。

translations.literal: Wei Taichang period—was Assistant Administrator of Yangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang era of Northern Wei, he served as assistant administrator of Yangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 周文帝曾使并州，與果遇。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Wen once dispatched to Bing province; encountered Guo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was sent on a mission to Bing province, he met Guo.

sentences.zh: 果知非常人，密托附焉。

translations.literal: Guo knew him not an ordinary man; secretly entrusted himself and attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo recognized that he was no ordinary man and quietly pledged himself to his cause.

sentences.zh: 永安末，盜賊蜂起，果從軍征討。

translations.literal: Yongan end—bandits and robbers swarmed up; Guo followed the army in punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongan era, when banditry erupted everywhere, Guo took the field with the army.

sentences.zh: 乘黃驄馬，衣青袍，每先登陷陣，時人號為「黃驄年少。

translations.literal: Rode yellow piebald horse; wore green robe; each time first climbed and broke into the ranks; people of the time called him "Young Yellow Piebald.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted on a dappled yellow horse and dressed in a green robe, he always led the charge into the enemy lines; men called him the Young Yellow Piebald.

sentences.zh: 」永熙中，授河北郡守。

translations.literal: " Yongxi period—granted Prefect of Hebei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Yongxi era he was appointed prefect of Hebei commandery.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武敗于沙苑，果乃率其宗党歸闕。

translations.literal: When Northern Qi Divine Warrior was defeated at Shayuan; Guo then led his clan and kin to return to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Huan's defeat at Shayuan, Guo led his clansmen to surrender to the Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 周文嘉之，賜田宅奴婢牛馬什物等。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen praised him; granted fields, houses, slaves, maidservants, oxen, horses, sundry goods, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was pleased and rewarded him with fields, houses, slaves, livestock, and household goods.

sentences.zh: 從戰河橋，解玉壁圍；

translations.literal: Followed in battle at Heqiao; relieved the siege of Yubi;
translations.idiomatic: He fought at the battle of Heqiao and broke the siege of Yubi;

sentences.zh: 摧鋒奮擊，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Crushed the vanguard and fought fiercely; wherever directed, scattered and routed.
translations.idiomatic: and wherever he struck with the vanguard, the enemy lines gave way.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，又從戰芒山。

translations.literal: Great Universal ninth year—again followed in battle at Mangshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Datong (543) he fought again at Mangshan.

sentences.zh: 于周文前挺身陷陣，禽東魏都督賀婁焉邏蘭。

translations.literal: Before Zhou Wen personally threw himself forward and broke into ranks; captured Eastern Wei Commander-in-Chief Helou Yanluolan.
translations.idiomatic: Before Emperor Wen's eyes he plunged into the enemy ranks and took captive the Eastern Wei commander Helou Yanluolan.

sentences.zh: 勇冠當時，眾人莫不嘆服。

translations.literal: Courage crowned the age; everyone none not sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: His valor stood foremost among his peers, and all marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 以此周文愈親待之。

translations.literal: Because of this Zhou Wen all the more treated him with personal intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: After this Emperor Wen held him in still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 補帳內都督，遷帥都督、平東將軍。

translations.literal: Supplemented as Colonel Within the Tent; promoted to Colonel Commander, General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Colonel Within the Tent, then promoted to Colonel Commander and General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 後從開府楊忠平隨、安陸，以功加大都督，除正平郡守。

translations.literal: Later followed Opening Grandee Yang Zhong in pacifying Sui and Anlu; for merit added Grand Colonel; appointed Prefect of Zhengping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the Duke Yang Zhong in the conquest of Sui and Anlu, and for his merits was promoted to Grand Colonel and made prefect of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 正平，果本郡也，以威猛為政，百姓畏之，資賊亦為之屏息。

translations.literal: Zhengping—Guo's native commandery; with fierce authority as policy; common people feared him; violent robbers also because of this held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengping was his home commandery; he governed with stern force, and both the people and the brigands were cowed into silence.

sentences.zh: 遷司農卿。

translations.literal: Transferred to Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 又從大將軍尉遲迥伐蜀，果率所部為前軍。

translations.literal: Again followed Great General Yuchi Jiong in campaign against Shu; Guo led his command as vanguard army.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the Great General Yuchi Jiong in the campaign against Shu, leading his troops as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 開劍閣，破季慶堡，降楊乾運，皆有功。

translations.literal: Opened Jian Pass; broke Ji Qing fortress; caused Yang Ganyun to surrender—all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jian Pass, stormed Ji Qing's fortress, and helped force the surrender of Yang Ganyun—all signal exploits.

sentences.zh: 廢帝三年，授龍州刺史，封冠軍縣侯。

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor third year—granted Governor of Long province; enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun county.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Deposed Emperor era, he was made Governor of Long province and created Marquis of Guanjun.

sentences.zh: 俄而州人張遁、李拓驅率百姓，圍逼州城；

translations.literal: Soon after—provincials Zhang Dun, Li Tuo drove and led common people; surrounded and pressed the provincial capital;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Dun and Li Tuo of the province stirred up the people and laid siege to the prefectural seat;

sentences.zh: 時糧仗皆闕，兵士又寡。

translations.literal: At the time grain and weapons all lacked; soldiers also few.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions and arms were scarce and his garrison was small.

sentences.zh: 果設方略以拒之，賊便退走。

translations.literal: Guo devised stratagem to resist them; bandits then withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo laid plans to hold them off, and the rebels soon broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是出兵追擊，累戰破之；

translations.literal: Thereupon sent troops in pursuit and attack; repeatedly battled and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: He then took the field in pursuit, winning a series of victories;

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，州境清晏。

translations.literal: Within ten days' time—the province's territory was clear and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: and within ten days the province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 轉陵州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Ling province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Ling province.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，除隆州刺史，加持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne; removed as Governor of Long province; added Staff of Authority, General of Flying Cavalry, Opening Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes; advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Guo was appointed Governor of Long province, granted the Staff of Authority, made General of Flying Cavalry and Opening Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, and raised to the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 曆眉、復二州刺史。

translations.literal: Successively served as governors of Mei and Fu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Mei and Fu provinces.

sentences.zh: 果性嚴猛，能斷決。

translations.literal: Guo by nature was stern and fierce; capable of decisive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Guo was stern and fierce by nature and capable of firm, decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 抑挫豪右，申理屈滯，曆牧數州，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Suppressed and humbled powerful families; set forth reason for the wronged and stalled; successively governed several provinces—called competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: He humbled local magnates, redressed neglected grievances, and over several provincial governorships earned a reputation for competent administration.

sentences.zh: 卒於位。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加絳、晉、建州刺史，諡曰質。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted his former offices; added Governor of Jiang, Jin, and Jian provinces; posthumous name Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former offices plus the governorships of Jiang, Jin, and Jian provinces, with the posthumous name Zhi.

sentences.zh: 子孝仁嗣。

translations.literal: Son Xiaoren succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoren succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 孝仁幼聰敏，涉獵經史，有譽于時。

translations.literal: Xiaoren in youth was clever and keen; ranged through classics and histories; had reputation in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoren was clever from childhood, read widely in the classics and histories, and won renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 起家舍人上士，累遷長寧鎮將，扞禦齊人，甚有威邊之略。

translations.literal: Rose from office as Senior Clerk Among Palace Attendants; repeatedly promoted to Defender-General of Changning; repelled Qi men—had very much the strategy of aweing the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Senior Clerk Among the Palace Attendants, rose to Defender-General of Changning, and in repelling Qi forces showed considerable talent for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 曆建、譙、亳三州刺史。

translations.literal: Successively served as governors of Jian, Qiao, and Bo provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He held the governorships of Jian, Qiao, and Bo provinces in succession.

sentences.zh: 裴寬，字長寬，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Kuan, courtesy name Changkuan—a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kuan, courtesy name Changkuan, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖德歡，魏中書侍郎、河內郡守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Dehuan—Wei Vice Director of the Secretariat, Prefect of Henei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dehuan served under Wei as Vice Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父靜慮，銀青光祿大夫，贈汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Jinglü—Silver Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; posthumously granted Governor of Fen province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jinglü was a Silver Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and was posthumously honored as Governor of Fen province.

sentences.zh: 寬儀貌瑰偉，博涉群書，弱冠為州裏所稱。

translations.literal: Kuan's bearing and appearance were magnificent; broadly ranged through many books; at weak crown was praised by the district.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was imposing in bearing, widely read, and was praised locally before he came of age.

sentences.zh: 親歿，撫諸弟以篤友聞，滎陽鄭孝穆嘗謂其從弟文直曰：「裴長寬兄弟，天倫篤睦，人之師表，吾愛之重之，汝可與之遊處。

translations.literal: Parents died; raised the younger brothers—known for devoted friendship; Xingyang Zheng Xiaomu once told his younger cousin Wenzhi: "Pei Changkuan's brothers—heavenly kinship deep and harmonious, men's model and standard; I love and value them; you may keep company with them.
translations.idiomatic: After their parents died, he raised his younger brothers and became known for devoted brotherhood. Zheng Xiaomu of Xingyang once said to his younger cousin Wenzhi, "The brothers of Pei Changkuan cherish one another as a model of family devotion—an example for all men. I love and respect them; you should seek their company.

sentences.zh: 」年十三，以選為魏孝明帝挽郎，釋褐員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: " At age thirteen, by selection made Wei Emperor Xiaoming's mournful attendant; upon leaving office appointed Supplementary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace in Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " At thirteen he was selected as a mournful attendant at Emperor Xiaoming of Wei's funeral and, upon leaving that office, was appointed Supplementary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace in Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，寬謂其諸弟曰：「君臣逆順，大義昭然。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Kuan told his younger brothers: "Ruler and minister, rebellion and obedience—the great principle is clear.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Kuan told his brothers, "The right and wrong of ruler and subject is plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 今天子西幸，理無東面以虧臣節。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven has gone west; in reason there is none to face east and impair the subject's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Son of Heaven has gone west, we cannot in reason turn east and fail in loyalty as subjects.

sentences.zh: 」乃將家屬避難于大石嶺。

translations.literal: " Thereupon led family members to take refuge at Great Stone Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon led his family to take refuge at Great Stone Ridge.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信鎮洛陽，始出見焉。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin garrisoned Luoyang; only then emerged to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin was stationed at Luoyang, Kuan finally emerged to meet him.

sentences.zh: 時汾州刺史韋子粲降於東魏，子粲兄弟在關中者咸已從坐。

translations.literal: At the time Fen Province Governor Wei Zican surrendered to Eastern Wei; Zican's brothers in Guanzhong all already suffered punishment by association.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei Zican, Governor of Fen province, had surrendered to Eastern Wei, and Zican's brothers still in the Guanzhong region had all been punished by association.

sentences.zh: 其季弟子爽先在洛，窘急乃投寬，寬開懷納之。

translations.literal: His youngest nephew's son Shuang was first in Luoyang; in desperate straits then came to Kuan; Kuan opened his heart and received him.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest nephew's son Shuang, who was already in Luoyang, came to Kuan in desperate straits, and Kuan received him with open arms.

sentences.zh: 遇有大赦，或傳子爽合免，因爾遂出，子爽卒以伏法。

translations.literal: Encountered a great amnesty; some reported Zican Shuang ought to be exempted; on that account then went out; Shuang in the end was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: When a general amnesty was proclaimed, word spread that Shuang would be spared; on that belief Kuan let him go abroad, but Shuang was eventually put to death.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信知而責之，寬曰：「窮來見歸，義無執送，今日獲罪，是所甘心。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin learned and rebuked him; Kuan said: "In distress he came seeking refuge; righteousness has none to seize and deliver; today to receive punishment—this is what the heart accepts willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin learned of this and rebuked him. Kuan said, "He came to me in distress; righteousness forbade handing him over. If I am punished today, I accept it willingly.

sentences.zh: 」以經赦宥，遂得不坐。

translations.literal: " Because it passed through amnesty and pardon, thereupon was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: " Because an amnesty had been proclaimed, he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，授都督、同軌防長史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Great Universal fifth year—granted Colonel, Chief Administrator of Tonggui Defense; added General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong (539) he was made Colonel and chief administrator of the Tonggui Defense Command, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從防主韋法保向潁川，解侯景圍。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year—followed Defense Commander Wei Fabao toward Yingchuan; relieved Hou Jing's siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (547) he followed the garrison commander Wei Fabao toward Yingchuan and broke the siege by Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 景密謀南叛，偽親狎於法保。

translations.literal: Jing secretly plotted southern rebellion; falsely feigned intimacy with Fabao.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing secretly planned to rebel southward and feigned intimacy with Fabao.

sentences.zh: 寬謂法保曰：「侯景狡猾，必不肯入關，雖托款於公，恐未可信。

translations.literal: Kuan told Fabao: "Hou Jing is cunning; surely will not consent to enter the passes; though he entrusts his sincerity to you, I fear not yet trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan said to Fabao, "Hou Jing is cunning and will never enter the passes. Though he offers you his trust, I fear he cannot be believed.

sentences.zh: 若伏兵以斬之，亦一時之功也。

translations.literal: If you set hidden troops to behead him, that too would be an achievement of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: If you lay an ambush and execute him, that would be a signal achievement in its own right.

sentences.zh: 如曰不然，便須深加嚴警，不得信其誑誘，自貽後悔。

translations.literal: If you say otherwise, then you must deeply add strict warnings; must not trust his deceit and enticement—bring regret on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you disagree, then you must be on strict guard—do not heed his flattery and deceit, or you will bring regret on yourself.

sentences.zh: 」法保納之。

translations.literal: " Fabao accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Fabao accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 然不能圖景，但自固而已。

translations.literal: Yet could not plot against Jing; only strengthened himself, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: But he could not bring himself to move against Hou Jing and contented himself with strengthening his defenses.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與東魏將彭樂、樂恂戰於新城，因傷被禽。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year—battled Eastern Wei generals Peng Le and Yue Xun at Xincheng; because wounded, was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (548) he fought the Eastern Wei generals Peng Le and Yue Xun at Xincheng, was wounded, and was captured.

sentences.zh: 至河陰，見齊文襄。

translations.literal: Reached Heyin; saw Northern Qi Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin he was brought before Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 寬舉止詳雅，善於占對，文襄甚賞異之；

translations.literal: Kuan's bearing was detailed and refined; skilled at answering; Wenxiang greatly admired and marveled at him;
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's bearing was dignified and refined and his responses apt; Wenxiang admired him greatly;

sentences.zh: 解鎖付館，厚加禮遇。

translations.literal: Removed his bonds and lodged him; generously added courtesy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: his bonds were removed and he was lodged with generous honors.

sentences.zh: 寬乃裁所臥氈，夜縋而出，因得遁還，見於周文帝。

translations.literal: Kuan then cut the felt he slept on; at night lowered himself by rope and went out; thereby escaped and returned; presented himself to Zhou Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan cut up the felt he slept on, lowered himself by rope at night, escaped back, and presented himself to Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 帝顧謂諸公曰：「被堅執銳，或有其人；

translations.literal: Emperor turned and told the assembled officials: "To don hard armor and grasp sharp weapons—perhaps there are such men;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to the assembled officials and said, "To don armor and wield sharp weapons—there may be men for that;

sentences.zh: 疾風勁草，歲寒方驗。

translations.literal: Blast-wind and stiff grass—in cold years only then tested.
translations.idiomatic: but the blast-wind and stiff grass are proved only in the bitter cold of winter.

sentences.zh: 裴長寬為高澄如此厚遇，乃能冒死歸我，雖古之竹帛所載，何以加之。

translations.literal: Pei Changkuan received such generous treatment from Gao Cheng, yet could risk death to return to us; though what the bamboo and silk of antiquity record—how could one add to it?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Changkuan, though treated with such lavish favor by Gao Cheng, risked death to return to us—what the bamboo and silk of antiquity record can scarcely surpass this.

sentences.zh: 」乃手書署寬名下，授持節、帥都督，封夏陽縣男，即除孔城城主。

translations.literal: " Thereupon in his own hand wrote and signed under Kuan's name; granted Staff of Authority, Colonel Commander; enfeoffed as Baron of Xiayang county; immediately appointed Warden of Kongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wrote the appointment in his own hand under Kuan's name, granted him the Staff of Authority and the rank of Colonel Commander, created him Baron of Xiayang, and immediately appointed him warden of Kongcheng.

sentences.zh: 寬弟漢，字仲霄。

translations.literal: Kuan's younger brother Han, courtesy name Zhongxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's younger brother Han, courtesy name Zhongxiao.

sentences.zh: 操尚弘雅，聰敏好學，嘗見人作百字詩，一覽便誦。

translations.literal: Conduct cherished lofty refinement; clever and fond of learning; once saw someone compose a hundred-character poem—one reading and at once recited.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished lofty refinement in conduct, was bright and fond of learning; once when he saw someone compose a hundred-character poem, he read it once and could recite it.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，解褐員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Xiaowu beginning—upon leaving office appointed Supplementary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace in Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign he left office and was appointed Supplementary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace in Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，除大丞相府士曹行參軍，轉墨曹。

translations.literal: Great Universal fifth year—appointed acting adjutant in the Grand Chancellor's Personnel Section; transferred to the Record Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong (539) he was made acting adjutant in the Personnel Section of the Grand Chancellor's office, then transferred to the Record Section.

sentences.zh: 漢善尺牘，尤便簿領，理識明贍，斷割如流。

translations.literal: Han was skilled at letters; especially adept at ledgers; reasoning clear and ample; decisions cut like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Han was skilled at correspondence and especially adept at ledger work; his judgment was clear and ample, and his decisions came like flowing water.

sentences.zh: 相府為之語曰「日下粲爛有裴漢。

translations.literal: The chancellor's office had a saying for him: "Under this sun there shines the brilliant Pei Han.
translations.idiomatic: They said at the chancellor's office, "Under this sun there shines the brilliant Pei Han.

sentences.zh: 」武成中，為司車路下大夫，與工部郭彥、太府高賓等參議格令。

translations.literal: " In the Wucheng era, served as Lower Grand Master of the Department of Chariots and Roads; with Works Ministry Guo Yan, Treasury Gao Bin, and others deliberated on statutes and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Wucheng era he was made Lower Grand Master of the Department of Chariots and Roads and, with Guo Yan of the Works Ministry and Gao Bin of the Treasury, deliberated on statutes and regulations.

sentences.zh: 每較量時事，必有條理。

translations.literal: Whenever weighing current affairs, invariably had order and method.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they weighed current policies, his arrangements were invariably ordered.

sentences.zh: 天和五年，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Tianhe fifth year—added Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianhe (569) he was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 漢少有宿疾，恆帶虛羸，劇職煩官，非其好也。

translations.literal: Han from youth had chronic illness; always carried frail weakness; taxing offices and heavy duties—not his preference.
translations.idiomatic: Han had suffered from chronic illness from youth and was always frail; taxing offices and heavy duties did not suit him.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護擅權，搢紳等多諂附之以圖仕進。

translations.literal: At the time Duke Jin held power alone; court gentry many fawned and attached to him to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Duke Jin Yuwen Hu held power, and many courtiers fawned upon him to advance their careers.

sentences.zh: 漢直道自守，故八年不徙職。

translations.literal: Han kept to the upright path and guarded himself; therefore eight years without transfer of office.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept to the upright path and therefore went eight years without a transfer.

sentences.zh: 性不飲酒，而雅好賓遊。

translations.literal: By nature did not drink wine, yet elegantly loved entertaining guests.
translations.idiomatic: He did not drink, yet he loved to entertain guests.

sentences.zh: 每良辰美景，必招引時彥，宴賞留連，間以篇什，當時人物，以此重之。

translations.literal: At every fine season and lovely vista, invariably summoned eminent men of the age; feasts and enjoyment lingered on; interspersed with poems; men of the time for this held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: At every fine season and lovely vista he would summon eminent contemporaries for feasts that lingered into verse; men of the age held him in esteem for this.

sentences.zh: 自寬沒後，遂斷絕遊從，不聽琴瑟；

translations.literal: From the time Kuan died, thereupon cut off all social outings; would not listen to zithers and lutes;
translations.idiomatic: After Kuan died, he cut off all social outings and would not listen to music;

sentences.zh: 歲時伏臘，哀慟而已。

translations.literal: At seasonal festivals of the year, grief and mourning—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: At the seasonal festivals he mourned in grief, and that was all.

sentences.zh: 撫養兄弟子，情甚篤至。

translations.literal: Raised his brother's sons; affection very deep and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his brother's sons with the deepest devotion.

sentences.zh: 借人異書，必躬自錄本，至於疾診彌年，亦未嘗釋卷。

translations.literal: When borrowing others' rare books, invariably copied them in person; even through years of illness, never once set aside his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: When he borrowed rare books from others he always copied them by hand himself, and even through years of illness he never set a scroll aside.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Died; posthumously granted Governor of Jin province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Governor of Jin province.

sentences.zh: 子鏡人，少聰敏，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Son Jingren—in youth clever and keen; ranged through classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingren was clever from youth and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 為大將軍、譚公會記室參軍，累遷春官府都上士。

translations.literal: Served as recorder on the staff of the Great General, Duke of Tan; repeatedly promoted to Senior Clerk in the Spring Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder on the staff of the Great General, the Duke of Tan, and rose to Senior Clerk in the Spring Office.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，位兵曹郎。

translations.literal: Served Sui; reached the post of director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he reached the post of director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 漢弟尼，字景尼，性弘雅，有器局，位禦正下大夫。

translations.literal: Han's younger brother Ni, courtesy name Jingni—nature magnanimous and refined; had breadth of character; served as Lower Grand Master of the Directorate of Corrective Measures.
translations.idiomatic: Han's younger brother Ni, courtesy name Jingni, was magnanimous and refined, possessed breadth of character, and served as Lower Grand Master of the Directorate of Corrective Measures.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈隨州刺史。

translations.literal: Died; posthumously granted Governor of Sui province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Governor of Sui province.

sentences.zh: 子之隱，趙王招府記室參軍。

translations.literal: Son Zhiyin—recorder on the staff of Prince Zhao Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiyin was recorder on the staff of Prince Zhao, Zhao.

sentences.zh: 之隱弟師人，好學有識度，見稱于時。

translations.literal: Zhiyin's younger brother Shiren—fond of learning, had discernment; praised in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyin's younger brother Shiren was fond of learning and possessed discernment; he was praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 起家秦王贄府記室參軍，仍兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Rose from office as recorder on the staff of Prince Qin Zan; concurrently served as tutor-reader.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as recorder on the staff of Prince Qin, Zan, and concurrently served as tutor-reader.

sentences.zh: 寬族弟鴻，少恭謹，有幹略。

translations.literal: Kuan's clansman younger brother Hong—in youth respectful and careful; had practical talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's clansman younger brother Hong was respectful and careful from youth and possessed practical talent.

sentences.zh: 曆官內外。

translations.literal: Successively served in offices inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served in posts inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 周天和初，拜郢州刺史，轉襄州總管府長史，賜爵高邑縣侯。

translations.literal: Zhou Tianhe beginning—appointed Governor of Ying province; transferred to chief administrator of the Xiangzhou Grand Commandant's office; granted the title Marquis of Gaoyi county.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianhe under Zhou (566) he was appointed Governor of Ying province, transferred to chief administrator of the Xiangzhou Grand Commandant's office, and created Marquis of Gaoyi county.

sentences.zh: 從衛公直南征，軍敗遂沒，尋卒于陳。

translations.literal: Followed Duke Wei Zhi on the southern campaign; army defeated and thereupon captured; soon died in Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Duke Wei Zhi on the southern campaign; the army was defeated and he was taken captive, and soon afterward died in Chen.

sentences.zh: 朝廷哀之，贈豐、資、遂三州刺史。

translations.literal: The court mourned him; posthumously granted governor of Feng, Zi, and Sui provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned him and posthumously honored him as governor of Feng, Zi, and Sui provinces.

sentences.zh: 裴俠，字嵩和，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Pei Xia, courtesy name Songhe—a man of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xia, courtesy name Songhe, was a native of Jie in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖思齊，舉秀才，拜議郎。

translations.literal: Grandfather Siqi—passed the provincial examination; appointed Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Siqi passed the provincial examination and was appointed Gentleman Consultant.

sentences.zh: 父欣，西河郡守，贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Xin—Prefect of Xihe commandery; posthumously granted Governor of Jin province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin was prefect of Xihe commandery and was posthumously honored as Governor of Jin province.

sentences.zh: 俠年七歲，猶不能言。

translations.literal: Xia at age seven still could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was seven years old and still could not speak.

sentences.zh: 後於洛城見群烏蔽天從西來，舉手指之而言。

translations.literal: Later at Luoyang saw a flock of crows covering the sky coming from the west; raised his hand, pointed at them, and spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Later in Luoyang he saw a flock of crows covering the sky coming from the west; he pointed at them and spoke.

sentences.zh: 遂志識聰慧，有異常童。

translations.literal: Thereupon his mind was bright and clever; no ordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his mind was bright and he was no ordinary child.

sentences.zh: 年十三，遭父憂，哀毀有若成人。

translations.literal: At age thirteen suffered his father's death; grief and ruin like an adult's.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he suffered his father's death and mourned with the grief of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 將擇葬地而行，空中有人曰：「童子何悲，葬于桑東，封公侯。

translations.literal: About to choose a burial ground and set out; someone in the air said: "Child, why grieve? Bury east of the mulberry grove and be enfeoffed duke or marquis.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to set out to choose a burial ground, a voice from the air said, "Child, why grieve? Bury him east of the mulberry grove and you shall be enfeoffed a duke or marquis.

sentences.zh: 」俠懼，以告其母。

translations.literal: " Xia was afraid; told his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " Xia was afraid and told his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「神也，吾聞鬼神福善，爾家未嘗有惡，當以吉祥告汝耳。

translations.literal: Mother said: "It is a spirit. I have heard that ghosts and gods reward the good; your family has never done evil—it must bring you an auspicious word.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "It is a spirit. I have heard that ghosts and gods reward the good; our family has never done evil—it must bring you an auspicious word.

sentences.zh: 」時俠宅側有大桑林，因葬焉。

translations.literal: " At the time beside Xia's house was a great mulberry grove; thereupon buried there.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time there was a great mulberry grove beside Xia's house, and there the burial was made.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk; passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: The province summoned him as chief clerk, and he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，解巾奉朝請，稍遷義陽郡守。

translations.literal: Wei Zhenguang period—took up office as Gentleman-in-Attendance; gradually promoted to Prefect of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era of Wei he took up office as Gentleman-in-Attendance and was gradually promoted to prefect of Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，使執其使人，焚其赦書。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; had Yuan's envoys arrested; burned Yuan's amnesty edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Xia had Yuan's envoys arrested and Yuan's amnesty edicts burned.

sentences.zh: 孝莊嘉之，授東郡太守，帶防城別將。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang praised him; appointed Administrator of Dong commandery; concurrently Separate Commander for city defense.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang praised him and appointed him Administrator of Dong commandery, concurrently serving as Separate Commander for the defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 及孝武與齊神武有隙，徵兵，俠率所部赴洛陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu and Northern Qi Divine Warrior had a rift, troops were mobilized; Xia led his command to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fell out with Gao Huan and troops were mobilized, Xia led his command to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍王思政謂曰：「當今權臣擅命，王室日卑，若何？

translations.literal: Martial Guard General Wang Sien said: "Today the powerful minister holds unbridled authority; the royal house daily grows low—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Sien of the Martial Guard said to him, "Today the powerful minister holds unbridled authority and the royal house grows weaker by the day—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」俠曰：「宇文泰為三軍所推，居百二之地，所謂己操戈矛，寧肯授人以柄，雖欲撫之，恐是'據於蒺藜'也」。

translations.literal: " Xia said: "Yuwen Tai is the choice of the three armies; occupies a land of strategic strength; as the saying goes, already holding spear and halberd—how would he willingly yield the hilt to another? Though you wish to win him over, I fear it would be 'standing among burr thorns.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Xia said, "Yuwen Tai is the choice of the three armies and holds a land of strategic strength. He already holds the spear in his own hand—would he willingly yield the hilt to another? Even if you wish to win him over, I fear it would be like 'standing among burr thorns.'"

sentences.zh: 思政曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: Sien said: "Then what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Sien said, "Then what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」俠曰：「圖歡有立至之憂，西巡有將來之慮。

translations.literal: " Xia said: "Gao Huan faces immediate peril; the western journey brings cares for the future.
translations.idiomatic: " Xia said, "Gao Huan faces immediate peril, and the western journey brings cares for the future.

sentences.zh: 且至關右，日慎一日，徐思其宜耳。

translations.literal: Once we reach the Guanzhong region, be more cautious with each passing day; slowly consider what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Once we reach the Guanzhong region, let us be more cautious with each passing day and slowly consider what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 」思政然之，乃進俠于帝，授左中郎將。

translations.literal: " Sien agreed; thereupon recommended Xia to the emperor; granted Left Commander of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " Sien agreed, recommended Xia to the emperor, and Xia was appointed Left Commander of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 及帝西遷，俠將行而妻子猶在東郡。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved west, Xia was about to depart though wife and children still remained in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved west, Xia was about to depart though his wife and children remained in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭偉謂俠曰：「天下方亂，未知烏之所集，何如東就妻子，徐擇木焉。

translations.literal: Xingyang Zheng Wei said to Xia: "The realm is in turmoil; no one knows where the birds will roost—why not go east to wife and children and wait to choose your perch?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wei of Xingyang said to Xia, "The realm is in turmoil and no one knows where the birds will roost—why not go east to your wife and children and wait to choose your perch?

sentences.zh: 」俠曰：「既食人祿，甯以妻子易圖也？

translations.literal: " Xia said: "Having eaten another's salary, how could I trade my purpose for wife and children?
translations.idiomatic: " Xia said, "Having eaten another's salary, how could I trade my purpose for my wife and children?

sentences.zh: 」遂從入關。

translations.literal: " Thereupon followed and entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon followed the emperor through the passes.

sentences.zh: 賜爵清河縣伯，除丞相府士曹參軍。

translations.literal: Granted title Marquis of Qinghe county; appointed Clerk in the Personnel Section of the chancellor's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title of Marquis of Qinghe county and appointed Clerk in the Personnel Section of the Chancellor's household.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，領鄉兵從戰沙苑，先鋒陷陣。

translations.literal: Datong year three—led local militia to follow battle at Shaye; vanguard broke the enemy formation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong he led local militia to the battle at Shaye and as vanguard broke the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 俠本名協，至是周文帝嘉其勇決，乃曰：「仁者必勇。

translations.literal: Xia's original name was Xie; at this point Zhou Emperor Wen admired his courage and decisiveness; thereupon said: "The benevolent are necessarily brave.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's original given name was Xie. At this point Emperor Wen of Zhou admired his courage and decisiveness and said, "The benevolent are necessarily brave.

sentences.zh: 」因命名俠焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon gave him the name Xia.
translations.idiomatic: " Accordingly he gave him the name Xia.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為侯。

translations.literal: For merit advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was advanced in rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 王思政鎮玉壁，以俠為長史。

translations.literal: Wang Sien garrisoned Yubi; made Xia chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sien was stationed at Yubi, he made Xia his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 齊神武以書招思政，思政令俠草報書甚壯烈。

translations.literal: Qi Divine Warrior by letter summoned Sien; Sien had Xia draft the reply—a letter of great defiance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent a letter trying to win over Wang Sien; Sien had Xia draft the reply—a letter of remarkable defiance.

sentences.zh: 周文善之曰：「雖魯仲連無以加也。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen was pleased and said: "Even Lu Zhonglian could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was pleased and said, "Even Lu Zhonglian could not surpass this.

sentences.zh: 」除河北郡守。

translations.literal: " Appointed Prefect of Hebei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Prefect of Hebei commandery.

sentences.zh: 俠躬履儉素，愛人如子，所食唯菽麥鹽菜而已，吏人莫不懷之。

translations.literal: Xia personally practiced thrift and simplicity; loved people as children; what he ate was only beans, wheat, salt, and vegetables; officials and people none failed to hold him in affection.
translations.idiomatic: Xia personally practiced thrift and simplicity, cared for people as for his own children, ate nothing but beans, wheat, salt, and vegetables, and none of his officials and people failed to hold him in affection.

sentences.zh: 此郡舊制，有漁獵夫三十人以供郡守。

translations.literal: This commandery's old regulation: thirty fishermen and hunters to serve the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations of this commandery, thirty fishermen and hunters were assigned to serve the prefect.

sentences.zh: 俠曰：「以口腹役人，吾所不為也。

translations.literal: Xia said: "To press men into service for the mouth and belly—what I will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Xia said, "To press men into service for my palate is something I will not do.

sentences.zh: 」乃悉罷之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon abolished them all.

sentences.zh: 又有丁三十人，供郡守役，俠亦不以入私，並收庸為市官馬。

translations.literal: Also thirty corvée laborers to serve the prefect; Xia also did not use them for private ends; together collected their labor fees to purchase horses for the market office.
translations.idiomatic: There were also thirty corvée laborers assigned to serve the prefect; Xia would not use them for private ends either, but collected their labor fees to purchase horses for the market office.

sentences.zh: 歲時既積，馬遂成群。

translations.literal: Years and seasons having accumulated, horses thereupon formed a herd.
translations.idiomatic: As the years passed, the horses eventually formed a herd.

sentences.zh: 去職之日，一無所取。

translations.literal: On the day he left office, took nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left office he took nothing with him.

sentences.zh: 人歌曰：「肥鮮不食，丁庸不取；

translations.literal: People sang: "Rich fare he would not eat; corvée labor he would not take;
translations.idiomatic: People sang, "Rich fare he would not eat, corvée labor he would not take;

sentences.zh: 裴公貞惠，為世規矩。

translations.literal: Lord Pei, upright and gracious—a model for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Pei, upright and gracious, a model for the age.

sentences.zh: 」俠嘗與諸牧守俱謁周文，周文命俠別立，謂諸牧守曰：「裴俠清慎奉公，為天下之最。

translations.literal: " Xia once with the various provincial governors together paid court to Zhou Wen; Zhou Wen ordered Xia to stand apart; said to the governors: "Pei Xia is pure, careful, and dutiful to the public weal—the finest under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Once when Xia was paying a joint call on Emperor Wen with the various provincial governors, the emperor had Xia stand apart and said to the governors, "Pei Xia is pure, careful, and dutiful to the public weal—the finest in the realm.

sentences.zh: 」令眾中有如俠者，可與之俱立。

translations.literal: " Ordered that among the company anyone like Xia might stand together with him.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered that anyone among the company comparable to Xia might stand together with him.

sentences.zh: 眾皆默然，無敢應者。

translations.literal: The company all fell silent; none dared respond.
translations.idiomatic: All remained silent; none dared respond.

sentences.zh: 周文乃厚賜俠，朝野服焉，號為「獨立使君」。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen thereupon richly rewarded Xia; court and countryside admired him; called "the Unmatched Governor."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen then richly rewarded Xia; court and countryside alike admired him, and he was called "the Unmatched Governor."

sentences.zh: 又撰九世伯祖《貞侯潛傳》，述裴氏清公，欲使後生奉而行之。

translations.literal: Also compiled a biography of his ninth-generation grand-uncle, Marquis of Integrity Qian, recounting the Pei family's upright public service; wished the younger generation to uphold and follow it.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a biography of his ancestor nine generations back, Marquis of Integrity Qian, recounting the Pei family's tradition of upright public service, wishing the younger generation to uphold and follow it.

sentences.zh: 宗室中知名者，咸付一通。

translations.literal: Notable men among the clan kindred—all received one copy each.
translations.idiomatic: All the notable men among the clan kindred received a copy each.

sentences.zh: 從弟伯鳳、世彥時並為丞相府佐，笑曰：「人生仕進，須身名並裕，清苦若此，竟欲何為？

translations.literal: Younger cousins Bofeng and Shiyan, then both aides in the chancellor's household, laughed and said: "In life's official advancement one must have body and name both ample; living in such austere poverty—what do you hope to accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousins Bofeng and Shiyan, who were then both aides in the Chancellor's household, laughed and said, "In pursuing an official career one must have both body and name well provided for—living in such austere poverty, what do you hope to accomplish?

sentences.zh: 」俠曰：「夫清者蒞職之本，儉者持身之基。

translations.literal: " Xia said: "Integrity is the root of holding office; frugality is the foundation of maintaining oneself.
translations.idiomatic: " Xia said, "Integrity is the root of holding office; frugality is the foundation of maintaining oneself.

sentences.zh: 況我大宗，世濟其美，故能存見稱於朝廷，沒流芳於典策。

translations.literal: Moreover our great house generation after generation carries on its excellence; therefore while living is praised at court, after death leaves a fragrant name in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, our great house has generation after generation carried on this excellence, and so its members have won praise at court while living and left a fragrant name in the historical records after death.

sentences.zh: 今吾幸以凡庸，濫蒙殊遇，固其窮困，非慕名也。

translations.literal: Now I happen by mediocrity to have undeservedly received extraordinary favor; my poverty is by nature—not for the sake of renown.
translations.idiomatic: Now I happen by my mediocrity to have undeservedly received extraordinary favor; my poverty is by nature, not for the sake of renown.

sentences.zh: 志在自修，懼辱先也，翻被嗤笑，知復何言！

translations.literal: My aim is self-cultivation; I fear disgracing my ancestors—yet instead am mocked; what more can I say!
translations.idiomatic: My aim is to cultivate myself, fearing to disgrace my ancestors—yet instead I am mocked. What more can I say!

sentences.zh: 」伯鳳等慚而退。

translations.literal: " Bofeng and the others withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: " Bofeng and the others withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 再遷郢州刺史，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Governor of Ying province; added Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Governor of Ying province, with the added title of Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 梁竟陵守孫皓、酂城守張建並以郡來附。

translations.literal: Liang's Defender of Jingling Sun Hao and Defender of Zan Zhang Jian both with their commands came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, defender of Jingling, and Zhang Jian, defender of Zan, both surrendered their commands to him.

sentences.zh: 俠見之，密謂人曰：「皓目動言肆，輕於去就者也；

translations.literal: Xia saw them; said privately to someone: "Hao's eyes shift and his speech is unrestrained—a man careless in choosing sides;
translations.idiomatic: When Xia saw them, he said privately to someone, "Hao's eyes shift and his speech is unrestrained—he is a man careless in choosing sides;

sentences.zh: 建神情審定，當無異心。

translations.literal: Jian's bearing is composed and steady; should have no disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's bearing is composed and steady; he should have no disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 」乃馳啟其狀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon sent an urgent report describing their circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon sent an urgent report describing their circumstances.

sentences.zh: 周文曰：「裴俠有鑒，深得之矣。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen said: "Pei Xia has true discernment—he has seen the matter deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "Pei Xia has true discernment—he has seen the matter deeply.

sentences.zh: 」遣大都督苻貴鎮竟陵，而酂城竟不遣監統。

translations.literal: " Dispatched Grand Commander Fu Gui to garrison Jingling; yet to Zan sent no overseer at all.
translations.idiomatic: " He dispatched Grand Commander Fu Gui to garrison Jingling, but sent no overseer to Zan.

sentences.zh: 及柳仲禮軍至，皓還以郢叛，卒如俠言。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhongli's army arrived, Hao turned back and rebelled with Ying—finally as Xia had said.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhongli's army arrived, Hao indeed turned and rebelled with Ying province—exactly as Xia had predicted.

sentences.zh: 尋轉大將軍、拓州刺史，徵拜雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to General-in-Chief and Governor of Tuo province; summoned and appointed Vice Administrator of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to General-in-Chief and Governor of Tuo province, and was summoned and appointed Vice Administrator of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐作，除司邑下大夫，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Xiaomin took the throne; appointed Clerk of Lower Rank in the Office of Local Administration; added General of Flying Cavalry and Opening Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes; advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Xia was appointed Clerk of Lower Rank in the Office of Local Administration, made General of Flying Cavalry and Opening Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, and raised in rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部中大夫。

translations.literal: Transferred to Clerk of Middle Rank in the Ministry of Population.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Clerk of Middle Rank in the Ministry of Population.

sentences.zh: 時有奸吏主守倉儲，積年隱沒至千萬者。

translations.literal: At the time there were corrupt clerks in charge of granaries; over years concealed amounts reaching into the millions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were corrupt clerks in charge of granaries who over years had concealed amounts reaching into the millions.

sentences.zh: 及俠在官，勵精發擿，數旬之內，奸盜略盡。

translations.literal: Once Xia held office, exerted himself to the utmost in investigation; within a few tens of days, the corrupt and thieving were nearly all rooted out.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xia took office he exerted himself to the utmost in investigation; within a few tens of days the corrupt and thieving were nearly all rooted out.

sentences.zh: 轉工部中大夫。

translations.literal: Transferred to Clerk of Middle Rank in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Clerk of Middle Rank in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 有大司空掌錢物典李貴乃於府中悲泣，或問其故，對曰：「所掌官物，多有費用，裴公清嚴有名，懼遭罪責，所以泣耳。

translations.literal: There was the Grand Minister of Works' controller of funds and goods, Li Gui, who wept in the ministry hall; someone asked the reason; he replied: "The official goods under my charge have been much diverted; Master Pei is famed for strict purity—I fear punishment, and so I weep.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui, controller of funds and goods in the office of the Grand Minister of Works, wept in the ministry hall. When asked why, he replied, "The official goods under my charge have been much diverted; Master Pei is famed for his strict purity—I fear punishment, and so I weep.

sentences.zh: 」俠聞之，許其自首。

translations.literal: " When Xia heard of it, permitted him to confess voluntarily.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xia heard of it, he permitted him to confess voluntarily.

sentences.zh: 貴自言隱費錢五百萬。

translations.literal: Gui himself reported concealed expenditures of five million coins.
translations.idiomatic: Gui himself reported concealed expenditures of five million coins.

sentences.zh: 俠嘗遇疾沈頓，士友憂之。

translations.literal: Xia once fell gravely ill and lay prostrate; scholar-official friends were anxious for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xia once fell gravely ill and lay prostrate; his fellow officials and friends were anxious for him.

sentences.zh: 忽聞五鼓，便即驚起，顧左右曰：「可向府耶。

translations.literal: Suddenly heard the fifth watch drum; immediately started up in alarm; turned to those beside him and said: "Can we now go to the ministry?
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he heard the fifth watch drum, immediately started up in alarm, and turning to those beside him said, "Can we now go to the ministry?

sentences.zh: 」所苦因此而瘳。

translations.literal: " His illness was thereby cured.
translations.idiomatic: " His illness was thereby cured.

sentences.zh: 晉公護聞之曰：「裴俠危篤若此而不廢憂公，因聞鼓聲，疾病遂愈，此豈非天祐其勤恪也？

translations.literal: Duke Jin Yuwen Hu heard of it and said: "Pei Xia was so critically ill and yet did not cease his concern for public duty; on hearing the drum his illness thereupon recovered—is this not Heaven's blessing upon his diligence?
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jin Yuwen Hu heard of it and said, "Pei Xia was so critically ill and yet did not cease his concern for public duty; on hearing the drum he recovered from his illness—is this not Heaven's blessing upon his diligence?

sentences.zh: 」又司空許國公宇文貴、小司空北海公申征並來侯俠疾。

translations.literal: " Also Grand Minister of Works Duke of Xuguo Yuwen Gui, Lesser Minister of Works Duke of Beihai Shen Zheng, and others all came to inquire after Xia's illness.
translations.idiomatic: " Also Grand Minister of Works Duke of Xuguo Yuwen Gui, Lesser Minister of Works Duke of Beihai Shen Zheng, and others all came to inquire after Xia's illness.

sentences.zh: 所居第屋，不免霜露。

translations.literal: The house where he lived was not proof against frost and dew.
translations.idiomatic: The house where he lived was not proof against frost and dew.

sentences.zh: 貴等還，言之於帝。

translations.literal: Gui and the others returned; reported it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui and the others returned, they reported this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝矜其貧苦，乃為起宅，並賜良田十頃，奴隸耕耒糧粟莫不備足。

translations.literal: The emperor, moved by pity for his poverty, had a residence built for him; also granted ten qing of fertile fields; slaves, farm implements, and grain—all fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved by pity for his poverty, had a residence built for him and also granted him ten qing of fertile fields; slaves, farm implements, and grain were all fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 搢紳咸以為榮。

translations.literal: The gentry all regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry regarded this as an honor.

sentences.zh: 卒于位，贈太子少師、蒲州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Died in office; posthumously granted Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Governor of Pu province; posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. Posthumously he was granted the titles of Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and Governor of Pu province, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 河北郡前功曹張回及吏人等感俠遺愛，乃作頌紀其清德焉。

translations.literal: Hebei commandery's former clerk recorder Zhang Hui and the other officials and clerks, moved by Xia's lingering kindness, composed a hymn commemorating his pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui, former clerk recorder of Hebei commandery, and the other officials and clerks, moved by Xia's lingering kindness, composed a hymn commemorating his pure virtue.

sentences.zh: 子祥，性忠謹，有理劇才。

translations.literal: Son Xiang—by nature loyal and careful; had talent for handling difficult affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang was loyal and careful by nature and had talent for handling difficult affairs.

sentences.zh: 少為城都令，清不及俠，斷決過之。

translations.literal: In youth served as magistrate of Chengdu; in purity did not equal Xia; in decisive judgment surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served as magistrate of Chengdu; he did not equal Xia in purity, but surpassed him in decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 後除長安令，為權貴所憚。

translations.literal: Later appointed magistrate of Chang'an; was feared by the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed magistrate of Chang'an and was feared by the powerful and noble.

sentences.zh: 遷司倉下大夫。

translations.literal: Transferred to Clerk of Lower Rank in the Office of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Clerk of Lower Rank in the Office of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 俠之終也，以毀卒。

translations.literal: At Xia's end, died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: At Xia's end, he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 祥弟肅。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother was Su.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's younger brother was Su.

sentences.zh: 肅字神封，貞亮有才藝。

translations.literal: Su, courtesy name Shenfeng—upright, bright, and gifted in the arts.
translations.idiomatic: Su, courtesy name Shenfeng, was upright, bright, and gifted in the arts.

sentences.zh: 少與安定梁毗同志友善。

translations.literal: In youth with Liang Pi of Anding shared the same ideals and were close friends.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was of one mind with Liang Pi of Anding and they were close friends.

sentences.zh: 天和中，舉秀才。

translations.literal: Tianhe era—passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷禦正下大夫，以行軍長史從韋孝寬征淮南。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Clerk of Lower Rank in the Office of Imperial Rectitude; as chief administrator on campaign followed Wei Xiaokuan in the expedition against Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Clerk of Lower Rank in the Office of Imperial Rectitude, and as chief administrator on campaign followed Wei Xiaokuan in the expedition against Huainan.

sentences.zh: 屬隋文帝為丞相，肅聞而歎曰：「武帝以雄才定六合，墳土未乾而一朝遷革，豈天道歟！

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui became chancellor, Su heard and sighed: "Emperor Wu by heroic talent settled the six directions; before the grave earth was dry the dynasty changed in a single morning—is this the way of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui became chancellor, Su heard of it and sighed, saying, "Emperor Wu by heroic talent settled the realm; before the grave earth was dry the dynasty changed in a single morning—is this the way of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」文帝聞之，甚不悅，由是廢於家。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Wen heard of it he was deeply displeased; for that reason was idle at home.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Wen heard of this he was deeply displeased, and Su was for that reason idle at home.

sentences.zh: 開皇五年，授膳部侍郎。

translations.literal: Kaihuang year five—appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Food.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Food.

sentences.zh: 曆朔州總管長史、貝州長史，俱有能名。

translations.literal: Successively chief administrator to the military governor of Shuozhou and chief administrator of Beizhou—both had reputations for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as chief administrator to the military governor of Shuozhou and chief administrator of Beizhou, and in each post earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，肅見皇太子勇、蜀王秀、左僕射高熲俱廢黜，遣使上書，言：「高熲天挺良才，元勳佐命，願錄其大功，忘其小過。

translations.literal: Renshou era—Su saw Crown Prince Yong, Prince of Shu Xiu, and Left Vice Director Gao Feng all deposed; sent an envoy with a memorial saying: "Gao Feng was Heaven-endowed with fine talent and as founding minister aided in establishing the dynasty—I beg that his great services be recorded and his petty faults forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era Su saw that Crown Prince Yong, Prince of Shu Xiu, and Left Vice Director Gao Feng had all been deposed. He sent an envoy with a memorial saying, "Gao Feng was Heaven-endowed with fine talent and as founding minister aided in establishing the dynasty—I beg that his great services be recorded and his petty faults forgotten.

sentences.zh: 二庶人得罪已久，寧無革心，願各封小國，觀其所為。

translations.literal: The two disfranchised princes have been guilty a long time—might they not yet reform their hearts? I beg that each be granted a small state and that their conduct be observed.
translations.idiomatic: The two disfranchised princes have been guilty a long time—might they not yet reform their hearts? I beg that each be granted a small state and that their conduct be observed.

sentences.zh: 若得遷善，漸更增益；

translations.literal: If they turn toward goodness, gradually increase their standing;
translations.idiomatic: If they turn toward goodness, their standing may gradually be increased;

sentences.zh: 如或不悛，貶削非晚。

translations.literal: If they do not amend, demotion and reduction will not come too late.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not amend, demotion and reduction will not come too late.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上謂楊素曰：「肅憂我家事如此，亦至誠也。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said to Yang Su: "Su's concern for my family's affairs is so great—it is also true sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said to Yang Su, "Su's concern for my family's affairs is so great—it is also true sincerity.

sentences.zh: 」於是征肅入朝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon summoned Su to court.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Su was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 皇太子聞之，謂左庶子張衡曰：「使勇自新，欲何為也？

translations.literal: The crown prince heard of it; said to Left Companion Zhang Heng: "Let Yong reform himself—what does he intend by that?
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince heard of it, he said to Left Companion Zhang Heng, "Let Yong reform himself—what does he intend by that?

sentences.zh: 」衡曰：「觀肅意欲令如吳太伯、漢東海王耳。

translations.literal: " Heng said: "Judging by Su's intent, he means to have him like Wu Taibo or the Prince of Donghai of Han.
translations.idiomatic: " Heng said, "Judging by Su's intent, he means to have him like Wu Taibo or the Prince of Donghai of Han.

sentences.zh: 」太子甚不悅。

translations.literal: " The crown prince was deeply displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 肅至京，見上于含章殿。

translations.literal: Su reached the capital; was received by the emperor in Hanchang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Su reached the capital he was received by the emperor in Hanchang Hall.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「貴為天子，富有四海，後宮寵倖，不過數人，自勇以下，並皆同母，非為愛憎，輕事廢立。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "Exalted as Son of Heaven, rich in the four seas, with favored consorts in the rear palace numbering no more than a few—from Yong downward all share the same mother; it was not from favor or dislike that I lightly changed the succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "Exalted as Son of Heaven, rich in the four seas, with favored consorts in the rear palace numbering no more than a few—Yong and those below him all share the same mother. It was not from favor or dislike that I lightly changed the succession.

sentences.zh: 」因言勇不可復收之意。

translations.literal: " Thereupon explained his view that Yong could not be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: " He then explained his view that Yong could not be recalled.

sentences.zh: 既已，罷遣之。

translations.literal: When this was done, dismissed and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When this was done, Su was dismissed and sent away.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上崩。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，不得調者久之，肅亦杜門不出。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne; went long without appointment; Su also closed his doors and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Su went long without appointment; he also closed his doors and did not go out.

sentences.zh: 後執政者以嶺表遐遠，希旨授肅永平郡丞，甚得夷人心。

translations.literal: Later those in power, because the Ling region was remote, appointed Su to please the emperor's wishes as Assistant Prefect of Yongping commandery; greatly won the hearts of the Yi peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Later those in power, because the Ling region was remote, appointed Su to please the emperor's wishes as Assistant Prefect of Yongping commandery, and he won the hearts of the Yi peoples.

sentences.zh: 歲餘卒，夷獠思之，為立廟于鄣江之浦。

translations.literal: After a year or more he died; the Yi and Liao peoples missed him; erected a shrine for him on the bank of the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: After a year or more he died; the Yi and Liao peoples missed him and erected a shrine for him on the bank of the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 有子尚賢。

translations.literal: Had a son Shangxian.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Shangxian.

sentences.zh: 裴文舉，字道裕，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Wenju, courtesy name Daoyu—a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wenju, courtesy name Daoyu, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖秀業，魏天水郡守，贈平州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandfather Xiuye—Wei Prefect of Tianshui commandery; posthumously granted Governor of Ping province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiuye served as Prefect of Tianshui commandery in Wei and was posthumously granted Governor of Ping province.

sentences.zh: 父邃，性方嚴，為州裏所推挹。

translations.literal: Father Sui—by nature stern and upright; was esteemed by his province and district.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui was stern and upright by nature and was esteemed by his province and district.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，東魏來寇，邃乃糾合鄉人，分據險要以自固。

translations.literal: Datong year three—Eastern Wei came to raid; Sui rallied the people of his district and seized strategic passes to hold his ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, when Eastern Wei invaded, Sui rallied the people of his district and seized strategic passes to hold his ground.
