sentences.zh: 及李弼略地東境，邃為之鄉導，多所降下。

translations.literal: When Li Bi swept the eastern frontier, Sui served as his local guide; many places surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi swept the eastern frontier, Sui served as his local guide and many places surrendered.

sentences.zh: 周文帝嘉之，特賞衣物，封澄城縣子。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Wen commended him; specially rewarded him with robes; enfeoffed as Viscount of Chengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou commended him, specially rewarded him with robes, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Chengcheng county.

sentences.zh: 卒于正平郡守，贈儀同三司、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Died while serving as Prefect of Zhengping commandery; posthumously granted Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes and Governor of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Prefect of Zhengping commandery and was posthumously granted the title of Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes and the governorship of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 文舉少忠謹，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Wenju in youth was loyal and careful; ranged widely through classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju from youth was loyal and careful and ranged widely through the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 大統十年，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: Datong year ten—first took office as Gentleman for Court Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Datong he first took office as Gentleman for Court Attendance.

sentences.zh: 時周文帝諸子年幼，盛簡賓友。

translations.literal: At the time the sons of Zhou Emperor Wen were still young; carefully selected companions for them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sons of Emperor Wen of Zhou were still young, and he carefully selected companions for them.

sentences.zh: 文舉以選與諸公子游，雅相欽敬，未嘗戲狎。

translations.literal: Wenju by selection kept company with the princes; refined mutual esteem; never treated them with levity or familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju was chosen to keep company with the princes; they held one another in refined esteem, and he never treated them with levity or familiarity.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎、中外府參軍。

translations.literal: Transferred to Compiler in the Imperial Library and Staff Officer for Inner and Outer Headquarters Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Compiler in the Imperial Library and Staff Officer for Inner and Outer Headquarters Affairs.

sentences.zh: 恭帝二年，賜姓賀蘭氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Gong year two—granted surname Helan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong he was granted the surname Helan.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，襲爵澄城縣子。

translations.literal: Zhou Emperor Xiaomin took the throne; inherited rank Viscount of Chengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Wenju inherited the title of Viscount of Chengcheng county.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲初開幕府，以文舉為司錄。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian first opened headquarters; made Wenju Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian first opened his headquarters, he appointed Wenju Registrar.

sentences.zh: 及憲出鎮劍南，復以文舉為總管府中郎。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Xian went out to garrison Jiannan; again made Wenju Middle-Rank Officer in the overall headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Xian went out to garrison Jiannan, Wenju was again made Middle-Rank Officer in the overall headquarters.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，就加使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wucheng year two—thereupon added Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wucheng he received the added ranks of Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 蜀土沃饒，商販百倍，或有勸文舉以利者，文舉答之曰：「利之為貴，莫若安身，身安則道隆。

translations.literal: Shu land fertile and rich; merchant profits tenfold; some urged Wenju toward profit; Wenju replied: "Of profit's worth, nothing surpasses securing the person; person secure then the Way is exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was fertile and rich, and merchant profits there ran tenfold higher; some urged Wenju to seek profit, and Wenju replied, "Of all things worth having, none surpasses keeping oneself secure; when the person is secure, the Way is exalted.

sentences.zh: 非貨之謂，是以不為，非惡財也。

translations.literal: That is not what wealth means; therefore I do not do it—not because I hate riches.
translations.idiomatic: That is not what wealth means—that is why I refuse, not because I hate riches.

sentences.zh: 」憲矜其貧窶，每欲資給之。

translations.literal: " Yuwen Xian pitied his poverty; always wished to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Xian pitied his poverty and always wished to supply him.

sentences.zh: 文舉恆自謙遜，辭多受少。

translations.literal: Wenju always self-effacing; declined much, accepted little.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju was always self-effacing, declining much and accepting little.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，遷絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Baoding year three—transferred to Governor of Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding he was transferred to Governor of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 邃之任正平也，以廉約自守。

translations.literal: When Sui held office at Zhengping—by integrity and frugality maintained himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui held office at Zhengping, he maintained himself through integrity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 每行春省俗，單車而已。

translations.literal: Whenever made spring rounds to inspect custom—single carriage only.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he made spring rounds to inspect local customs, he traveled with a single carriage and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 及文舉臨州，一遵其法，百姓美而化之。

translations.literal: When Wenju took the province—followed his methods entirely; the people praised and were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenju took the province, he followed his father's methods in every respect, and the people praised his conduct and were transformed by it.

sentences.zh: 總管韋孝寬特相欽重，每與談論，不覺膝前于席。

translations.literal: Overall commander Wei Xiaokuan especially esteemed him; whenever they conversed, unawares knees forward on the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Overall commander Wei Xiaokuan especially esteemed him; whenever they conversed, he unawares leaned forward on his mat.

sentences.zh: 天和初，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，尋為孝寬柱國府司馬。

translations.literal: Tianhe opening—promoted General of Flying Cavalry and Opening Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes; soon made marshal in Wei Xiaokuan's Pillar Duke headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe he was promoted to General of Flying Cavalry and Opening Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, and soon was appointed Marshal in Wei Xiaokuan's Pillar Duke headquarters.

sentences.zh: 六年，入為司憲中大夫，進爵為伯，轉軍司馬。

translations.literal: Year six—entered court as Clerk of Middle Rank in the Office of the Censorate; advanced in rank to marquis; transferred to Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he entered court as Clerk of Middle Rank in the Office of the Censorate, was raised in rank to marquis, and was transferred to Army Marshal.

sentences.zh: 裴仁基，字德本，河東人也。

translations.literal: Pei Renji, courtesy name Deben—a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Renji, courtesy name Deben, was a native of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖伯鳳，周汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandfather Bofeng—Governor of Fen province under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bofeng served as Governor of Fen province under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父定，上儀同。

translations.literal: Father Ding—Upper Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding held the rank of Upper Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 仁基少驍武，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Renji in youth fierce and martial; skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Renji from youth was fierce and martial, skilled with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以親衛從征，先登陷陣，拜儀同，賜物千段。

translations.literal: Campaign against Chen—as personal guard followed the expedition; first to ascend and break the formation; granted Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes; rewarded a thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen he followed the expedition as a personal guard, was first to ascend and break the enemy lines, was granted the rank of Grandee with Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes, and was rewarded with a thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 以本官領漢王諒府親信。

translations.literal: With existing rank led Prince of Han Yang Liang's household trusted aides.
translations.idiomatic: With his existing rank he served as a trusted aide in Prince of Han Yang Liang's household.

sentences.zh: 諒反，仁基苦諫見囚。

translations.literal: Liang rebelled; Renji argued strenuously and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rebelled, Renji argued strenuously against it and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 諒敗，超拜護軍。

translations.literal: Liang defeated—promoted out of turn to Defender of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was defeated, Renji was promoted out of turn to Defender of the Army.

sentences.zh: 後改授武賁郎將，從將軍李景討叛蠻向思多於黔安，以功進銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later reassigned Captain of the Martial Guard; followed General Li Jing to suppress rebel Man chieftain Xiang Siduo at Qian'an; for merit promoted Silver-Crown Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was reassigned as Captain of the Martial Guard, followed General Li Jing in suppressing the rebel Man chieftain Xiang Siduo at Qian'an, and for his merit was promoted to Silver-Crown Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 擊破吐谷渾，加授金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Defeated Tuyuhun; further granted Gold-Crown Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Tuyuhun and was further granted the rank of Gold-Crown Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 斬獲寇掠靺鞨，拜左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Cut down and captured Mohe raiders; appointed Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He cut down and captured Mohe raiders and was appointed Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從征高麗，進位光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Followed expedition against Goguryeo; advanced to Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the expedition against Goguryeo and was advanced to Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 李密據洛口，帝令仁基為河南道討捕大使，據武牢拒密。

translations.literal: Li Mi held Luokou; emperor ordered Renji Commissioner for Pursuit and Capture on Henan Circuit; held Hulao to resist Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi held Luokou, the emperor ordered Renji to serve as Commissioner for Pursuit and Capture on the Henan Circuit, holding Hulao to resist Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 仁基見強寇在前，士卒勞弊，所得軍資，即用分賞。

translations.literal: Renji saw formidable enemy before him; soldiers weary and worn; military supplies obtained—immediately distributed as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Renji saw a formidable enemy before him and his soldiers weary and worn; whatever military supplies he obtained he immediately distributed as rewards.

sentences.zh: 臨軍御史蕭懷靜止之，眾咸怒懷靜。

translations.literal: Army-attached censor Xiao Huaijing forbade it; all were furious with Huaijing.
translations.idiomatic: Army-attached censor Xiao Huaijing forbade this, and all the men were furious with Huaijing.

sentences.zh: 懷靜又陰持仁基長短，欲有奏劾。

translations.literal: Huaijing also secretly collected Renji's faults and shortcomings; intended to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijing also secretly collected evidence of Renji's faults and intended to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 仁基懼，殺懷靜，以其眾歸密。

translations.literal: Renji in fear killed Huaijing; with his troops submitted to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Renji, in fear, killed Huaijing and brought his troops over to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密以為河東郡公。

translations.literal: Li Mi made him Duke of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi made him Duke of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 其子行儼，驍勇善戰。

translations.literal: His son Xingyan—fierce, brave, skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingyan was fierce, brave, and skilled in battle.

sentences.zh: 密復以為絳郡公，甚相委昵。

translations.literal: Li Mi again made him Duke of Jiang commandery; greatly entrusted and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi again made him Duke of Jiang commandery and entrusted him with great intimacy.

sentences.zh: 王世充以東都食盡，悉眾詣偃師，求決戰。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong because Eastern Capital food exhausted—led entire force to Yanshi; sought decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, because the Eastern Capital's food was exhausted, led his entire force to Yanshi to seek a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 密與諸將計。

translations.literal: Li Mi with the generals deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi consulted with his generals.

sentences.zh: 仁基曰：「世充盡銳而至，洛下必虛。

translations.literal: Renji said: "Wang Shichong brings full strength—Luoyang below must be empty.
translations.idiomatic: Renji said, "Wang Shichong has brought his full strength—Luoyang below must be weak.

sentences.zh: 可分兵守其要路，令不得東；

translations.literal: Can divide forces to hold key routes; keep him from advancing east;
translations.idiomatic: We can divide our forces to hold the key routes and keep him from advancing east;

sentences.zh: 簡精兵三萬，傍河西出，以逼東都。

translations.literal: select thirty thousand elite troops; march out along the west bank of the river; press the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: select thirty thousand elite troops to march out along the west bank of the river and press the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世充卻還，我且按甲。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong turns back—we hold arms at rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong turns back, we hold our arms at rest.

sentences.zh: 世充重出，我又逼之。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong comes out again—we press him once more.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong comes out again, we press him once more.

sentences.zh: 如此，則我有餘力，彼勞奔命。

translations.literal: Thus—we keep strength in reserve; they wear themselves out rushing back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: In this way we keep our strength in reserve while they wear themselves out rushing back and forth.

sentences.zh: 兵法所謂彼出我歸，彼歸我出，數戰以疲之，多方以誤之者也。

translations.literal: What the art of war calls: when they go out we rest, when they return we go out—fight repeated battles to wear them down, use many stratagems to confound them.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the art of war calls: when they go out we rest, when they return we go out—fight repeated battles to wear them down and use many stratagems to confound them.

sentences.zh: 」密曰：「公知其一，不知其二。

translations.literal: " Li Mi said: "You know one part but not the other.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Mi said, "You know one part but not the other.

sentences.zh: 東都兵馬有三不可當：器械精一也，決計而來二也，食盡求鬥三也。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital troops have three reasons they cannot be withstood: arms refined—first; came resolved to fight—second; food exhausted and they seek battle—third.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital's troops have three reasons they cannot be withstood: their arms are refined—that is the first; they have come resolved to fight—that is the second; their food is exhausted and they seek battle—that is the third.

sentences.zh: 我按兵蓄力以觀其弊，彼求鬥不得，欲走無路。

translations.literal: We hold arms and conserve strength to watch for their weakness; they seek battle and cannot obtain it; wish to flee—no road.
translations.idiomatic: We hold our arms and conserve strength to watch for their weakness; they seek battle and cannot obtain it, and if they wish to flee there is no road.

sentences.zh: 不過十日，世充之首可懸於麾下。

translations.literal: In no more than ten days Wang Shichong's head can be hung beneath your banner.
translations.idiomatic: In no more than ten days, Wang Shichong's head can be hung beneath your banner.

sentences.zh: 」單雄信等諸將輕世充，皆請戰。

translations.literal: " Generals Shan Xiongxin and others looked down on Wang Shichong; all requested battle.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals Shan Xiongxin and the others looked down on Wang Shichong and all requested battle.

sentences.zh: 仁基苦爭不得。

translations.literal: Renji argued strenuously but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Renji argued strenuously but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 密難違諸將言，戰遂大敗。

translations.literal: Li Mi found it hard to go against the generals' words; battle thereupon ended in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi found it hard to go against what the generals said, and the battle ended in a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 仁基為世充所虜。

translations.literal: Renji was captured by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Renji was captured by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 世充以仁基父子並驍勇，深禮之，以兄女妻行儼。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong because Renji and his son were both fierce and brave—treated them with deep courtesy; gave elder brother's daughter in marriage to Xingyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, because Renji and his son were both fierce and brave, treated them with deep courtesy and gave his elder brother's daughter in marriage to Xingyan.

sentences.zh: 及僭尊號，署仁基為禮部尚書，行儼為左輔大將軍。

translations.literal: When he usurped the imperial title—appointed Renji Minister of Rites; Xingyan Grand General of the Left Companion.
translations.idiomatic: When he usurped the imperial title, he appointed Renji Minister of Rites and Xingyan Grand General of the Left Companion.

sentences.zh: 行儼每戰，所當皆披靡，號萬人敵。

translations.literal: Whenever Xingyan fought, none who faced him failed to scatter; called a match for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xingyan fought, none who faced him failed to scatter; he was called a match for ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 世充憚其威名，頗加猜防。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong feared their formidable reputation; added considerable suspicion and precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong feared their formidable reputation and added considerable suspicion and precaution.

sentences.zh: 仁基知之，甚不自安，遂與世充所署尚書左丞宇文儒童、尚食直長陳謙、秘書丞崔德本等謀。

translations.literal: Renji knowing this was deeply uneasy; thereupon plotted with Yuwen Rutong, Left Assistant in the Ministry of Rites under Wang Shichong's regime, Chen Qian Direct Attendant of the Office of Imperial Food, Cui Deben Secretary of the Secretariat, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Renji, knowing this, was deeply uneasy, and thereupon plotted with Yuwen Rutong, Left Assistant in the Ministry of Rites under Wang Shichong's regime, Chen Qian, Direct Attendant of the Office of Imperial Food, Cui Deben, Secretary of the Secretariat, and others.

sentences.zh: 令陳謙於上食之際，持匕首劫世充，行儼以兵應之。

translations.literal: Ordered Chen Qian at the moment of the emperor's meal to seize Wang Shichong at dagger-point; Xingyan would respond with troops.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered Chen Qian, at the moment of the emperor's meal, to seize Wang Shichong at dagger-point, while Xingyan would respond with troops.

sentences.zh: 事定，然後輔越王侗。

translations.literal: Once the affair was settled—then assist Prince of Yue Yang Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Once the affair was settled, they would then assist Prince of Yue Yang Tong.

sentences.zh: 事臨發，將軍張童兒告之，俱為世充所殺。

translations.literal: As the plot was about to be launched General Zhang Tong'er reported it; all were killed by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: As the plot was about to be launched, General Zhang Tong'er reported it, and they were all killed by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 論曰：裴駿雅業有資，器行仍世，所以布於列位，不替其美。

translations.literal: Commentary: Pei Jun refined learning had endowment; talent conduct persisted generation after generation; therefore filled ranks of office without losing excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Pei Jun had refined learning and solid endowment; talent and conduct persisted generation after generation—hence they filled the ranks of office without losing their excellence.

sentences.zh: 延俊器能位望，有可稱乎。

translations.literal: Yanjun's capacity and standing—worthy of praise, are they not?
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun's capacity and standing deserve praise, do they not?

sentences.zh: 伯茂才名，亦時之良也。

translations.literal: Bomao's talent and reputation—also a worthy man of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Bomao's talent and reputation likewise made him a worthy man of his age.

sentences.zh: 元化以文學傳業，而又修史著美。

translations.literal: Yuanhua by literary learning passed down his calling; moreover through historiography won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhua passed down his literary calling and further won renown through historiography.

sentences.zh: 讓之弟兄，修身厲行，觀夫出處之跡，良足稱乎。

translations.literal: Rangzhi's brothers cultivated themselves and toughened conduct; judged by the record of entering and leaving office—indeed worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Rangzhi cultivated themselves and toughened their conduct—judged by the record of how they entered and left office, they are indeed worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 矩學涉經史，頗有幹局。

translations.literal: Ju's learning ranged through classics and histories; had considerable practical capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's learning ranged through the classics and histories, and he possessed considerable practical capacity.

sentences.zh: 至於恪勤匪懈，夙夜在公，求之古人，殆未之有。

translations.literal: As for tireless diligence and constant devotion to public duty—search among the ancients and scarcely find his equal.
translations.idiomatic: As for his tireless diligence and constant devotion to public duty—search among the ancients and you would scarcely find his equal.

sentences.zh: 與聞政事，多曆歲年，雖處危亂之中，未虧廉謹之節。

translations.literal: Took part in government over many years; though amid turmoil never lost integrity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in government over many years; though he lived amid turmoil, he never lost his integrity and prudence.

sentences.zh: 然與時消息，承望風旨，使高昌入朝，伊吾獻地；

translations.literal: Yet read the times and deferred to prevailing intent—brought Gaochang to court, won submission of Yiwu's territory;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he read the times and deferred to prevailing intent, bringing Gaochang to court and winning the submission of Yiwu's territory;

sentences.zh: 聚糧且末，師出玉門，關右騷然，頗亦矩之由矣。

translations.literal: stockpiled grain at Qiemo; armies out through Yumen Pass; lands west of the Pass in turmoil—owed much to Ju as well.
translations.idiomatic: stockpiling grain at Qiemo and sending armies out through Yumen Pass—the disturbances in the lands west of the Pass owed much to Ju as well.

sentences.zh: 果及長寬，早知去就。

translations.literal: Guo and Changkuan understood early when to stay and when to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Guo and Changkuan understood early when to stay and when to leave.

sentences.zh: 而寬淪跡異域，蓋乃命乎。

translations.literal: Yet Kuan ended his days in a foreign land—perhaps that was fate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kuan ended his days in a foreign land—perhaps that was fate.

sentences.zh: 嵩和廉約居身，忠勤奉上，人懷其惠，吏畏其威，雖古之良吏，何以加此。

translations.literal: Songhe lived simply and frugally; served loyally and diligently—the people cherished his kindness, officials feared his authority; even good magistrates of old could scarcely surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Songhe lived simply and frugally, served loyally and diligently—the people cherished his kindness, officials feared his authority; even the good magistrates of old could scarcely surpass this.

sentences.zh: 肅曆官周、隋，志存鯁正。

translations.literal: Su served through Zhou and Sui; his aim pure and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Su served through Zhou and Sui, his aim pure and upright.

sentences.zh: 竟而忠誠慷慨，犯忤龍鱗，固知嫠婦憂宗周之亡，處女悲太子之少，非徒語也。

translations.literal: In the end loyal fervor led him to offend the dragon's scales—one truly knows the widow mourning Zhou's fall, the maiden grieving the crown prince's youth; no mere figures of speech.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his loyal fervor led him to offend the dragon's scales—one truly knows the widow mourning Zhou's fall, the maiden grieving the crown prince's youth; these were no mere figures of speech.

sentences.zh: 文舉之在絳州，世載清德，辭多受少，有廉讓之風焉。

translations.literal: Wenju's tenure in Jiang province continued a hereditary tradition of pure virtue; declined much, accepted little—had a reputation for integrity and modesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju's tenure in Jiang province continued a hereditary tradition of pure virtue; declining much and accepting little, he had a reputation for integrity and modesty.

sentences.zh: 仁基以武略見知，自升顯級，竟而蹈履非所，身名隳壞，時也。

translations.literal: Renji was recognized for martial strategy and rose to eminent rank; yet in the end walked paths ill suited to him and destroyed body and name—such was the time.
translations.idiomatic: Renji was recognized for martial strategy and rose to eminent rank, yet in the end walked paths ill suited to him and destroyed both body and name—such was the time.
